sources.note: The actual EXECUTED research output of the kernel-reduction/minimality experiment mandated by this batch's own prompt document (kernel-reduction-ablation-experiment-protocol), explicitly labelled [EXP] research, not architecture/governance/canon, with an authorization boundary stating this lane cannot canonize a kernel. Tests the candidate 13-operator set C0={Observe,Interpret,Represent,Relate,Discriminate,Hypothesize,Infer,DetectGap,Challenge,Validate,Revise,Determine,Select} plus Qualify (held outside C0). Builds a formal, mechanically-checked anti-circularity apparatus: an operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms (14 atoms: world-contact, meaning-assignment, symbolic-encoding, relational-linking, difference-decision, content-generation, entailment, norm-comparison, adversarial-negation, warrant-assessment, state-mutation, closure-judgment, preference-over-actions, evidential-qualification), so 'redefine Y to secretly also do X' becomes a mechanically detectable change to Y's atom set (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a valid composition; atoms are deliberately allowed to be SHARED (two atoms are shared: difference-decision between Discriminate/DetectGap, and norm-comparison between DetectGap/Determine) since a 1:1 operator-to-atom mapping would make the experiment vacuous by construction. Defines a typed carrier-derivation table (ambient carriers: World/Context/Inquiry/IdealState/Policy/Rule/Objective/ActionSet/EpistemicState(K_t) -- none produced by any operator; derived carriers: Observation/SemanticContent/Representation/Evidence/Relation/Discrimination/Hypothesis/Claim/Defeater/Verdict/NormDelta/Gap/Determination/Decision) where a carrier kind is derived from (input-kind multiset, atoms introduced) rather than stamped by whichever operator produced it, formalizing Reach(S) as a monotone, terminating least fixpoint over ambient carriers -- deliberately excluding any hand-added 'obvious' closures or helper functions that could smuggle in a removed operator's work. Produces a 25-capability model (the protocol's C1-C24 plus a NEWLY ADDED C25 'admit an observation as evidence under a policy', justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) means C10's Verdict-requires-Evidence type rule is otherwise unrealizable -- an addition that makes minimization HARDER, not easier, so cannot be a convenience), with C18 (provenance) explicitly marked NON-DISCRIMINATING (structurally guaranteed by the reach engine's derivation-DAG bookkeeping, hence untestable by this instrument -- an explicit limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel) and C20 (non-identifiability) operationalized with an explicit overreach failure mode (holding >=2 hypotheses plus returning UNDECIDED; failing by producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives). Computes an operator x capability matrix via actual leave-one-out removal-and-reevaluation (not asserted), yielding the experiment's headline empirical finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are BOTH ALL-ZERO ROWS under leave-one-out (neither is individually required for any capability, because each covers the other's shared atoms) -- explicitly NOT evidence the capabilities are unneeded but evidence the OPERATOR PACKAGING IS REDUNDANT; correspondingly C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero COLUMNS under leave-one-out and only become irreducible under PAIRWISE ablation (C5 lost only if {Discriminate,DetectGap} are BOTH removed, at the shared atom difference-decision; C8 lost if {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are both removed, at difference-decision+norm-comparison) -- concluding a leave-one-out matrix alone would have wrongly declared C5/C8 unnecessary, which is the concrete justification for why pairwise ablation is mandatory and cardinality is only a secondary result. Confirms via the type system that Claim is producible ONLY via entailment (making its warrant kind DEDUCTIVE by construction, so a Verdict from generate-and-test is never a Claim, keeping 'Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize' a genuine open question rather than a definitional trick), that Verdict requires Evidence (making the corpus's absent Qualify function fatal to any C0-only realization), and that Determination requires BOTH NormDelta (hence IdealState) AND Inquiry (encoding the prior constraint that Ideal State is inquiry-relative). Formally distinguishes three notions of operator necessity that can and do disagree without being a defect -- empirically necessary (scenario/simulation fails without it), formally necessary (no valid composition of the rest supplies it via Reach), and DDD-necessary (a distinct domain responsibility) -- explicitly reporting they disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Rates per-operator corpus support from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-a-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Select, Relate).

Re-registered in B0057 to satisfy this batch label-registration check; this batch (S2347-S2354, S2356, S2361-S2366, S2380-S2381) reads the direct continuation (parts VII-XXVI) of the same KR-2026-09-01 experiment whose first sections (01,03,04,05,06) B0056 already registered under this label. relation_to_existing copied unchanged from the B0056 original proposal per cross-batch identity discipline.

rows.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
rows.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

rows.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
rows.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

rows.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
rows.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

rows.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
rows.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

rows.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
rows.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

rows.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
rows.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

rows.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
rows.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

rows.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
rows.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

rows.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
rows.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

rows.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
rows.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

rows.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
rows.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

rows.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
rows.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

rows.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
rows.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

rows.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
rows.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

rows.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
rows.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

experiment.hypothesis: Leave-one-out ablation is sufficient to determine which capabilities are dispensable
experiment.setup: Operator x capability matrix computed by removing one operator at a time from C0+Qualify and re-evaluating Reach(S)
experiment.assumptions: Two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared across operators
experiment.inputs: C0 operator set, 25-capability model, 14-atom vocabulary
experiment.method: Leave-one-out ablation followed by pairwise ablation over the same model
experiment.result: C5 and C8 are all-zero columns under leave-one-out but become lost under specific pairwise removals
experiment.interpretation: Leave-one-out alone would misclassify C5 and C8 as unnecessary
experiment.limitations: Result is specific to this atom-sharing model; scheduled for attack under robustness variant V4
experiment.conclusion: Pairwise (not merely leave-one-out) ablation is mandatory for this kind of minimality claim

rows.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
rows.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

rows.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
rows.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

rows.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
rows.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

rows.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
rows.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

rows.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
rows.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

rows.anchor: A scenario passes iff every required capability is achievable *given that scenario's ambient set*
rows.statement: A scenario in the 16-scenario canonical test suite passes iff every capability it requires is achievable given only the ambient carriers that scenario itself supplies; a scenario supplying no IdealState cannot be passed by producing a Determination.

rows.anchor: S7 and S11–S12 are the only scenarios supplying `IdealState`. This encodes prior constraint 5 and makes property P6 (adequacy) testable rather than assumed.
rows.statement: Only scenarios S7 and S11-S12 supply the IdealState ambient carrier, deliberately encoding the constraint that determination/gap require an Ideal State and making adequacy (property P6) an empirically testable claim rather than an assumption.

rows.anchor: S13 is the only scenario supplying `Objective` and `ActionSet`. Action selection is therefore *structurally isolated* from epistemic determination — matching the corpus, which places the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection.
rows.statement: Because only scenario S13 supplies Objective and ActionSet, action-selection capability is structurally isolated from epistemic determination in the scenario suite, matching the corpus's placement of the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection; if Select performed epistemic work it would appear elsewhere, and it does not.

rows.anchor: S9 is the only scenario supplying `Rule`. Deductive inference is thereby not available for free.
rows.statement: Restricting the Rule ambient carrier to scenario S9 alone means deductive inference is not available by default in the other 15 scenarios, forcing the experiment to distinguish entailed (deductive) content from generated/hypothesized content.

rows.anchor: Scenarios do **not** declare which operators must be used. They declare capabilities. Any operator set that reaches them passes.
rows.statement: The scenario suite is defined purely in terms of required capabilities and ambient carriers, never in terms of which operators must be invoked, so that any operator set reaching the required capabilities counts as passing — an anti-circularity design constraint.

rows.anchor: A narrative simulator ... is precisely the instrument in which semantic smuggling is invisible ... Instead the simulator is an **algebra**: operators are atom sets, carriers are derived from (inputs, atoms), and reconstruction is a fixpoint search. Smuggling then becomes a *detectable edit to the model* rather than an invisible line of code.
rows.statement: A narrative simulator (helper functions that 'interpret'/'validate' example data) makes semantic smuggling invisible because a helper can quietly perform a removed operator's job; the kernel-reduction simulator is instead built as an algebra (operators = atom sets, carriers derived from inputs+atoms via a fixpoint search over reachability) so that smuggling becomes a detectable edit to the declared model rather than a hidden line of code.

rows.anchor: Only domain operators count toward kernel size, and there are exactly 14 of them (the `Op` entries in `kr/operators.py`).
rows.statement: Every function in the kernel-reduction codebase is classified into one of: domain operator, data structure operation, test harness, serialization/logging, or alternative-model-specification; only the 14 declared domain operators (the Op entries) count toward kernel size — no helper function is permitted to introduce a new semantic atom.

rows.anchor: K_t ≈ { claims, representations, relations, evidence, provenance, assumptions, alternatives, uncertainty, context, history } ... **This is NOT claimed to be the canonical KnowledgeOS state model.**
rows.statement: The simulator's [PROP] state representation approximates K_t as a record of ten fields (claims, representations, relations, evidence, provenance, assumptions, alternatives, uncertainty, context, history), explicitly disclaimed as not the canonical KnowledgeOS state model; in the actual simulator this record is represented by the reachable-carrier-set plus derivation DAG, with an explicit carrier-to-field mapping given.

assumptions.statement: K_t can be approximated for simulation purposes by ten named fields mapped onto derived carrier kinds.
assumptions.anchor: This is NOT claimed to be the canonical KnowledgeOS state model.

rows.anchor: Because the simulator reasons about *reachability of kinds* rather than about *instances*, it cannot express failures of degree ... It answers "can this operator set do X at all?", never "how well". Every result in this experiment must be read inside that boundary.
rows.statement: Because the simulator reasons about reachability of carrier kinds rather than instances, it cannot distinguish a poor interpretation from a rich one, or otherwise express failures of degree — it only answers whether an operator set can achieve a capability at all, never how well; every experimental result must be read within this boundary.

rows.anchor: **Disable** `o` — remove it from the set. Nothing else changes. **Do NOT rewrite** the remaining operators to absorb `o`. (Enforced structurally...) **Attempt reconstruction** — the reach fixpoint *is* an exhaustive search over all valid typed compositions of the remaining operators.
rows.statement: The ablation procedure for each operator o: disable it without rewriting remaining operators to absorb it (structurally enforced, since absorption would require changing another operator's atom set, which the reach engine cannot do mid-search); reconstruction is attempted via an exhaustive reach fixpoint over all valid typed compositions of the remaining operators, removing any 'reasonable attempts exhausted' judgment call; then run all 16 scenarios and 10 randomized properties, record the exact failed capability/failure class, and determine whether a failure is fundamental or a simulator artifact (F19/F20).

rows.anchor: `A` apparently irreducible · `B` derivable/composable · `C` redundant with another operator · `D` ambiguous semantics · `E` unsupported by current evidence · `F` unresolved. Operators are **not** forced into A/B.
rows.statement: Defines a six-value classification vocabulary (A apparently irreducible, B derivable/composable, C redundant with another operator, D ambiguous semantics, E unsupported by current evidence, F unresolved) for reporting each operator's ablation status, explicitly refusing to force a binary irreducible/derivable classification.

rows.anchor: F1 representation · F2 semantic interpretation · ... F18 governance/authorization confusion · **F19 implementation artifact** · **F20 simulator artifact**. F19/F20 are never counted as kernel failures.
rows.statement: Defines twenty named failure classes F1-F20 covering representation, semantic interpretation, relation, discrimination, hypothesis generation, inference, gap detection, challenge, validation, revision, determination, action selection, context, temporal, provenance, alternative preservation, non-identifiability, and governance/authorization confusion failures, plus F19 (implementation artifact) and F20 (simulator artifact) which are never counted as genuine kernel-necessity findings.

rows.anchor: The forbidden move — `Y := X-in-disguise` — is run **deliberately**, as a control ... Every probe is reported with `SMUGGLING = TRUE` and `verdict = REJECTED`. A probe that restores full coverage is *not* evidence of reducibility; it is evidence that the test is necessary.
rows.statement: The forbidden 'semantic smuggling' move (redefining a remaining operator Y to secretly perform a removed operator X's job) is deliberately executed as a control probe (smuggling_probe), always reported SMUGGLING=TRUE / verdict=REJECTED; a smuggling probe that restores full capability coverage is not evidence of reducibility but evidence that the smuggling test itself is a necessary safeguard against fake minimality claims.

rows.anchor: "The baseline must succeed before ablation results are interpreted." The `C0` baseline **does not succeed** (§10). The experiment therefore runs on a **repaired baseline** `C0+ = C0 ∪ {Qualify}` and reports both arms, with the raw `C0` arm retained as robustness variant **V7**
rows.statement: Applying the discipline that a baseline operator set must succeed before its ablation results can be interpreted, the raw candidate 13-operator set C0 fails to succeed (documented in §10/N-1), so the experiment adopts a repaired baseline C0+ = C0 union {Qualify} as its primary arm while retaining the original C0 as robustness variant V7 so the failure is not hidden.
dependencies: qualify (Observation x Policy -> Evidence, corpus G1 gap)

rows.anchor: Recorded in every `results/*.json` under `_meta`: experiment_id KR-2026-09-01 · model_version kr-model-1.0 · date 2026-09-01 · python 3.x · seeds [1,7,13,101,2718] · trials_per_seed 2000
rows.statement: Reproducibility metadata for the experiment is recorded in every results JSON file's _meta block (experiment_id KR-2026-09-01, model_version kr-model-1.0, date, python version, five fixed random seeds, 2000 trials per seed, the capability model version, and the operator sets tested); the reach fixpoint is deterministic and seed-independent, only randomized property worlds consume the seed, and the code is reproducible via `python3 run_all.py`.

rows.anchor: **4 pairs show synergistic loss** — a capability lost by the pair that neither member loses alone.
rows.statement: Of all 91 pairwise ablations of C0+, exactly four pairs (DetectGap+Determine, DetectGap+Discriminate, Hypothesize+Infer, Hypothesize+Represent) show synergistic capability loss: a capability lost by removing the pair together that is lost by neither operator removed alone.

experiment.hypothesis: Leave-one-out ablation alone correctly identifies all necessary operators/capability dependencies.
experiment.setup: Ablate all 91 pairs of the 14-operator C0+ set and re-run the 25-capability x 16-scenario evaluation for each pair.
experiment.assumptions: Reach fixpoint correctly models valid typed composition.
experiment.inputs: C0+ operator set, capability model C1-C25, 16 scenarios.
experiment.method: Exhaustive pairwise removal-and-reevaluation.
experiment.result: 4 of 91 pairs show synergistic loss not predicted by either single-operator ablation.
experiment.interpretation: Leave-one-out granularity is insufficient; some necessity is second-order (shared atoms or joint content-supply roles).
experiment.limitations: Simulator answers reachability only, not degree (see 09-simulation-design).
experiment.conclusion: Pairwise ablation is mandatory, not optional, for a sound minimality claim.

rows.anchor: `DetectGap` sits at the intersection of both pairs — it is the only operator that appears in two synergistic pairs, and the only one holding no exclusive atom. Structurally, `DetectGap` is the *union* of two powers already owned elsewhere.
rows.statement: DetectGap's synergistic loss in two separate pairs ({DetectGap,Determine} and {DetectGap,Discriminate}) is explained structurally: DetectGap holds no exclusive atom and is the union of two powers (difference-decision, norm-comparison) already owned by Discriminate and Determine respectively.

rows.anchor: There must be at least one operator that produces a proposition-bearing artifact, but the system does not care which one. `Hypothesize` (non-entailed content) and `Infer` (entailed content) are *substitutable as suppliers* to the critical lane while remaining *non-substitutable in warrant kind*.
rows.statement: The critical challenge/validate lane (C9, C10) requires at least one upstream operator producing a proposition-bearing artifact (Claim or Hypothesis); Hypothesize and Infer are substitutable AS SUPPLIERS to that lane (either one alone suffices to keep the lane alive) while remaining non-substitutable in the warrant kind they produce (non-entailed vs entailed content) — this is termed an 'operator bundle': jointly necessary as a role, individually deletable, answering protocol question Q8 affirmatively.

rows.anchor: `[NEG]` **No third-order interaction was found.** All observed structure is second-order — pairs sharing an atom, or pairs jointly feeding one downstream carrier. Higher-order ablation was run and returned nothing new; that is a negative result worth recording, since it bounds how complex the dependency structure of this model actually is.
rows.statement: Selected triple ablations over the clusters implicated by the pairwise results yielded exactly the union of the pairwise losses with no genuine third-order effect; the dependency structure of the C0+ model is therefore bounded at second order, a negative result recorded explicitly to bound model complexity.

rows.anchor: Without it, the leave-one-out matrix (§05) would have reported that **C5 and C8 are needed by no operator** — a false conclusion produced by a correct procedure applied at the wrong granularity.
rows.statement: Leave-one-out ablation alone would have incorrectly concluded capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are needed by no operator — a false conclusion produced by applying a correct procedure at too coarse a granularity, corrected only by pairwise ablation.

rows.anchor: `DDD-necessary` is a **third, independent** notion of necessity — it may disagree with formal and empirical necessity, and where it does, the disagreement is the result.
rows.statement: DDD-necessity (does an operator represent a genuine, distinct domain responsibility with its own invariant and I/O contract) is treated as a third, independent notion of necessity alongside formal necessity (irreducible under the reach fixpoint) and empirical necessity (required by scenario/simulation); where the three notions disagree, the disagreement itself is reported as the finding rather than resolved by fiat.

rows.anchor: Formal ablation says removable (only because `DetectGap` redundantly carries its atom). DDD says keep: *Buddhi* ... is a first-class domain responsibility ... **Resolution: retain `Discriminate`, drop `DetectGap`.** All three notions then agree.
rows.statement: Discriminate is formally derivable under leave-one-out (because DetectGap redundantly carries its atom) but is DDD-necessary as Buddhi, the first-class domain power to decide difference/contradiction/specificity/supersession/compatibility/incomparability/unknown; under variant V4 the formal result flips to irreducible, so all three notions agree once packaging is corrected: retain Discriminate, drop DetectGap as a kernel primitive (it is a derived predicate, the union of two other operators' powers, with no exclusive atom, no independent invariant, and no independent reason to change).

rows.anchor: The evidence is consistent with `Select` being a **domain capability of a neighbouring bounded context**, not of the epistemic kernel: it consumes an `Objective` the kernel does not own, and it produces a `Decision` no epistemic capability consumes. ... **Status: `UNRESOLVED`.** ... a minimality experiment is the wrong instrument to settle it.
rows.statement: Select is formally irreducible in 7 of 8 model variants (fails only V5) but fires in exactly one of 16 scenarios (S13, the only one supplying Objective and ActionSet) and has the weakest corpus support (3 role-uses) of any tested operator; the corpus places it in the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection, so the evidence is consistent with Select being a domain capability of a neighbouring bounded context rather than of the epistemic kernel — explicitly left UNRESOLVED (not deleted, not promoted) since a minimality experiment is judged the wrong instrument to settle a strategic-DDD context-boundary question.
missing: a strategic-DDD context-map analysis of whether Select belongs to the epistemic kernel or a neighbouring bounded context

rows.anchor: `state-mutation` is exclusive and its removal costs C11, C15 and C24 — formally decisive. But DDD question 7 ("domain concept or implementation mechanism?") is genuinely unclear ... the corpus carries **seven** revision verbs (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire) that are *epistemically distinct* though they share the mechanism. ... **Status: `AMBIGUOUS`**
rows.statement: Revise is formally decisive/irreducible (its exclusive state-mutation atom's removal costs capabilities C11, C15, C24) but DDD-ambiguous: it is unclear whether committing to K_t is a domain concept or an implementation mechanism, since the corpus carries seven epistemically distinct revision verbs (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire) that share one mechanism but which the current simulator cannot distinguish; status recorded AMBIGUOUS — irreducible as a power, under-modelled as a domain concept.
missing: a test of whether the seven corpus revision verbs are epistemically distinguishable, which the current simulator cannot perform

rows.anchor: **Zero** | predicate, not primitive | **CONFIRMED** `[EXP]`. `Gap` is produced by `difference-decision ∘ norm-comparison`; `DetectGap` holds no exclusive power. `Zero(K_t, I_Q, EC)` behaves as a state predicate over a normative comparison.
rows.statement: The hypothesis that Zero is a predicate rather than a primitive kernel operation is CONFIRMED experimentally: Gap is produced by composing difference-decision with norm-comparison, DetectGap holds no exclusive atom/power, and Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) behaves as a state predicate over a normative comparison rather than an irreducible operation.

rows.anchor: **Ideal State** | state/target construct, not an operator | **CONFIRMED by construction and load-bearing**: `IdealState` is ambient; no `Determination` and no `Gap` is reachable without it. ... **Inquiry** | domain input, not an operator | **CONFIRMED**: ambient; `Determination` requires `NormDelta` **and** `Inquiry**
rows.statement: IdealState is confirmed by construction to be a load-bearing ambient state/target construct rather than an operator: no Determination and no Gap is reachable without it, and scenarios lacking it correspondingly demand neither. Inquiry is similarly confirmed as an ambient domain input rather than an operator: the type rule for Determination requires both NormDelta and Inquiry, directly encoding inquiry-relative adequacy.

rows.anchor: **Governance** | external constraint | **CONFIRMED by modelling, not by test**: `Policy` and `Objective` are ambient carriers supplied to `Qualify` and `Select`. No operator produces them. `[INF]` — this was assumed in the model, so it is not independent evidence. **Authorization** | governance mechanism | **NOT TESTED.**
rows.statement: Governance's status as an external constraint is confirmed only BY MODELLING (Policy and Objective are ambient carriers no operator produces, supplied to Qualify and Select) rather than by independent empirical test, since this was assumed in the model rather than discovered by it; Authorization's hypothesized status as a governance mechanism was NOT TESTED at all — no scenario exercises it and no F18 (governance/authorization confusion) failure could even in principle be observed.
missing: an experiment that tests, rather than assumes, Governance-as-external-constraint and Authorization-as-governance-mechanism

rows.anchor: `C0` as given achieves 21/25 capabilities and 9/16 scenarios. It cannot produce `Evidence`, therefore cannot produce a `Verdict`, therefore cannot validate ... **The candidate operator set is not adequate to its own stated purpose.**
rows.statement: N-1: the raw candidate 13-operator set C0 achieves only 21/25 capabilities and 9/16 scenarios and cannot produce Evidence (hence no Verdict, no validation, no represented uncertainty or assumptions), so the candidate operator set as originally proposed is not adequate to its own stated purpose; all downstream ablation had to be run on a repaired baseline.

rows.anchor: 0 capabilities lost, 0 of 16 scenarios lost, 0 property failures, in all 8 model variants. This is the cleanest negative result in the experiment and it is a *positive* finding about the kernel.
rows.statement: N-2: removing DetectGap loses 0 capabilities, 0 scenarios, and causes 0 property failures across all 8 model variants — the cleanest negative result in the experiment, treated as positive evidence that DetectGap is not a kernel primitive.

rows.anchor: `Discriminate` appeared removable **only because `DetectGap` redundantly carried its atom.** Under V4 ... `Discriminate` is irreducible. This is exactly the failure mode Part XXI names ... Recorded as F19, **not** as a kernel result.
rows.statement: N-3: Discriminate's apparent removability under plain leave-one-out is an implementation artifact (F19) caused by DetectGap redundantly carrying Discriminate's atom, not a genuine kernel finding; under variant V4 (difference-decision scoped to the norm delta) Discriminate becomes irreducible.

rows.anchor: `{DetectGap, Determine}`, `{DetectGap, Discriminate}`, `{Hypothesize, Infer}`, `{Hypothesize, Represent}`. Structural dependency, not redundancy. A leave-one-out-only study would have reported C5 and C8 as needed by nobody.
rows.statement: N-4: five operators across four pairs are individually removable but not jointly removable, reflecting structural dependency rather than redundancy; a leave-one-out-only study would have wrongly reported capabilities C5 and C8 as needed by no operator.

rows.anchor: Triple ablations over both implicated clusters returned exactly the union of the pairwise losses. The dependency structure of this model is second-order. Recorded because it *bounds* the complexity.
rows.statement: N-5: triple ablations over both implicated clusters returned exactly the union of the corresponding pairwise losses, showing no third-order interaction and bounding the C0+ model's dependency structure at second order.

rows.anchor: removing `Validate`, `Qualify`, `Observe` or `Interpret` drives P10's guard to **0.00**; removing `Determine` drives P2's and P6's guards to **0.00**. Those arms' "no property failures" are **vacuous passes**. Property tests detect *misbehaviour*; ablation produces *incapacity*; the two are different and only the second is what leave-one-out creates.
rows.statement: N-6: removing certain operators (Validate/Qualify/Observe/Interpret for P10's guard; Determine for P2/P6's guards) drives the corresponding randomized-property guard-activation rate to 0.00, making those arms' 'no property failures' vacuous passes rather than genuine evidence of correct behaviour; property tests detect misbehaviour while ablation produces incapacity, and only the latter is what leave-one-out measures — with the standing methodological consequence that an algebraic/behavioural property should never be reported from a zero-counterexample result without a degeneracy (active-trial-count) check.
invariants: never report a zero-counterexample algebraic/behavioural property result without a degeneracy check and the count of active trials

rows.anchor: Guard activation 0.00 in every arm. The simulator carries provenance structurally, so no operator set can lose it. Its universal pass is worthless and C18 was reclassified non-discriminating (§03 M-2). This is a **simulator artifact**, not a kernel property.
rows.statement: N-7: property P3 (provenance) is untestable in this instrument — guard activation is 0.00 in every arm because the simulator carries provenance structurally via its derivation DAG, so no operator set can ever lose it; its universal pass is worthless evidence and capability C18 was reclassified non-discriminating, a simulator artifact (F20) rather than a finding about the kernel.

rows.anchor: In V7 (no `Qualify`) `Validate` classifies as derivable — but only because *no* operator set can produce a `Verdict` at all, so its atom is inert. A vacuous derivability. Rejected as evidence.
rows.statement: N-8: under variant V7 (no Qualify), Validate classifies as derivable only because no operator set whatsoever can produce a Verdict, rendering its warrant-assessment atom inert — a vacuous derivability (F20) explicitly rejected as evidence.

rows.anchor: 7 of 7 absorptions restored full coverage. **Reduction by absorption is always available and always worthless.** Any minimality claim lacking an explicit smuggling test is unfalsifiable.
rows.statement: N-9: every one of 7 semantic-smuggling absorption probes succeeded in restoring full capability coverage, demonstrating that reduction by absorption (secretly folding a removed operator's job into a remaining one) is always available and therefore always worthless as evidence of genuine minimality; any minimality claim lacking an explicit smuggling test is unfalsifiable.

rows.anchor: V1 fuses `meaning-assignment` and `symbolic-encoding` into one atom and **loses no capability.** So "all 14 atoms are irreducible" holds *relative to the declared capability model* and is not an absolute result.
rows.statement: N-10: model variant V1, which fuses the meaning-assignment and symbolic-encoding atoms into one, loses no capability, so the claim that all 14 atoms are irreducible holds only relative to the declared 25-capability model and is not an absolute result — directly limiting the atom-level 'shape hypothesis'.

rows.anchor: No scenario exercises it; failure class F18 (governance/authorization confusion) was observed zero times *because it could not be observed*. The Part XVI hypothesis "Authorization = governance mechanism" is **assumed in the model, not tested by it**
rows.statement: N-11: Authorization was never experimentally tested — no scenario exercises it and failure class F18 could not even in principle be observed — so the hypothesis 'Authorization = governance mechanism' (and likewise 'Governance = external constraint') is assumed in the model rather than tested by it, and neither may be cited as an experimental result.
missing: a scenario/experiment design that could actually exercise Authorization and Governance rather than assume them

rows.anchor: It answers "can this operator set do X at all?", never "how well". The corpus's seven distinct revision verbs are indistinguishable to it; so are a rich and a poor interpretation. Every result is bounded by this.
rows.statement: N-12: the simulator cannot see degree at all (only reachability of a capability kind), so the corpus's seven distinct revision verbs are indistinguishable to it, as are a rich and a poor interpretation; every result in the experiment is bounded by this structural limitation.

rows.anchor: Both are 13. The result the protocol warned against — optimizing for numerical smallness — was structurally unavailable here. This is fortunate rather than clever.
rows.statement: N-13: the experiment's two candidate minimal kernels both have cardinality 13, so cardinality alone could not discriminate between them — the protocol's warned-against failure mode of optimizing for numerical smallness over semantic/compositional minimality was structurally unavailable in this run, described as fortunate rather than a deliberate methodological achievement.

rows.anchor: Only 6 of 1 782 corpus files contain ≥6 of the 13 operator tokens ... `Hypothesize` (2 role files), `Select` (3) and `Represent` (5) are near-unsupported. The experiment tested a *proposal*, not an established vocabulary, and its conclusions inherit that limitation.
rows.statement: N-14: the C0 operator set as a whole has almost no corpus provenance — only 6 of 1,782 corpus files contain at least 6 of the 13 operator tokens, and half of those are this research lane's own prompts or same-day external extracts; Hypothesize, Select and Represent are near-unsupported by the corpus, meaning the experiment tested a proposed vocabulary rather than an established one, and every downstream conclusion inherits that limitation.

rows.anchor: Every "irreducible" claim carries a conceivable falsifier. A claim without one is not a result.
rows.statement: Standing methodological discipline for the kernel-reduction experiment: every claim that an operator or atom is irreducible/primitive must carry a conceivable falsifier, or it does not count as a result.

rows.anchor: `Observe` is primitive (`world-contact`) | Exhibit a typed composition of the remaining operators that yields an `Observation` carrying empirical content about the world. ... **Refuting this refutes P7.**
rows.statement: F-1: the falsifier for Observe's primitivity (world-contact atom) is a typed composition of the remaining operators yielding an Observation carrying empirical content about the world; this would require some operator to introduce world contact without world contact, which would itself violate property P7 (no information creation) or constitute smuggling — so refuting F-1 would also refute P7.

rows.anchor: **Already falsified under V1**, where encoding and meaning are one atom. Survives only if the corpus distinction `Observation ≠ Proposition ≠ Knowledge` is load-bearing at *both* steps.
rows.statement: F-3: Represent's primitivity (symbolic-encoding atom) is already falsified under variant V1, which fuses encoding and meaning into one atom without losing capability; Represent survives as a distinct primitive only if the corpus's Observation != Proposition != Knowledge distinction is load-bearing at both the meaning-assignment and the symbolic-encoding steps separately.

rows.anchor: **Already falsified under V3**, where adequacy is `difference-decision` over the norm delta w.r.t. requirements. Survives only if closure carries something a difference verdict does not — plausibly the *epistemic contract* `EC`. Decisive test: is `EC` reducible to a requirement set?
rows.statement: F-12: Determine's primitivity (closure-judgment atom) is already falsified under variant V3 (adequacy modelled as a difference-decision over the norm delta relative to requirements); it survives as primitive only if 'closure' carries something a bare difference-verdict does not, plausibly the epistemic contract EC, making 'is EC reducible to a requirement set?' the decisive open test.
missing: a determination of whether the epistemic contract EC is reducible to a requirement set

rows.anchor: **Already falsified under V5**. Survives only if choosing under an objective is more than deciding a difference. Also open on the *other* side: `Select` may belong to a neighbouring bounded context entirely (§13).
rows.statement: F-13: Select's primitivity (preference-over-actions atom) is already falsified under variant V5; it survives as a kernel primitive only if choosing under an objective is more than deciding a difference, and remains additionally open on whether Select belongs to the epistemic kernel or a neighbouring bounded context entirely.

rows.anchor: Fuse any two atoms into one and show no capability distinction is lost. V1 does exactly this for `meaning`/`encoding` and **no capability was lost** — so this claim is already *conditionally* falsified, and holds only relative to the declared capability model.
rows.statement: F-15: the claim that all 14 atoms are irreducible is already conditionally falsified by variant V1's fusion of the meaning-assignment and symbolic-encoding atoms without capability loss, so atom-irreducibility holds only relative to the declared capability model, not absolutely.

rows.anchor: Exhibit a required capability that depends on the *packaging* — something two kernels with identical atoms but different operator groupings do differently. This experiment found none, but did not search hard for one. `[OPEN]`
rows.statement: F-16: falsifying the claim that the kernel is better described as an operator set than as a (P,R,delta) triple (primitives/composition-relations/transition-mechanism) requires exhibiting a required capability that depends on operator packaging rather than atom content; the experiment found no such capability but did not search hard for one, leaving this genuinely open.
missing: a deliberate search for a packaging-dependent capability distinguishing operator-set kernels from (P,R,delta)-shaped kernels

rows.anchor: Is `closure-judgment` primitive, or is adequacy a difference-decision over the norm delta? `Determine`'s status flips on it (V3). Determines whether the kernel has 13 or 12 irreducible powers.
rows.statement: Q-1 (blocking): whether closure-judgment is a primitive atom or reducible to a difference-decision over the norm delta determines whether Determine survives as irreducible (flips under V3) and therefore whether the kernel has 13 or 12 irreducible powers; the cheapest next test is deciding whether the epistemic contract EC is reducible to a requirement set.

rows.anchor: Does `Select` belong to the epistemic kernel at all, or to a neighbouring bounded context? ... A strategic-DDD context-map question, **not** a minimality experiment. Wrong instrument used so far.
rows.statement: Q-3 (blocking): whether Select belongs to the epistemic kernel or a neighbouring bounded context is identified as a strategic-DDD context-map question that a minimality experiment is the wrong instrument to answer, since Select is the only operator whose output no epistemic capability consumes and whose input (Objective) the kernel does not own.

rows.anchor: Is `Revise` a domain operation or an infrastructure mechanism? If mechanism, the kernel emits *proposals* and committing belongs elsewhere — a different kernel shape.
rows.statement: Q-4 (blocking): whether Revise is a domain operation or an infrastructure mechanism is unresolved; if it is a mechanism, the kernel would properly emit proposals with committing belonging to a different context entirely, implying a materially different kernel shape. Cheapest next test: check whether the corpus's seven revision verbs are epistemically distinguishable, which the current simulator cannot do.

rows.anchor: The capability set C1–C25 was largely inherited from the prompt. What would an *independently derived* capability set look like, and would the results survive it? (This is the deepest robustness question and V1–V7 only scratch it.)
rows.statement: Q-14 (method-level, flagged as the deepest robustness question): the capability set C1-C25 was largely inherited from the originating prompt rather than independently derived, and it is unknown whether the experiment's results would survive an independently derived capability set; the eight tested variants V1-V7 only scratch this concern.
missing: an independently derived capability set to test the robustness of C1-C25-based conclusions

rows.anchor: Not *"which operator do we delete?"* but: **What is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive?** ... all 14 atoms irreducible but only 12 of 14 operators; two minimal kernels of identical cardinality differing only in packaging; and three operators ... whose status flips under a single defensible change of granularity. **The instability is in the granularity, not in the count.**
rows.statement: The experiment's terminal [PROP] reframing: the right next research question is not 'which operator do we delete' but 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive', supported by the evidence that all 14 atoms are irreducible while only 12 of 14 operators are, that two minimal kernels of identical cardinality (13) differ only in packaging, and that Interpret/Represent, Determine, and Select each flip status under a single defensible granularity change — concluding the instability discovered by this experiment is in granularity, not in count.

rows.anchor: The experiment provides structural evidence for several distinctions and exposes several candidate primitives, but it also demonstrates that the current notion of primitive/minimality is model-dependent and that some apparent results are artifacts of the simulator's representation and guards.
rows.statement: States the file's core adjudication verdict: the kernel-reduction experiment does not prove the proposed kernel and does not falsify the KnowledgeOS programme, but it does falsify the stronger claim that the current 12/13-operator list is already the minimal kernel, and demonstrates that primitive/minimality is model-dependent with some apparent results being simulator artifacts.

rows.anchor: "The rates are properties of the generator, not estimates of any population." ... They establish something much narrower: P_generator(failure|ablation) under the specified synthetic world generator. The Wilson intervals therefore measure: Monte-Carlo uncertainty not: theoretical uncertainty.
rows.statement: Endorses as methodologically correct the report's own statistical discipline: randomized-trial failure rates and Wilson confidence intervals measure only Monte-Carlo uncertainty about the synthetic world generator's behaviour, not theoretical/population uncertainty about KnowledgeOS itself.

rows.anchor: the actual inference is: $$G_\theta\models P$$ or: $$G_\theta\not\models P.$$ It is not: $$KnowledgeOS\models P$$ in the unrestricted sense.
rows.statement: Identifies a fundamental limitation: because the experiment samples worlds from a synthetic generator G_theta rather than 'the world', every property result is properly stated as G_theta |= P or G_theta not|= P, never as the unrestricted KnowledgeOS |= P; this distinction should become explicit in the final methodology.

rows.anchor: "A property whose antecedent is never active passes vacuously." ... If removing `Validate` makes validation impossible, then: No invalid validation is trivially true. ... Vacuity audit = validated methodological requirement ... I would make this a permanent KnowledgeOS experiment rule.
rows.statement: Endorses the vacuity audit as probably the most scientifically important part of the experiment: a property whose antecedent never becomes active passes vacuously (e.g. removing Validate trivially makes 'no invalid validation occurs' true because validation cannot occur at all), so operator-ablation results reporting 'no failures' cannot be read as evidence of unnecessity without checking guard activation; proposes making the vacuity audit a permanent KnowledgeOS experiment rule.

rows.anchor: Safety: Nothing invalid happens. from: Liveness/capability: The required thing can happen. ... Every candidate kernel operation should be tested on at least: $$Capability \times Safety$$
rows.statement: Introduces a formal safety-vs-capability(liveness) distinction (safety: nothing invalid happens; capability/liveness: the required thing can happen) and proposes a two-dimensional Capability x Safety verification matrix for every candidate kernel operation, with a worked example table (Challenge/Validate/Determine/Interpret/Revise each given both a capability question and a safety question), as an improvement over reporting a single failure rate per operator.

rows.anchor: P(P10 failure|P10 active)=1. ... removing `Challenge` produces verdicts without possible defeat. ... the causal/model-criticism experiment independently produces: OLS beta=1.852, R^2=.899, true causal effect=0. ... This gives genuine **cross-instrument convergence**.
rows.statement: Identifies Challenge as the strongest candidate primitive found so far: its guard-conditioned failure rate is 1.0 (removing Challenge always produces verdicts without possible defeat, surviving the vacuity check since the guard is active), independently corroborated by a separate causal/model-criticism experiment showing strong statistical fit (R^2=.899) coexisting with zero true causal effect -- a genuine cross-instrument convergence stronger than a single randomized failure rate.

rows.anchor: The experiment establishes: Some challenge/defeater functionality is necessary for the tested epistemic contract. It does **not** establish: `Challenge` must be an irreducible kernel primitive. Because perhaps: Challenge = GenerateAlternative + TestAgainstEvidence + EvaluateDefeater. ... I would record: Challenge: [PROP] strong functional necessity not: Challenge: [CANON] primitive.
rows.statement: Corrects the strength of the Challenge finding: the experiment establishes that some challenge/defeater functionality is necessary, not that a named Challenge operator is an irreducible kernel primitive, since Challenge could in principle decompose into GenerateAlternative+TestAgainstEvidence+EvaluateDefeater, or CounterexampleSearch+Validate, or Revise+Infer under a different state representation; recommends recording Challenge only as [PROP] strong functional necessity, not [CANON] primitive.

rows.anchor: V6 is defined as: a `Verdict` requires a surviving-defeater step. Then naturally: V6=>Challenge required. That is almost definitional. The stronger experiment would ask: Can *any* implementation that lacks the specific `Challenge` operator nevertheless satisfy the same epistemic requirement through a composition of other operators? ... we need a **semantic capability test**, not merely an operator-name ablation.
rows.statement: Warns that variant V6's causal-necessity result for Challenge may be partly circular ('baking the answer into the experiment') because V6 defines a Verdict as requiring a surviving-defeater step, making Challenge-required almost definitional; argues for a semantic capability test asking whether any Challenge-free composition of remaining operators could satisfy the same requirement, rather than a bare operator-name ablation.
missing: a semantic capability test for whether Challenge-free compositions can satisfy the same epistemic requirement as V6

rows.anchor:
$$Model\ fit
eq epistemic\ validity.$$ ... A system can have: R^2=.899 and: beta=1.852 while: ATE=0. Therefore: $$Infer
eq Validate.$$ and: $$Fit
eq Truth.$$
rows.statement: Generalizes the causal OLS-vs-true-effect result (R^2=.899, beta=1.852, true ATE=0) beyond Freedman's association != causation into the broader KnowledgeOS principles ModelFit != EpistemicValidity and, correspondingly, Infer != Validate and Fit != Truth, offered as strong support for keeping model-criticism/challenge functionality somewhere in the epistemic pipeline.

rows.anchor: `DetectGap` is derivable in 8/8 variants, including V4, which was deliberately designed to protect it. ... $$DetectGap\text{ is probably not primitive.}$$ ... Potentially: DetectGap = Compare + Qualify. ... $$Zero:\text{ predicate}$$ and: $$DetectGap:\text{ derived operation}$$
rows.statement: Identifies DetectGap-is-derivable-in-8/8-variants (including V4, deliberately designed to protect it) as the strongest result against the then-current kernel, reinforcing the hypothesis that Zero is a state predicate rather than an operation, and proposing DetectGap = Compare + Qualify as a candidate elegant reduction, formalized as Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) = [Adequacy(K_t,I_Q,EC)=false] with DetectGap = Evaluate(Zero).
missing: experimental confirmation of the specific Zero=Adequacy-false / DetectGap=Evaluate(Zero) formalization

rows.anchor: `Discriminate` is derivable in 7/8 variants, failing only V4. ... the apparent primitiveness of `Discriminate` depends partly on how `DetectGap` was represented. This is a classic **representation-relative minimality** problem.
rows.statement: Identifies Discriminate's derivability in 7/8 variants (failing only V4) as a classic representation-relative-minimality problem: its apparent primitiveness depends on how DetectGap's atom was scoped, so Primitive(f) cannot mean merely 'the simulator could not eliminate the function' but must mean 'no admissible representation and composition of the remaining semantic capabilities can reproduce the function.'

rows.anchor: Syntactic irreducibility: $$f\notin Closure(F\setminus\{f\})$$ in one chosen simulator representation. from: Semantic irreducibility: $$\not\exists R'\in\mathcal R,\,C'\in\mathcal C: Semantics(f)=Semantics(C'(R',F\setminus f)).$$ The second is what we actually want.
rows.statement: Formalizes the distinction between syntactic irreducibility (f not derivable from the remaining operators within one fixed simulator representation) and semantic irreducibility (no admissible representation R' and composition C' can reproduce f's semantics from the remaining operators), arguing the kernel-minimality problem is properly a representation+composition+semantic-equivalence minimality problem, not mere operator ablation.

rows.anchor: under V1, where meaning-assignment and symbolic-encoding are merged, `Interpret` and `Represent` derive each other. ... They could be two projections of one deeper transformation: SemanticEncoding or: MeaningRepresentation ... The correct conclusion is: Interpret/Represent split is not proven primitive.
rows.statement: Argues the V1 result (Interpret and Represent mutually derivable when meaning-assignment and symbolic-encoding are merged into one atom) confirms Davidson-derived expectations that the two may not be ontologically separate operations but two projections of one deeper SemanticEncoding/MeaningRepresentation transformation; recommends not merging them yet but concluding only that the Interpret/Represent split is not proven primitive, and that the decomposition is representation-dependent (a 'modelling choice').

rows.anchor: the sentence "no downstream operator can recover what the meaning step did not carry" requires an important qualification. It is only true if downstream processing receives **no additional information**. ... the correct principle is: No downstream transformation of S' alone can increase its mutual information with X. Not: No downstream system can ever recover it.
rows.statement: Corrects an overstatement in the information-theoretic sub-experiment (I(X;S)=1.5 with meaning assignment, I(X;S')=0.5 without it, loss 1.0 bit): the correct data-processing-inequality-consistent principle is that no downstream transformation of S' alone can increase its mutual information with X, not that no downstream system whatsoever can ever recover the lost information (recovery is possible if additional context is supplied alongside S').

rows.anchor: $$Information\ loss\neq Semantic\ inadequacy.$$ And: $$Semantic\ inadequacy\neq Epistemic\ invalidity.$$ ... we now have three different failure layers: L_1=information loss, L_2=semantic inadequacy, L_3=epistemic invalidity.
rows.statement: Endorses and names a three-layer failure taxonomy distinguishing L1 (information loss), L2 (semantic inadequacy) and L3 (epistemic invalidity) as non-collapsing, generalizing the information/semantic-adequacy/epistemic-validity separation the source report already draws.

rows.anchor: the previous candidate list ... implicitly assumed that **operations are the primary mathematical objects**. I now think that assumption itself needs testing. A more fundamental model may be: $$State + Constraints + Transformations$$ rather than: $$Operator\ List.$$
rows.statement: Argues the entire operator-list framing of the kernel implicitly assumes operations are the primary mathematical objects, an assumption itself needing testing, and proposes a more fundamental candidate model of State + Constraints + Transformations (Zero as predicate, Evidence as state component, Standards as parameter, Relations as structure) with only some transformations being genuine kernel operations.

rows.anchor: $$\mathcal E_t=(K_t,E_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,R_t)$$ ... $$\mathcal E_{t+1}=T(\mathcal E_t,e_{t+1})$$ rather than immediately defining T as a fixed list of named operations. The kernel question becomes: What is the smallest transformation algebra capable of producing the required state transitions?
rows.statement: Proposes reformalizing the epistemic system as a state E_t=(K_t,E_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,R_t) with transitions E_{t+1}=T(E_t,e_{t+1}), deferring the decomposition of T into named operations, reframing the kernel question as finding the smallest transformation algebra capable of producing required state transitions rather than naming a fixed operator list.

rows.anchor: The report finds `Select` derivable under V5 when: ActionChoice = DifferenceDecision + Objective. This strongly suggests that: Select should probably **not** be assumed to belong to the epistemic kernel. It may belong to: DecisionTheory. ... I currently favor: $$Select\notin\ epistemic\ kernel$$ as a hypothesis
rows.statement: Argues, from V5's decomposition of ActionChoice into DifferenceDecision+Objective, that Select probably does not belong to the epistemic kernel but to a separate decision-theory layer, consistent with Titelbaum's theoretical/practical-rationality split; favors the hypothesis Select not-in epistemic kernel, held as [PROP].

rows.anchor: If the simulator internally stores: SemanticContent, Hypothesis, Evidence, NormDelta then it has already provided a representation layer for free. Ablating `Represent` therefore may not actually remove representation. ... Represent ablation must remove representational capability, not merely the operator name.
rows.statement: Warns that Represent showing no ablation failure may indicate representation is silently built into every simulator object (SemanticContent, Hypothesis, Evidence, NormDelta already exist as data structures independent of the Represent operator), so ablating the operator's name may not actually remove representational capability -- a general warning that ablation must remove a capability, not merely a function label. A parallel concern is raised for Observe: if simulated worlds already contain pre-formed Entity/Observation/Claim/Evidence objects, ablating Observe tests 'label removal' rather than 'capability removal.'

rows.anchor: `Hypothesize` could be decomposed into: GenerateCandidate + Represent + Relate or even: Interpret + Infer. Therefore the real question is: Can alternative-generation be semantically reconstructed from the other capabilities?
rows.statement: Argues Hypothesize's ablation failures (P2/P8) are potentially strong evidence but that Hypothesize could still decompose into GenerateCandidate+Represent+Relate or Interpret+Infer, framing the real open question as whether alternative-generation can be semantically reconstructed from other capabilities, requiring a dedicated experiment.
missing: a dedicated experiment testing whether Hypothesize decomposes into other capabilities

rows.anchor: $$Determination\ without\ alternative\ awareness\ can\ produce\ fabricated\ uniqueness.$$ ... Potential formal invariant: $$Determine(H)\Rightarrow Alternatives(H,Q)\text{ have been adequately considered}$$ ... connect: Davidson's interpretive alternatives; Dretske's relevant alternatives; Freedman's rival explanations; Bayesian hypothesis spaces; KnowledgeOS `Challenge`; Zero.
rows.statement: Proposes what it calls potentially the biggest theoretical discovery: 'determination without alternative awareness can produce fabricated uniqueness', formalized as a candidate invariant Determine(H) => Alternatives(H,Q) have been adequately considered, and notes this would connect six independent cross-source threads (Davidson's interpretive alternatives, Dretske's relevant alternatives, Freedman's rival explanations, Bayesian hypothesis spaces, KnowledgeOS Challenge, and Zero) into one convergent finding -- named 'No Determination Without Alternative Space', formalized as Determine(K,Q,EC) => exists a nonempty alternative space A_Q={H_1,...,H_n} against which the determination is evaluated.
missing: a dedicated experiment proving the No-Determination-Without-Alternative-Space invariant rather than merely proposing it

rows.anchor: Old question: Which operators belong to the KnowledgeOS kernel? Better question: **Which epistemic capabilities and invariants are irreducible under admissible alternative representations and compositions?** Then operators become one possible implementation of those capabilities.
rows.statement: Reframes the guiding kernel-research question from 'which operators belong to the kernel' to 'which epistemic capabilities and invariants are irreducible under admissible alternative representations and compositions', treating named operators as merely one possible implementation of underlying capabilities.

rows.anchor: I1 -- Evidence/state separation E_t!=K_t ... I6 -- Determination is inquiry-relative Determine=Determine(K,Q,EC) ... I8 -- Determination requires adequate alternative handling ... I10 -- Zero is not probability zero. These are considerably more fundamental than the current operator list.
rows.statement: Consolidates ten candidate KnowledgeOS invariants (I1-I10: Evidence!=State; Claim!=Assessment; Credence!=Truth; ModelFit!=Validity; InformationQuantity!=SemanticAdequacy; Determination is inquiry-relative; evidence accumulation does not imply knowledge accumulation; determination requires adequate alternative handling; verdicts require defeater consideration; Zero is not probability-zero) as the file's recommended things-to-freeze-as-research-findings, explicitly held as not yet canon and more fundamental than the operator list itself.

rows.anchor: I would explicitly reject the following conclusions from the current experiment: Not established: Challenge is mathematically primitive ... Observe is primitive ... Interpret and Represent are separate primitives ... Hypothesize is primitive ... Relate is primitive ... Validate is primitive ... Determine is primitive ... Select belongs to the epistemic kernel ... The 12/13-operation kernel is minimal.
rows.statement: Explicitly enumerates nine conclusions the file rejects as not-yet-established from the reviewed experiment: primitivity of Challenge, Observe, Hypothesize, Relate, Validate, Determine; separateness of Interpret/Represent; Select's kernel membership; and minimality of the 12/13-operator kernel overall.

rows.anchor: EXP-01 The current simulator can distinguish capability loss from safety-property failure. EXP-02 Vacuous property satisfaction is a real threat and must be audited. EXP-03 Randomized property testing alone is insufficient for kernel minimality. EXP-04 Capability and scenario ablation are more informative for primitive testing. ... EXP-08 `DetectGap` appears derivable ... EXP-09 `Discriminate` appears representation-dependent ... EXP-10 `Interpret`/`Represent` decomposition is representation-dependent. EXP-11 `Determine` remains model-dependent. EXP-12 `Select` remains model-dependent and may belong downstream.
rows.statement: Consolidates twelve findings (EXP-01..EXP-12) the file DOES accept as established by the reviewed experiment, spanning methodological results (simulator can distinguish capability loss from safety failure; vacuity is a real threat; randomized testing alone is insufficient; capability/scenario ablation is more informative) and substantive operator results (DetectGap derivable; Discriminate and Interpret/Represent-split representation-dependent; Determine and Select model-dependent).

rows.anchor: # Semantic Kernel Equivalence Experiment ... construct multiple semantically equivalent implementations ... Behavior(K) =? Behavior(K-{Challenge}+Composition) under a formal observation interface. If yes: Challenge is not primitive. If no across all admissible representations tested: Challenge becomes a much stronger primitive candidate.
rows.statement: Proposes a follow-on 'Semantic Kernel Equivalence Experiment': for each candidate primitive f, construct multiple independently plausible semantically equivalent implementations (e.g. three different decompositions of Challenge) and test observable-behaviour equivalence Behavior(K) =? Behavior(K-{f}+Composition) under a formal observation interface, rather than relying on a single simulator's internal atom bookkeeping.

rows.anchor: Define an externally observable behavior: $$B(\mathcal K,W,Q,EC)$$ rather than comparing internal operator traces. ... two implementations are equivalent if: $$B_1(W,Q,EC)=B_2(W,Q,EC)$$ for all relevant test worlds W. For probabilistic systems: $$\mathcal L(B_1|W,Q,EC)=\mathcal L(B_2|W,Q,EC).$$
rows.statement: Proposes a formal notion of behavioral equivalence for kernel implementations, defined via an externally observable behaviour function B(K,W,Q,EC): two candidate kernels K1,K2 are equivalent iff their observable behaviours (or, for probabilistic systems, their laws) agree for all relevant test worlds W -- explicitly identified as currently missing from the experiment.
missing: a concrete definition of the observable-behaviour function B for KnowledgeOS

rows.anchor: Instead of random ablation only: propose a reduction; search for a counterexample; if counterexample exists, preserve the primitive; if not, generate another semantic decomposition; continue. In other words: $$CEGAR$$ style kernel reduction.
rows.statement: Proposes counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR)-style kernel reduction as an alternative to pure random ablation: iteratively propose a reduction, search for a counterexample world where the reduced kernel's behaviour differs, and either preserve the primitive (counterexample found) or generate a new decomposition and continue, framed as a search for min|K| subject to universal behavioural equivalence, acknowledging the universal quantifier cannot be proven computationally but can be attacked by aggressive counterexample search.

rows.anchor: $$K_t=\Phi(E_{\leq t},S_t,Q_t,C_t,R_t)$$ with: $$K_{t+1}=U(K_t,e_{t+1},S_{t+1},Q_{t+1},C_{t+1}).$$ ... $$Decision_t=D(K_t,Q,Objective,Authorization).$$ This gives a much cleaner separation: Epistemic system -> Decision system -> Governance/Authorization.
rows.statement: Restates the file's provisional overall mathematical model: K_t = Phi(E_{<=t},S_t,Q_t,C_t,R_t), K_{t+1}=U(K_t,e_{t+1},S_{t+1},Q_{t+1},C_{t+1}), with Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) as a predicate, Determine(K_t,Q,EC) as a judgment/transition of unknown primitive status, and Decision_t=D(K_t,Q,Objective,Authorization), giving a three-layer separation Epistemic system -> Decision system -> Governance/Authorization.

rows.anchor: The 2,052-line protocol was authored by me (ChatGPT) and supplied to Claude Code CLI as the experimental execution prompt. Claude was the executor of the protocol, not the author of the experimental methodology. ... three layers: ChatGPT-authored protocol ... Claude Code CLI execution ... Our current audit
rows.statement: Discloses and formalizes the multi-agent provenance of the kernel-reduction research: the 2,052-line experimental protocol (research question, constraints, capability model, composition rules, ablation/scenario design, falsification logic) was authored by a separate agent identified as 'ChatGPT' and merely executed by Claude Code CLI (which built the simulator and generated the 18 artifacts and results); the current document is a third, independent audit layer assessing whether the protocol itself was well-posed, distinct from assessing the execution's fidelity.

rows.anchor: `C0` omits `Qualify`. ... the corpus reconstruction subsequently establishes: Qualify: Observation x Policy -> Evidence as an already existing candidate capability, with prior status G1 -- irreducible. Therefore: The experiment did not begin with the complete candidate universe.
rows.statement: Identifies as the critical protocol-design flaw that the baseline candidate set C0 omitted Qualify (Observation x Policy -> Evidence), even though the corpus's own prior reconstruction had already identified Qualify as an existing candidate capability with irreducible status G1 -- meaning the experiment did not begin with a complete candidate universe, and the defensible conclusion is only that C0 as specified fails its own baseline capability requirements, not that 'the KnowledgeOS kernel requires 14 irreducible powers.'

rows.anchor: Experiment A -- reduction: Given a closed candidate universe C: find minimal S subset-of C such that all required capabilities are reachable. Experiment B -- candidate discovery: Determine whether C itself contains all capabilities required by the corpus/theory. Those should have been separated.
rows.statement: Diagnoses that the protocol conflated two experiments that should have been kept separate: Experiment A (closed-world reduction: given a fixed candidate universe C, find the minimal subset reaching all required capabilities) and Experiment B (candidate discovery: determine whether C itself is complete relative to the corpus/theory) -- the closed-world reduction began before candidate completeness had been established.

rows.anchor: `C0` has weak corpus provenance ... a research construction. ... the corpus has a much larger operator vocabulary: ~50 candidate names across nine families. ... $$DetectGap\in\mathcal O?$$ according to the corpus itself. So the experiment's finding DetectGap is derivable is **independently supported by corpus classification**.
