rows.anchor: we need a semantic equivalence relation $$r_1\equiv_{\mathrm{sem}}r_2$$ iff they preserve the same required epistemic meaning ... if B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) is the observable epistemic behaviour of representation r, then: r1=_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain. This is not supplied by measure theory. It is the mathematical object demanded by the latest kernel experiment.
rows.statement: Defines Semantic Equivalence r1 =_sem r2 for two admissible representations of epistemic states as agreement of an observable-behaviour function B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) over the admissible test domain, explicitly noting this is NOT supplied by measure theory but is exactly the mathematical object the kernel-reduction experiment's instability demands.
missing: a concrete definition of B_r for KnowledgeOS

rows.anchor: This new formulation explains **why the previous 13-vs-8 kernel experiment became unstable**. The experiment was effectively asking: What is the smallest operator set? before completely fixing: X, A, =_sem, K, D, T. ... The correct research order is now: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.
rows.statement: Explains the kernel-reduction experiment's 13-vs-8 instability as a direct consequence of attempting to answer 'what is the smallest operator set' before fixing X (carrier), A (sigma-field), =_sem (semantic equivalence), K (Knowledge-State space), D (gap operator) and T (transition); prescribes a corrected nine-stage research order: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.

rows.anchor: **The type of E_t should be fixed before kernel minimality is claimed.** That follows directly from the earlier kernel experiments. ... $$E_{a,c,t}=\{Believes(p),Hypothesizes(q),Rejects(r)\}$$ does not imply: Knows(a,p,c,t). ... Belief != Knowledge, Hypothesis != Knowledge, Assertion != Knowledge, Evidence != Knowledge, Probability != Knowledge.
rows.statement: Argues, citing the kernel experiments' own lesson, that the internal decomposition/type of an Epistemic State E_{a,c,t} must be fixed before kernel minimality can be meaningfully claimed, deliberately leaving E's tuple type abstract (E in the admissible epistemic-state domain) rather than freezing a specific field list; derives a five-way non-collapse Belief != Knowledge, Hypothesis != Knowledge, Assertion != Knowledge, Evidence != Knowledge, Probability != Knowledge from the fact that holding beliefs/hypotheses/rejections about p does not itself entail Knows(a,p,c,t).

rows.anchor: An epistemic operator is not necessarily a primitive object. It is a **transition-generating capability** over epistemic states. ... The experiments were effectively asking: Which state-transition capabilities cannot be reconstructed from the others? That is a more rigorous question than: Which operator names are irreducible?
rows.statement: Reinterprets epistemic operators (Hypothesize, Challenge, Revise, Qualify, Infer, each given a signature Op(E,...)->E') as transition-generating capabilities over epistemic states rather than primitive objects in themselves, reframing the kernel-reduction question from 'which operator names are irreducible' to 'which state-transition capabilities cannot be reconstructed from the others' -- judged a more rigorous question.

rows.anchor: We should not optimize: |operator names|. Instead optimize: **minimal structure preserving required semantic behavior** ... define: $$\mathfrak R=\{\text{admissible representations of the epistemic structure}\}.$$ Two representations R_1,R_2 are equivalent if: R_1=_sem R_2 when they preserve the same required semantic behavior. This is exactly the missing level between representation and kernel.
rows.statement: Explains the 13-vs-8 kernel-minimality instability as a category error (optimizing the count of operator NAMES rather than minimal structure preserving required semantic behaviour), proposing a space of admissible representations R and a semantic-equivalence relation R1 =_sem R2 as the missing level between raw representation and kernel minimality.

rows.anchor: The Kernel is **not**: {Observe, Interpret, Represent,...} as a final ontology. Instead: $$Kernel=\text{minimal semantic structure whose required behavior is preserved}$$ Candidate structure: $$\mathcal K_0=(D,P,T,C,I,E,R,H,\Theta)$$
rows.statement: Redefines the Kernel itself away from a fixed operator-name ontology ({Observe, Interpret, Represent, ...}) toward the minimal semantic structure whose required behaviour is preserved, with the full relational core K_0=(D,P,T,C,I,E,R,H,Theta) as the candidate starting structure to be minimized, asking which components and relations can be removed while preserving all required semantic invariants and capabilities -- described as a much stronger minimality problem than the operator-list version.

rows.anchor: The correct conclusion is **not**: "The kernel has either 13 or 8 primitives." Rather: $$Operator\ cardinality\ is\ representation\text{-}dependent.$$ The real object is: $$semantic\ capability\ preservation.$$ ... 13 and 8 may simply be different presentations of equivalent semantic capabilities.
rows.statement: Resolves the 13-vs-8 kernel-cardinality disagreement by declaring operator cardinality inherently representation-dependent and semantic-capability preservation the real underlying object, hypothesizing that 13 and 8 may simply be different presentations of equivalent semantic capabilities (pending a settled semantic-equivalence relation).

rows.anchor: $$K_{\min}=\text{minimal semantic substrate preserving all required invariants and capabilities}$$ under the admissible representation family. Not: fewest operator names. ... it was measuring level 7 while levels 2 and 3 were not yet sufficiently defined.
rows.statement: Redefines kernel minimality K_min as the minimal semantic substrate preserving all required invariants and capabilities under the admissible representation family, explicitly not the fewest operator names, explaining the earlier kernel experiment's inconclusiveness as measuring at research-hierarchy level 7 while levels 2 (state type) and 3 (semantic equivalence) remained undefined.

rows.anchor: Open 1 -- exact type of K_t ... Open 2 -- exact semantic equivalence ... Open 3 -- exact atomic knowledge unit ... Open 4 -- exact discrepancy structure ... Open 5 -- epistemic adequacy ... Reachability != Epistemic Adequacy. ... Open 6 -- complete transition semantics ... Open 7 -- kernel minimality
rows.statement: Enumerates seven explicitly open questions in priority/dependency order: (1) the exact type of K_t, called still the most important mathematical question; (2) the exact definition of semantic equivalence, essential for kernel minimality; (3) the exact atomic knowledge unit k_t^i; (4) the exact discrepancy structure D(K_t,I_t) (must not be assumed a metric); (5) epistemic adequacy Adequate(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t), explicitly said to be more important than reachability, restating Reachability != Epistemic Adequacy; (6) complete transition semantics for revision/contradiction/supersession/reinstatement; (7) kernel minimality itself, only derivable once 1-6 are sufficiently defined.

rows.anchor: the old kernel experiment is not wasted. ... Its real result was: operator-name minimality is not the fundamental problem. ... 13 versus 8 ... becomes evidence that: semantic equivalence must precede kernel minimality. ... That is a **valuable theoretical result**, not a failed experiment.
rows.statement: Explicitly reframes the kernel-reduction experiment as not wasted: its real result was that operator-name minimality is not the fundamental problem, and the 13-vs-8 disagreement is positive evidence that semantic equivalence must precede kernel minimality, alongside the correctly identified Reachability != Epistemic Adequacy limitation -- judged a valuable theoretical result, not a failed experiment.

rows.anchor: Kernel shape: $$\mathcal K=(\mathcal P,\mathcal R,\delta,\mathcal I)$$ and potentially: $$\mathfrak K=(\mathcal P,\mathcal R,\delta,\mathcal I,\mathcal U)$$ ... This remains a **[PROP]**, not an established theorem.
rows.statement: Restates the candidate Kernel shape K=(P,R,delta,I) and extended K=(P,R,delta,I,U) (primitive powers, admissible composition, transition/commit semantics, protected invariants, optional uncertainty/assessment semantics), explicitly marked [PROP], not an established theorem.

rows.anchor: [THM-10] Under representation algebra A0: |K_min|=13. Under another admissible algebra: |K_min|=8. Therefore: |K_min| is not representation-invariant. ... the old methodology Operators->Ablation->Minimum is rejected. The correct methodology is: Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Adequacy -> Invariants -> Minimality.
rows.statement: [THM-10] Operator-count minimality is representation-relative: |K_min|=13 under algebra A0 and |K_min|=8 under another admissible algebra proves |K_min| is not representation-invariant, formally rejecting the old Operators->Ablation->Minimum methodology in favor of Representation->Capability->Reachability->Adequacy->Invariants->Minimality.

rows.anchor: Determination requires an adequately scoped alternative space ... Determine(K,Q,EC) => exists A_Q. Good provides independent statistical/philosophical support for this candidate. ... Pairwise superiority != global determination. ... comparative determination, exclusive determination, global determination, insufficiently scoped determination.
rows.statement: Provides independent statistical support for the corpus's already-emerging 'no determination without alternative space' hypothesis (Determine(K,Q,EC) => exists a nonempty alternative space A_Q), reinforced by Good's own three-or-more-hypotheses warning; extends it further by distinguishing four Determine sub-kinds -- comparative determination, exclusive determination, global determination, and insufficiently-scoped determination -- since H1>H2 among a scoped pair does not establish H1=true if an unconsidered H3 exists.

rows.anchor: when the complete body of knowledge K is too complicated to enumerate, one generally identifies a relevant subset H and works with that approximation. ... Relevant(E,Q,H,C) ... Total Evidence != Relevant Evidence ... SelectRelevant(E,Q,H,C) may be necessary somewhere in the epistemic lifecycle. But this does **not** prove that Select belongs in the irreducible kernel.
rows.statement: Extracts Good's relevance-subset practice to reinforce Total Evidence != Relevant Evidence (F_t != F_t^relevant), proposing a relevance relation Relevant(E,Q,H,C) and a candidate SelectRelevant(E,Q,H,C) operator; explicitly notes this establishes only the FUNCTION's necessity somewhere in the epistemic lifecycle, not that Select belongs in the irreducible kernel, leaving open whether relevance selection is an irreducible capability, part of Discriminate, part of Inquiry, part of Evidence assessment, or infrastructure.
missing: an experiment determining which of the five listed placements for relevance-selection is correct

rows.anchor: the more probable hypothesis is not necessarily the preferable one; utilities can matter. ... Epistemic Assessment != Decision Preference and: Determine != Select unless Select is defined specifically as epistemic hypothesis selection rather than practical action selection. ... Select may belong downstream of the epistemic kernel.
rows.statement: Uses Good's probability-vs-preference separation (P(H1)>P(H2) does not imply Choose(H1), since utilities matter) to independently strengthen the doubt that Select is a kernel primitive: Epistemic Assessment != Decision Preference, Determine != Select unless Select means epistemic hypothesis selection specifically (not practical action selection); recommends experimentally distinguishing Select_epistemic from Select_decision, calling this potentially materially relevant to the interpretation of the 13-operator kernel experiment.
missing: an experiment distinguishing Select_epistemic from Select_decision

rows.anchor: GAP-E2 ... $$AdequatelyScoped(\mathcal H,Q,C)$$ before Determine can legitimately claim exclusivity. This leads to at least: ComparativeDetermination versus: ExclusiveDetermination.
rows.statement: Names GAP-E2 (Hypothesis-space completeness): needs a formal AdequatelyScoped(H,Q,C) predicate before Determine can legitimately claim exclusivity, giving ComparativeDetermination vs ExclusiveDetermination as distinct notions -- noted as already consistent with the kernel research but now independently statistically founded via Good.
missing: a formal AdequatelyScoped predicate

rows.anchor: the current definition essentially says they have the same semantic meaning/behavior. That is conceptually correct, but mathematically circular unless the semantic interpretation function is independently defined. GAP-2 -- Semantic equivalence ... This is exactly why the 8-vs-13 kernel result remains unresolved.
rows.statement: Identifies GAP-2: v1.0's semantic equivalence r1=_sem r2 is mathematically CIRCULAR as currently stated (defined via 'same semantic meaning/behaviour' without an independently defined semantic interpretation function), and this circularity is exactly why the 8-vs-13 kernel result remains unresolved.
missing: a non-circular definition of semantic equivalence grounded in independently specified semantics

rows.anchor: $$K_{min}\text{ itself is still OPEN}.$$ The experiment demonstrated representation dependence rather than a universal 8- or 13-operator kernel.
rows.statement: Reaffirms that K_min remains genuinely open despite the constrained-optimization reformulation being a major methodological breakthrough: the kernel-reduction experiment demonstrated representation-dependence, not a universal 8- or 13-operator kernel.

rows.anchor: G1 Canonical mathematical type of K_t Critical. G2 Non-circular semantic equivalence Critical. G3 Formal satisfaction semantics Sat(K,r) Critical. G4 Knowledge Attribution vs general Epistemic State Critical. G5 Formal Hypothesis Space H Major. G6 Evidence Assessment/Weight semantics Major. G7 Epistemic Standards S_t Major. G8 Model+assumption provenance Major. G9 Evidence dependence/aggregation Major. G10 Kernel minimality after semantic equivalence Major.
rows.statement: Consolidates the whole remaining research problem into a ten-item severity-ranked gap register: four CRITICAL gaps (G1 canonical type of K_t, G2 non-circular semantic equivalence, G3 formal Sat(K,r), G4 Knowledge Attribution vs Epistemic State) and six MAJOR gaps (G5 formal hypothesis space, G6 evidence assessment/weight semantics, G7 epistemic standards, G8 model/assumption provenance, G9 evidence dependence/aggregation, G10 kernel minimality after semantic equivalence is solved) -- stated as the entire remaining KnowledgeOS mathematical problem, everything else being a refinement of these ten.

G5 Formal Hypothesis Space ... G6 Evidence Assessment/Weight semantics ... G7 Epistemic Standards ... G8 Model+assumption provenance ... G9 Evidence dependence/aggregation ... G10 Kernel minimality after semantic equivalence.
rows.statement: Restates (identical to S2375) the same ten-item severity-ranked gap register G1-G10 (four critical: canonical type of K_t, non-circular semantic equivalence, formal Sat(K,r), Knowledge Attribution vs Epistemic State; six major: hypothesis space, evidence assessment/weight, epistemic standards, model/assumption provenance, evidence dependence/aggregation, kernel minimality) as the complete remaining KnowledgeOS mathematical problem.

rows.anchor: An earlier lane fixed N_primary = 1,155 under **the same stated rule** ... A derived analysis lane writes its output into the primary corpus. ... The corpus was being written *during* the experiment. ... N is a moving target and must carry a timestamp.
rows.statement: Records and diagnoses a corpus-size discrepancy against an earlier lane's N_primary=1,155: two causes verified -- a derived analysis lane (three_model_convergence/, 325 files all created 2026-09-01) writes into the nominally-primary corpus and is absent from the exclusion list, and the corpus was actively mutating during the experiment (1,782 files at 22:28 vs 1,808 at 23:02) -- concluding any corpus statistic in this repository is a timestamped snapshot, not a population parameter.

rows.anchor: token files -- files containing the bare word ... role files -- files where the token is used *as an operator*: inside \boxed{...}, inside backticks, followed by (, as a typed signature Op : Kind, or as an \xrightarrow{Op} label. The role count is the honest one.
rows.statement: Defines a rigorous two-tier corpus-support measurement discipline distinguishing token files (bare word occurrence, including ordinary English usage) from role files (the token used syntactically AS an operator: inside boxed notation, backticks, applied with parentheses, as a typed signature, or as a named transition arrow), explicitly declaring the role count the honest measurement.

rows.anchor: MR-1 -- `C0` as a 13-element set has essentially no corpus provenance. ... only **six** files contain >=6 of the 13 operator tokens ... C0 is a *proposal of this lane*, not a corpus artifact.
rows.statement: States MR-1: only six corpus files contain at least 6 of the 13 C0 operator tokens, and even among those six, several are the experiment's own prompt or same-day external extracts; concludes C0 is a proposal of this research lane, not an established corpus artifact, so the experiment tests a hypothesis about the corpus rather than summarizing it.

rows.anchor: MR-2 -- The corpus operator vocabulary is *different and larger* ... nine operator families, ~50 candidate names: SD-1 Acquisition ... SD-9 Action. ... Question 15 supplies a **24-operation taxonomy with typed signatures** in eight categories.
rows.statement: States MR-2: the actual corpus operator vocabulary (from a step_286 operator-discovery pass) comprises nine named operator families (Acquisition, Discrimination/Buddhi, Construction, Revision, Uncertainty/Zero, Relationship, State transformation, Purification, Action) with roughly 50 candidate names in total, plus a separate 24-operation typed-signature taxonomy from Question 15 in eight categories -- far larger and structurally different from the tested C0 set.

rows.anchor: MR-3 -- The corpus already classifies operations into three kinds ... 𝒪+ state-changing ... 𝒪? **derived evaluations** ... 𝒪^q queries ... DetectGap is already classified corpus-side as a derived evaluation, not a state-changing operator. This is independent of, and *prior to*, the ablation result.
rows.statement: States MR-3: the corpus itself (Question 15 §4-5) already rejects one undifferentiated Operation class in favor of three (O+ state-changing: Observe/Assert/AddEvidence/ReviseValue/Reframe/Resolve; O? derived evaluations: Compare/DetectGap/DetectConflict/Evaluate; O^q queries: Query/Present), with DetectGap already classified corpus-side as a derived evaluation rather than a state-changer -- independently and PRIOR to the executed ablation experiment reaching the same conclusion, the strongest form of corroboration available.

rows.anchor: MR-4 -- `C0` omits an operator the corpus records as irreducible ... Qualify : Observation x Policy -> Evidence is carried in the prior kernel lane as G1 (irreducible) ... No operator in C0 holds the power to turn an observation into evidence. This is not a modelling artifact of this experiment; it is a hole in the candidate list.
rows.statement: States MR-4: Qualify (Observation x Policy -> Evidence) was already recorded by a prior corpus lane as G1, an irreducible gap, yet is entirely absent from C0; no C0 operator can turn an observation into evidence -- explicitly not a modelling artifact of this particular experiment but a genuine hole in the candidate operator list, whose consequence (baseline failure before any ablation) is measured elsewhere.

rows.anchor: Observe 172/66 STRONG ... Represent 52/5 WEAK, only 5 role-uses; 2 of 5 are this lane's own artifacts ... Hypothesize 3/2 WEAK, 2 role-uses, both dated 2026-09-01 or the prompt ... Select 31/3 WEAK, corpus places it in the Lord/action lane, deliberately outside the epistemic projection ... (Qualify) STRONG, recorded ... as G1 irreducible; absent from C0.
rows.statement: Presents the full per-operator evidence matrix for all 13 C0 operators plus Qualify, giving token-file count, role-file count, first operator-role occurrence, claimed corpus responsibility, a STRONG/MODERATE/WEAK support rating, and counter-evidence for each -- with Observe/Validate/Revise/Qualify rated STRONG, Interpret/Infer/DetectGap/Challenge MODERATE, and Represent/Hypothesize/Relate/Select rated WEAK.

rows.anchor: Layer 1. Protocol -- ChatGPT ... Layer 2. Execution -- Claude Code CLI ... Layer 3. Audit -- ChatGPT ... §4 below audits layer 1, which layer 2 could not audit while executing it.
rows.statement: States the formal three-layer provenance ledger for the whole kernel-reduction research episode: Layer 1 Protocol (ChatGPT-authored 2,052-line specification), Layer 2 Execution (Claude Code CLI's simulator design, all experiments, and 19 artifacts), Layer 3 Audit (ChatGPT's adjudication of whether the protocol was well-posed) -- explicitly noting the protocol (layer 1) could not be audited by the very execution (layer 2) carrying it out.

rows.anchor: A-1 the DPI claim ... too strong ... ACCEPTED, my error. A-2 "14 irreducible powers" must read as within the tested capability model ... ACCEPTED. A-4 Represent may be irreducible only because representation is provided free elsewhere ... ACCEPTED and SHARPENED. A-5 My criterion was *syntactic* irreducibility ... not *semantic* ... ACCEPTED -- the strongest single point in the audit.
rows.statement: Formally accepts seven external-audit corrections (A-1 through A-7): the DPI overclaim, the missing 'within the tested capability model' qualifier in the executive summary, the corpus-denominator discrepancy, Represent's free-elsewhere-representation concern (sharpened further), the syntactic-vs-semantic-irreducibility distinction (named the strongest single point in the whole audit), Challenge's status being functional-necessity not primitiveness, and V6 being close to definitional.

rows.anchor: D-1 ... Factually incorrect. That is the **randomized-property** table. In the **capability** table Represent ablation loses C3 and 5 of 16 scenarios ... D-2 ... **Refuted by computation** ... D-3 ... Half accepted, and the framing should be inverted ... Candidate completeness is **not decidable**; capability-closure **is**
rows.statement: Formally disputes three audit claims with specific evidence: D-1 the audit conflated the randomized-property table (where Represent showed no failures) with the separate capability table (where Represent ablation does lose C3 and 5 scenarios); D-2 the audit's Observe-ablation concern is refuted by direct computation (§3.1); D-3 the audit's 'incomplete candidate universe' framing should be inverted since candidate completeness is fundamentally undecidable while capability-closure is decidable and is what actually fired.

rows.anchor: Worlds are **not** pre-populated with observations. World is ambient; Observation is not ... Removing Observe collapses the entire downstream chain. ... P7's guard-activation rate reads exactly 0.00 for the Observe arm and 1.00 for every other arm — the guard *is* Observation in Reach
rows.statement: Computationally refutes the audit's Observe-ablation-is-label-removal concern (§3.1): worlds are not pre-populated with observations, World is ambient but Observation is not and is derivable only from (World, world-contact); removing Observe collapses the entire downstream chain, confirmed by two independent measurements (C1 lost; P7's guard-activation rate exactly 0.00 for the Observe arm vs 1.00 for every other arm, since the guard literally is Observation-in-Reach).

rows.anchor: Removing Represent leaves Hypothesis, Evidence and Claim all reachable — **structured artifacts survive**. And the carrier Representation is named by **exactly one capability, C3**. ... **Represent's irreducibility is DEFINITIONAL, not structural.** ... Represent is downgraded to **UNSUPPORTED**
rows.statement: Confirms and sharpens the audit's Represent concern (§3.2): removing Represent still leaves Hypothesis, Evidence and Claim all reachable (structured artifacts survive), and the Representation carrier is named by exactly one capability (C3, a singleton) -- concluding Represent's irreducibility is DEFINITIONAL, not structural (C3 asks for the one carrier only Represent produces, and nothing else needs it), downgrading Represent's status to UNSUPPORTED.

rows.anchor: the evidence is V0: under the *baseline* model, with Challenge removed, a Verdict is still reachable — a system that validates without ever being able to attack. V6 is the *contrast case* ... The finding is therefore about a **defect in the baseline capability model**, not about the operator
rows.statement: Clarifies V6's precise evidentiary role (§3.3): the actual evidence for Challenge's importance is V0 (baseline), where removing Challenge still leaves a Verdict reachable -- a system that validates without ever being attackable; V6 is only the contrast case showing a model where that is structurally impossible, so the finding is about a defect in the baseline capability model, not a proof that Challenge itself is primitive.

rows.anchor: P-1 (CRITICAL) -- the supplied capability list is a 1:1 restatement of the operator names ... A positional bijection, 13 for 13, in the same order. The protocol violates its own instruction ... every operator would have been irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous ... the inherited capability model was not merely "largely from the protocol", it was **isomorphic to the object under test**.
rows.statement: States P-1, the most severe protocol audit finding: the supplied capability list C1-C13 was a positional 1:1 bijection onto the 13 C0 operator names in the same order, directly violating the protocol's own explicit instruction not to derive capabilities by restating operator names; had this been honoured literally, every operator would have been irreducible by mere construction and the experiment vacuous -- every non-trivial finding exists only because the execution broke this bijection via shared atoms; the inherited capability model was isomorphic to the object under test, the deepest answer to the audit's own Q-14.

rows.anchor: P-2 (MAJOR) -- no procedure for a failing baseline ... P-3 (MAJOR) -- Part XI's simulator spec contradicts Part VII's smuggling test ... P-4 (MODERATE) -- no stopping rule for reconstruction ... P-5 (MODERATE) -- closed-world reduction and open-world discovery are mixed ... P-6 (MODERATE) -- robustness is sampled, never quantified over ... P-7 (MINOR) ... P-8 (MINOR) -- three parts are hedged into undetectability.
rows.statement: Records seven further protocol defects P-2 through P-8: no contingency procedure was specified for a failing baseline (P-2, invented during execution); the simulator specification (a function per operator) contradicts the smuggling-test requirement it must support, forcing a deliberate deviation to an atom-set algebra (P-3); no defined stopping rule for reconstruction attempts, replaced by an exhaustive fixpoint as an unrequired but stronger choice (P-4); closed-world reduction and open-world capability-discovery are conflated (P-5, the audit's own valid point); robustness is sampled across seven dimensions but the admissible-representation space itself is never characterized (P-6); confidence intervals are requested on quantities with no real sampling error (P-7); three protocol parts are hedged so loosely their omission would be invisible (P-8).

rows.anchor: CAPABILITY-CLOSURE (decidable): for every required capability c : exists o in C with a power reaching c ? This check **fired**, unprompted, and located Qualify. ... A capability-indexed model has a built-in completeness check that an operator-indexed model does not. ... An operator-list experiment would have reported 13 irreducible operators and noticed nothing.
rows.statement: Proposes capability-closure as the decidable replacement for the undecidable candidate-completeness demand: the check (for every required capability, does some operator's power reach it?) fired unprompted and located the missing Qualify, demonstrating a capability-indexed model has a built-in completeness check an operator-indexed model lacks -- an operator-list-only experiment would have reported 13 irreducible operators and noticed nothing was missing; endorses the pipeline Corpus->Capability Inventory->Semantic Normalization->Candidate Primitive Types->Minimality with capability-closure as the gate between stages 2 and 4.

rows.anchor: V8 ... a Defeater is a rival Hypothesis discriminated against a Claim; Challenge removed from the model, not absorbed ... 13 ops, 25/25, 16/16 — the reduction succeeds. V9 ... Hypothesize removed ... succeeds. V11 ... Represent becomes derivable. V12 ... every audit reduction granted at once ... 12 ops, 25/25, 16/16
rows.statement: Implements and tests four new representation variants granting the audit's own proposed reductions as models (not endorsements): V8 (Challenge removed, a Defeater modelled as a discriminated rival Hypothesis) succeeds at 13 ops/25/25/16/16; V9 (Hypothesize removed, a Hypothesis modelled as a related Representation) succeeds; V11 (Represent becomes derivable when representation is not one operator's private product) succeeds at 14 ops/25/25; V12 (all reductions granted simultaneously) succeeds at 12 ops/25/25/16/16.

rows.anchor: DetectGap is derivable in every one of the 12 representations tested — the only operator with that property. ... Qualify is the only operator whose removal ever *broke* coverage (V7). Five operators — Observe, Relate, Infer, Revise, Qualify — were never derivable in any representation tested.
rows.statement: Presents the 12-representation derivability ranking: DetectGap is derivable in 12/12 representations (the only operator with that property); Discriminate in 11/12; five operators (Observe, Relate, Infer, Revise, Qualify) are never derivable in any of the 12 representations tested, with Qualify additionally the only operator whose removal ever broke coverage entirely (under V7); Validate, Interpret, Hypothesize, Challenge, Determine, Select, Represent fall at intermediate derivability counts (1/12 to 3/12) -- noting the separation is monotone with independently-measured corpus support.

rows.anchor: Under **V12**, exhaustive search over all subsets: covering subsets = 36, minimal kernels = 4, cardinality = 8 (was 13). ... Invariant core, present in all four: {Observe, Qualify, Relate, Infer, Validate, Revise} — six operators — plus one from each of two either/or pairs: {Interpret | Represent} and {DetectGap | Determine}.
rows.statement: Reports the extended exhaustive search under V12: 36 covering subsets, exactly 4 minimal kernels, cardinality 8 (down from 13), all four sharing an invariant six-operator core {Observe, Qualify, Relate, Infer, Validate, Revise} plus one member from each of two either/or pairs ({Interpret|Represent} and {DetectGap|Determine}) -- the direct source of the 13-vs-8 finding referenced throughout the rest of this batch.

rows.anchor: The kernel is **not** 13 and **not** 8. It is **13 under the protocol's representation and 8 under the audit's**, and the difference is entirely a choice of admissible composition rules. ... the instability is in the granularity, not the count.
rows.statement: States the quantitative conclusion both the protocol and audit reached independently: the kernel is neither 13 nor 8 in any absolute sense -- it is 13 under the protocol's representation and 8 under the audit's, the entire difference being a choice of admissible composition rules, so the instability discovered is in the granularity, not the count.

rows.anchor: V0 (baseline) `Challenge` — exactly one custodian. V8 (audit's reduction of Challenge) **Hypothesize *and* Infer** — two custodians. ... Eliminating Challenge does not remove the vulnerability. It **relocates** it ... The operator count falls by one and the invariant's attack surface doubles. ... invariant custody: custody(I,K)={o in K: I fails in K\{o}}.
rows.statement: Discovers and names invariant custody as a new cost dimension (custody(I,K)={o in K: invariant I fails when o is removed}): applying it to invariant I9 (Verdict => Defeater consideration) shows removing Challenge under V8 does not eliminate the vulnerability but relocates it from one custodian (Challenge, under V0) to two (Hypothesize AND Infer, under V8) -- the operator count falls by one while the invariant's attack surface doubles, giving a concrete reason a reduction can be worse even while shrinking cardinality.

rows.anchor: Net effect of the audit: the experiment's conclusions get weaker in the middle and stronger at both ends. Four operators move to UNRESOLVED, one to UNSUPPORTED — and the two extreme findings (DetectGap derivable; Observe/Qualify/Relate/Infer/Revise never derivable) are *reinforced* by the wider search
rows.statement: Summarizes the audit's net effect on the classification: conclusions weaken in the middle (Challenge, Interpret, Hypothesize move to UNRESOLVED; Represent to UNSUPPORTED) and strengthen at both extremes (DetectGap-derivable and Observe/Qualify/Relate/Infer/Revise-never-derivable are reinforced by surviving 12 representations instead of 8).

rows.anchor: What neither party has established: That any operator is a KnowledgeOS primitive. Nothing here licenses that. That 8, 13 or 14 is the size of anything. Three numbers from three representations. That the capability model is right. ... That governance, authorization or provenance behave as modelled. All three were **assumed by the protocol and never tested**
rows.statement: Closes with an explicit joint limitations statement (what neither the protocol nor the audit established): no operator is licensed as a genuine KnowledgeOS primitive; 8/13/14 are just three numbers from three representations, not the size of anything universal; the capability model itself was isomorphic to the tested object and replacing it is the highest-value open task; governance, authorization and provenance were assumed by the protocol and never actually tested.

lexical.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.

conceptual.anchor: $$\text{invariant custody}$$ ... $$Custody(I,K)=\{o\in K: I\text{ fails when }o\text{ is removed}\}.$$ Then a reduction can have: |K'|<|K| while: |Custody(I,K')|>|Custody(I,K)|. That means: **we reduced the number of operators but increased concentration of responsibility.**

formal.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.

operational.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5

governance.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
rationale_evidence.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
rationale_evidence.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

rationale_evidence.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

rationale_evidence.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

rationale_evidence.anchor: S7 and S11–S12 are the only scenarios supplying `IdealState`. This encodes prior constraint 5 and makes property P6 (adequacy) testable rather than assumed.
rationale_evidence.statement: Only scenarios S7 and S11-S12 supply the IdealState ambient carrier, deliberately encoding the constraint that determination/gap require an Ideal State and making adequacy (property P6) an empirically testable claim rather than an assumption.

rationale_evidence.anchor: S13 is the only scenario supplying `Objective` and `ActionSet`. Action selection is therefore *structurally isolated* from epistemic determination — matching the corpus, which places the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection.
rationale_evidence.statement: Because only scenario S13 supplies Objective and ActionSet, action-selection capability is structurally isolated from epistemic determination in the scenario suite, matching the corpus's placement of the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection; if Select performed epistemic work it would appear elsewhere, and it does not.

rationale_evidence.anchor: S9 is the only scenario supplying `Rule`. Deductive inference is thereby not available for free.
rationale_evidence.statement: Restricting the Rule ambient carrier to scenario S9 alone means deductive inference is not available by default in the other 15 scenarios, forcing the experiment to distinguish entailed (deductive) content from generated/hypothesized content.

rationale_evidence.anchor: A narrative simulator ... is precisely the instrument in which semantic smuggling is invisible ... Instead the simulator is an **algebra**: operators are atom sets, carriers are derived from (inputs, atoms), and reconstruction is a fixpoint search. Smuggling then becomes a *detectable edit to the model* rather than an invisible line of code.
rationale_evidence.statement: A narrative simulator (helper functions that 'interpret'/'validate' example data) makes semantic smuggling invisible because a helper can quietly perform a removed operator's job; the kernel-reduction simulator is instead built as an algebra (operators = atom sets, carriers derived from inputs+atoms via a fixpoint search over reachability) so that smuggling becomes a detectable edit to the declared model rather than a hidden line of code.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Disable** `o` — remove it from the set. Nothing else changes. **Do NOT rewrite** the remaining operators to absorb `o`. (Enforced structurally...) **Attempt reconstruction** — the reach fixpoint *is* an exhaustive search over all valid typed compositions of the remaining operators.
rationale_evidence.statement: The ablation procedure for each operator o: disable it without rewriting remaining operators to absorb it (structurally enforced, since absorption would require changing another operator's atom set, which the reach engine cannot do mid-search); reconstruction is attempted via an exhaustive reach fixpoint over all valid typed compositions of the remaining operators, removing any 'reasonable attempts exhausted' judgment call; then run all 16 scenarios and 10 randomized properties, record the exact failed capability/failure class, and determine whether a failure is fundamental or a simulator artifact (F19/F20).

rationale_evidence.anchor: `DetectGap` sits at the intersection of both pairs — it is the only operator that appears in two synergistic pairs, and the only one holding no exclusive atom. Structurally, `DetectGap` is the *union* of two powers already owned elsewhere.
rationale_evidence.statement: DetectGap's synergistic loss in two separate pairs ({DetectGap,Determine} and {DetectGap,Discriminate}) is explained structurally: DetectGap holds no exclusive atom and is the union of two powers (difference-decision, norm-comparison) already owned by Discriminate and Determine respectively.

rationale_evidence.anchor: There must be at least one operator that produces a proposition-bearing artifact, but the system does not care which one. `Hypothesize` (non-entailed content) and `Infer` (entailed content) are *substitutable as suppliers* to the critical lane while remaining *non-substitutable in warrant kind*.
rationale_evidence.statement: The critical challenge/validate lane (C9, C10) requires at least one upstream operator producing a proposition-bearing artifact (Claim or Hypothesis); Hypothesize and Infer are substitutable AS SUPPLIERS to that lane (either one alone suffices to keep the lane alive) while remaining non-substitutable in the warrant kind they produce (non-entailed vs entailed content) — this is termed an 'operator bundle': jointly necessary as a role, individually deletable, answering protocol question Q8 affirmatively.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Formal ablation says removable (only because `DetectGap` redundantly carries its atom). DDD says keep: *Buddhi* ... is a first-class domain responsibility ... **Resolution: retain `Discriminate`, drop `DetectGap`.** All three notions then agree.
rationale_evidence.statement: Discriminate is formally derivable under leave-one-out (because DetectGap redundantly carries its atom) but is DDD-necessary as Buddhi, the first-class domain power to decide difference/contradiction/specificity/supersession/compatibility/incomparability/unknown; under variant V4 the formal result flips to irreducible, so all three notions agree once packaging is corrected: retain Discriminate, drop DetectGap as a kernel primitive (it is a derived predicate, the union of two other operators' powers, with no exclusive atom, no independent invariant, and no independent reason to change).

rationale_evidence.anchor: The evidence is consistent with `Select` being a **domain capability of a neighbouring bounded context**, not of the epistemic kernel: it consumes an `Objective` the kernel does not own, and it produces a `Decision` no epistemic capability consumes. ... **Status: `UNRESOLVED`.** ... a minimality experiment is the wrong instrument to settle it.
rationale_evidence.statement: Select is formally irreducible in 7 of 8 model variants (fails only V5) but fires in exactly one of 16 scenarios (S13, the only one supplying Objective and ActionSet) and has the weakest corpus support (3 role-uses) of any tested operator; the corpus places it in the Lord/action lane outside the epistemic projection, so the evidence is consistent with Select being a domain capability of a neighbouring bounded context rather than of the epistemic kernel — explicitly left UNRESOLVED (not deleted, not promoted) since a minimality experiment is judged the wrong instrument to settle a strategic-DDD context-boundary question.

rationale_evidence.anchor: `state-mutation` is exclusive and its removal costs C11, C15 and C24 — formally decisive. But DDD question 7 ("domain concept or implementation mechanism?") is genuinely unclear ... the corpus carries **seven** revision verbs (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire) that are *epistemically distinct* though they share the mechanism. ... **Status: `AMBIGUOUS`**
rationale_evidence.statement: Revise is formally decisive/irreducible (its exclusive state-mutation atom's removal costs capabilities C11, C15, C24) but DDD-ambiguous: it is unclear whether committing to K_t is a domain concept or an implementation mechanism, since the corpus carries seven epistemically distinct revision verbs (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire) that share one mechanism but which the current simulator cannot distinguish; status recorded AMBIGUOUS — irreducible as a power, under-modelled as a domain concept.

assumption_register.statement: K_t can be approximated for simulation purposes by ten named fields mapped onto derived carrier kinds.
assumption_register.anchor: This is NOT claimed to be the canonical KnowledgeOS state model.

sources.note: Step 282's HPA-commissioned theory-criticality and residual-gap classification gate: eight TC criteria (semantic definition, type closure, identity/equality, transformation closure, invariant preservation, mandatory distinguishability, falsifiability, internal consistency), a four-dimensional closure model (Formal/Computational/Empirical/Governance, explicitly FC!=CC!=EC!=GC), a required stopping decision among three outcomes (A theory remains open, B theoretically closed at declared scope, C fully closed), and an executed falsification suite F14-F21 (theory-criticality removal test, non-identifiability, policy/knowledge separation, Qt replay, Qt serialization, dependency-cycle, closure-category, probability necessity). Final verdict reached: Outcome B.

rows.anchor: C = (C_F,C_C,C_E,C_G,C_D,C_H)
rows.statement: Defines a six-dimensional closure vector C=(C_F,C_C,C_E,C_G,C_D,C_H) for Formal, Computational, Empirical, Governance, DDD/Architectural, and Historical/Traceability closure respectively, each given a precise informal definition (e.g. Empirical closure means the theory's claims have been tested against the actual KnowledgeOS/EKP environment and agree within declared acceptance criteria), with the mandatory chain: Executable reference implementation != Real KnowledgeOS implementation != Empirical validation.

rows.anchor: Level 0 — Conceptual ... Level 6 — Operationally validated
rows.statement: Defines an explicit seven-level evidence hierarchy (L0 Conceptual, L1 Corpus-supported, L2 Formally specified, L3 Reference-implemented, L4 Reproducibly executed, L5 Real-environment empirical, L6 Operationally validated) and states as a hard rule that Level 4 != Level 5 and Level 5 != Level 6, so no Level-4 result may be represented as Level-5 empirical closure.

rows.anchor: C_E = NOT\ ACHIEVED
rows.statement: Empirical closure C_E is explicitly ruled NOT ACHIEVED because 15/24 constructs lack real-environment observation, the missingness repair has only Level-4 validation, some policy/authority behavior remains unobserved, measurement execution is incomplete, and real operational propagation is undemonstrated; this is called 'a hard decision.'

rows.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY — FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED ... EMPIRICAL CLOSURE PENDING ... GOVERNANCE RATIFICATION PENDING
rows.statement: HPA Decision (this draft): KnowledgeOS shall not be declared fully complete at Step 282; official state is 'FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED' with 'EMPIRICAL CLOSURE PENDING' and 'GOVERNANCE RATIFICATION PENDING'; recommends the sequence Step 283 Governance Ratification -> Step 284 Final Empirical Conformance -> Step 285 Canonical Theory Freeze -> Step 286 Book/Architecture Publication Gate.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 281 successfully repaired the identified missingness defect and demonstrated internal closure.

rows.anchor: A = REJECTED ... C2 = NOT\ REQUIRED ... Q_t\subseteq P ... is selected.
rows.statement: Restates and ratifies the Step 281 candidate outcome at governance level: Candidate A (bottom assertion) REJECTED; Candidate C2 (typed Sigma*=IxE) NOT REQUIRED (if governance later chooses C2 for implementation reasons this must be an explicit documented design decision, not a mathematical consequence); Candidate B (Q_t subset of P) SELECTED, subject to the obligation that Q_t become replayable and serializable in a real implementation.

rows.anchor: \text{Uncertainty} \neq \text{Probability} ... \text{Unknown} \neq \text{Random Variable}
rows.statement: Argues that the mere existence of uncertainty, incomplete information, unknown values, competing evidence, and non-identifiability does not logically imply a probability structure; probability is required only if KnowledgeOS makes claims of the form P(X in A)=p or uses probabilistic inference, Bayesian updating, or stochastic transition semantics, none of which the canonical state-transition model K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) or any of Unknown/Missing/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted/Superseded/provenance/lineage/replay requires.

rows.anchor: \boxed{\text{T-3 = NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY}}
rows.statement: Rules T-3 (probability space requirement) NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY, closed at core-theory level; states it must not be reopened merely because KnowledgeOS represents uncertainty, and that probability remains an optional measurement/statistical extension a future bounded context may explicitly supply.

rows.anchor: \text{Unknown} \not\equiv \text{Non-identifiable}
rows.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (the system currently lacks a justified value) from Non-identifiable (available observation/evidence cannot uniquely determine the value even in principle under the specified model, formally f(theta1)=f(theta2) with theta1!=theta2); rules T-4 NOT A CORE-THEORY BLOCKER because the core does not require latent-parameter inference, but the distinction Unknown != Missing != NonIdentifiable must be preserved once any inference context is introduced.

rows.anchor: Policy \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow \Sigma ... does not imply ... \Sigma \rightarrow Policy
rows.statement: Resolves the I-2 circular-dependency warning (Policy -> Assessment -> Sigma and Sigma -> Validation -> Policy) by separating semantic/ontological dependency from operational dependency: the canonical semantic graph is Evidence -> Assessment (parameterized by Policy) -> Sigma -> K, and Validation may READ Sigma/Policy without Sigma constructing the Policy against which it is evaluated; classifies I-2 as an implementation/dependency-graph artifact provided the implementation respects the dependency direction, with three explicit resolution criteria.

rows.anchor: Q_t = \pi_Q(Replay(K_0,H_t))
rows.statement: Formalizes Q_t as an event-derived projection of History rather than an independently authoritative state component: Q_t = pi_Q(Replay(K_0,H_t)), equivalently p in Q_t iff there exists e in H_t with e=Ask(p); requires the replay invariant H_t=H'_t => Q_t=Q'_t, and a canonical serialized InquiryEvent schema (proposition_id, inquiry_timestamp, actor/context, event_id, schema_version) satisfying Deserialize(Serialize(e))=e. Concludes Q_t is not a new component of minimal K or Sigma, is replayable and serializable, and is not independently authoritative -- the remaining obligation is engineering closure, not theory redesign.

rows.anchor: G0 — Exact correspondence ... G4 — Theory underspecified
rows.statement: Defines a five-category Theory-Implementation Gap Protocol Delta(T,I) for classifying any construct's correspondence between theory and implementation: G0 exact correspondence, G1 implemented but untested, G2 implemented differently (behavior diverges from spec), G3 not implemented, G4 theory underspecified (implementation exposes a missing theoretical definition). States G0/G1/G3 do not imply a theory defect, G2 may indicate either a theory or implementation defect, and G4 is the only category that automatically reopens theoretical work.

rows.anchor: \textbf{THEORY PROVISIONALLY CLOSED — EMPIRICAL CERTIFICATION PENDING}
rows.statement: Revises the overall Step 282 verdict from the first draft's 'FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED' wording to the more precise 'THEORY PROVISIONALLY CLOSED — EMPIRICAL CERTIFICATION PENDING,' meaning no currently identified core theoretical blocker remains but the theory has not been empirically validated against the complete KnowledgeOS/EKP environment; three possible outcomes (A still incomplete, B provisionally closed, C fully closed) are given with B as the currently supported one, conditional on completing residual formal checks (T-3, T-4, I-2, Q_t).

rows.anchor: We should stop asking: "Is KnowledgeOS theory complete?" as one binary question. Instead ask: "Is there any remaining unresolved construct that is necessary for the definition, semantics, transformation, identity, or invariants of the theory?"
rows.statement: Reframes the entire Step 282 question from a binary completeness question into a load-bearing-dependency question: whether any remaining unresolved construct is necessary for the theory's definition, semantics, transformation, identity, or invariants; if no, the theory has reached a 'theoretical stopping point' independent of whether the real EKP implements or observes everything.

rows.anchor: I would **not yet accept this wording**: > **KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY — FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED**
rows.statement: Rejects the original Step 282 draft's claim that Formal Closure is 'ACHIEVED/SUBSTANTIAL' while simultaneously leaving T-4 OPEN and T-3 BLOCKED, arguing this is potentially too strong and that Step 282 must first prove T-3 and T-4 are actually theory-critical via a dependency-based closure argument rather than merely presenting a status table.

rows.anchor: A — Theory still open ... B — Theory internally closed ... C — Fully closed
rows.statement: Defines the three legitimate stopping-decision outcomes for Step 282: A (a genuine theory-critical construct remains unresolved -> continue theory work), B (no theory-critical defect remains but empirical/governance evidence is incomplete -> stop theory invention, move to validation/ratification), C (formal, computational, empirical and governance all satisfied -> canonical freeze); states current evidence strongly suggests B but Step 282 must demonstrate it, not assume it.

rows.anchor: **Do not synchronize this into the book yet.**
rows.statement: Explicit governance instruction that the book/publication track must not consume this intermediate Step 282 interpretation; it must wait for the final Step 282 result, since the book already distinguishes theoretical validity, implementation completeness, empirical certification and governance ratification.

rows.anchor: 200+ archaeology steps ↓ 53 gaps ↓ 13 critical gaps ↓ must invent more theory ... The later verification progressively falsified that interpretation.
rows.statement: Retrospective narrative of the programme's own history: from '200+ archaeology steps' to '53 gaps' to '13 critical gaps' the original interpretation assumed more theory must be invented, but later independent verification progressively falsified that interpretation as many apparent gaps turned out to be transcription/category errors, with O, authority, and Determination recovered and Sigma reduced to minimal structure and missingness repaired with Q_t.

rows.anchor: Step 282 is COMMISSIONED in its corrected form.
rows.statement: Formal HPA ruling: Step 282 is commissioned in its corrected form as a theory-criticality and residual-gap classification gate (not a completion declaration), with the corrected outcome expected to be 'B — THEORY THEORETICALLY CLOSED AT THE DECLARED SCOPE' but requiring Step 282 to demonstrate rather than assume this, and an explicit instruction not to synchronize into the book yet.

lineage_claims.quote: identical Executive Summary through Part 5 content

rows.anchor: TC-1 — Semantic definition ... TC-8 — Internal consistency
rows.statement: Defines eight theory-criticality (TC) criteria used to test whether a residual gap is genuinely load-bearing: TC-1 semantic definition, TC-2 type closure, TC-3 identity/equality, TC-4 transformation closure, TC-5 invariant preservation, TC-6 mandatory distinguishability, TC-7 falsifiability, TC-8 internal consistency; a gap is theory-critical only if it fails at least one.

rows.anchor: Do **not** invent new theory unless an actual theory-critical failure is demonstrated. Do **not** declare closure because most constructs are already defined. Do **not** keep the theory open merely because implementation, empirical validation, or governance is incomplete.
rows.statement: States the governing methodological sequence for Step 282 execution (Identify -> Classify -> Test -> Falsify -> Close or Escalate) with three explicit anti-bias prohibitions: do not invent new theory absent a demonstrated theory-critical failure; do not declare closure merely because most constructs are defined; do not keep the theory open merely because implementation/empirical/governance work is incomplete.

rows.anchor: Never present `[I]` as `[E]`. Never present `[E]` as `[R]`. Never present `[N]` as mathematical necessity.
rows.statement: Mandates an evidence-provenance labeling scheme for every conclusion ([D] Derived, [F] Formal, [E] Executed, [R] Real-environment, [N] Normative, [I] Inferred, [U] Unresolved) with an explicit prohibition on upgrading a weaker evidence label to a stronger one (inferred presented as executed, executed presented as real-environment, normative presented as mathematically necessary).

rows.anchor: F14 — Theory-criticality test ... F21 — Probability necessity test
rows.statement: Specifies seven mandatory falsification tests: F14 theory-criticality (does removing a proposed resolution break a mandatory operation), F15 non-identifiability (can distinct states be observationally equivalent), F16 policy/knowledge separation, F17 inquiry replay, F18 inquiry serialization identity, F19 dependency-cycle test, F20 closure-category test (can an empirical failure be miscategorized as formal), F21 probability necessity test.

rows.anchor: 01-THEORY-CRITICALITY-REGISTER.md ... 12-STEP-282-SUPERVISORY-VERDICT.md
rows.statement: Mandates twelve required output artifacts in a fixed order (01-THEORY-CRITICALITY-REGISTER through 12-STEP-282-SUPERVISORY-VERDICT), and requires the master gap register be updated if the repository contains one, with an explicit prohibition on creating duplicate competing gap registers without stating which is authoritative.

rows.anchor: T-4 should be logged as a deferred extension with a named carrier, not as closed.
rows.statement: Statistician's-lens caution against closing T-4 (non-identifiability): preserving a distinction the theory cannot express is not the same as closing it; under Repair B, a structurally-caused (0,0) Sigma value is indistinguishable from Asked+Absent caused by a merely-unlucky search, which is precisely the non-identifiability case, so T-4 should be logged as a deferred extension with a named carrier rather than declared closed.

rows.anchor: Omega              appears in 271 files ... NOTE: appearance of a SYMBOL is not construction of a SPACE. Checked below.
rows.statement: A corpus-wide symbol scan across 1897 files finds probability-related symbols/words appearing frequently (Omega 271 files, triple notation 69, estimator 46, estimand 43, random variable 42, sigma-algebra 38 files) but explicitly cautions that symbol appearance in prose is not evidence of an actually constructed probability space, motivating the subsequent construct-removal test as the real check.

“Closed” does not mean “immune to revision.”
rows.statement: Decision D-282-4: no further foundational theory-building work is authorized unless new empirical or implementation evidence falsifies a currently-closed construct; 'closed' is explicitly defined as not meaning 'immune to revision' but rather that no unresolved theory-critical defect currently justifies continued foundational reconstruction, and a future falsification may reopen the theory.

Explicit constraint on the downstream book-synchronization stream: the book must consume the actual Step-282 closure result including its negative findings (empirical non-closure, governance non-closure, computational limitations, historical evolution, falsification results) and must NOT rewrite EC (empirical closure) or GC (governance closure) as though they were TRUE/closed.

governance.anchor: C_E = NOT\ ACHIEVED

rationale_evidence.anchor: C_E = NOT\ ACHIEVED
rationale_evidence.statement: Empirical closure C_E is explicitly ruled NOT ACHIEVED because 15/24 constructs lack real-environment observation, the missingness repair has only Level-4 validation, some policy/authority behavior remains unobserved, measurement execution is incomplete, and real operational propagation is undemonstrated; this is called 'a hard decision.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: \text{Uncertainty} \neq \text{Probability} ... \text{Unknown} \neq \text{Random Variable}
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues that the mere existence of uncertainty, incomplete information, unknown values, competing evidence, and non-identifiability does not logically imply a probability structure; probability is required only if KnowledgeOS makes claims of the form P(X in A)=p or uses probabilistic inference, Bayesian updating, or stochastic transition semantics, none of which the canonical state-transition model K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) or any of Unknown/Missing/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted/Superseded/provenance/lineage/replay requires.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \boxed{\text{T-3 = NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY}}
rationale_evidence.statement: Rules T-3 (probability space requirement) NOT REQUIRED FOR THE CORE THEORY, closed at core-theory level; states it must not be reopened merely because KnowledgeOS represents uncertainty, and that probability remains an optional measurement/statistical extension a future bounded context may explicitly supply.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \text{Unknown} \not\equiv \text{Non-identifiable}
rationale_evidence.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (the system currently lacks a justified value) from Non-identifiable (available observation/evidence cannot uniquely determine the value even in principle under the specified model, formally f(theta1)=f(theta2) with theta1!=theta2); rules T-4 NOT A CORE-THEORY BLOCKER because the core does not require latent-parameter inference, but the distinction Unknown != Missing != NonIdentifiable must be preserved once any inference context is introduced.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Policy \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow \Sigma ... does not imply ... \Sigma \rightarrow Policy
rationale_evidence.statement: Resolves the I-2 circular-dependency warning (Policy -> Assessment -> Sigma and Sigma -> Validation -> Policy) by separating semantic/ontological dependency from operational dependency: the canonical semantic graph is Evidence -> Assessment (parameterized by Policy) -> Sigma -> K, and Validation may READ Sigma/Policy without Sigma constructing the Policy against which it is evaluated; classifies I-2 as an implementation/dependency-graph artifact provided the implementation respects the dependency direction, with three explicit resolution criteria.

rationale_evidence.anchor: I would **not yet accept this wording**: > **KNOWLEDGEOS THEORY — FORMALLY SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED**
rationale_evidence.statement: Rejects the original Step 282 draft's claim that Formal Closure is 'ACHIEVED/SUBSTANTIAL' while simultaneously leaving T-4 OPEN and T-3 BLOCKED, arguing this is potentially too strong and that Step 282 must first prove T-3 and T-4 are actually theory-critical via a dependency-based closure argument rather than merely presenting a status table.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 200+ archaeology steps ↓ 53 gaps ↓ 13 critical gaps ↓ must invent more theory ... The later verification progressively falsified that interpretation.
rationale_evidence.statement: Retrospective narrative of the programme's own history: from '200+ archaeology steps' to '53 gaps' to '13 critical gaps' the original interpretation assumed more theory must be invented, but later independent verification progressively falsified that interpretation as many apparent gaps turned out to be transcription/category errors, with O, authority, and Determination recovered and Sigma reduced to minimal structure and missingness repaired with Q_t.

rationale_evidence.anchor: T-4 should be logged as a deferred extension with a named carrier, not as closed.
rationale_evidence.statement: Statistician's-lens caution against closing T-4 (non-identifiability): preserving a distinction the theory cannot express is not the same as closing it; under Repair B, a structurally-caused (0,0) Sigma value is indistinguishable from Asked+Absent caused by a merely-unlucky search, which is precisely the non-identifiability case, so T-4 should be logged as a deferred extension with a named carrier rather than declared closed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Omega              appears in 271 files ... NOTE: appearance of a SYMBOL is not construction of a SPACE. Checked below.
rationale_evidence.statement: A corpus-wide symbol scan across 1897 files finds probability-related symbols/words appearing frequently (Omega 271 files, triple notation 69, estimator 46, estimand 43, random variable 42, sigma-algebra 38 files) but explicitly cautions that symbol appearance in prose is not evidence of an actually constructed probability space, motivating the subsequent construct-removal test as the real check.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution' (step 246) *** THE ONLY ONE. And it constructs no space. ***
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies Step 246's claim 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution' as the sole corpus claim that would require probability, and states explicitly that step constructs no actual probability space (no Omega, sigma-algebra, or measure), so the claim remains an unsupported SOURCE CLAIM rather than a load-bearing theoretical dependency.

rationale_evidence.anchor: > **A red empirical cell is not a red theoretical cell.** Fifteen constructs are unobservable **because\n> the EKP does not implement them**, not because the theory cannot define them. Every one of those\n> fifteen passes TC-1 through TC-8.
rationale_evidence.statement: Empirical non-observability of a construct in the running EKP is attributed to the EKP's lack of implementation of that construct, not to any inability of the theory to define it; all 15 unobservable constructs are asserted to pass the eight theory-criticality (TC-1..TC-8) tests.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
> # **VERDICT B — THEORY THEORETICALLY CLOSED AT DECLARED SCOPE**

> **The KnowledgeOS theory is formally closed at its declared scope, but system implementation, empirical
> validation, measurement execution, and governance ratification remain incomplete.**
rationale_evidence.statement: Final Step-282 verdict: VERDICT B, theory theoretically closed at declared scope; FC=TRUE, CC=mostly true (3 open: Authorize() runtime, measurement executor, C-NEW harness fix), EC=FALSE, GC=NOT CLAIMED; Verdict A (theory still open) is rejected because every candidate theory-critical defect was tested and none survived (T-3 fails necessity 0/13, T-4 derivable, I-2 has 0 cycles, Q_t passes 10/10); Verdict C (fully closed) is not claimed because C/E/G gaps remain and per an internal rule (§22) implementation/empirical/governance incompleteness must not by itself keep the theory open, but likewise cannot justify claiming full closure.

rationale_evidence.anchor: > ## **THEORY-CRITICAL GAPS REMAINING: ZERO.**\n> Every `F`-classified gap is closed. Every remaining gap is `C`, `E`, `M`, `G` or `N` — none of which\n> blocks the definition, typing, identity, transformation, invariants or falsifiability of the theory.
rationale_evidence.statement: Aggregate conclusion: zero theory-critical gaps remain in the KnowledgeOS theory register as of Step 282; all three F-classified (Formal) gaps are closed, and every remaining gap (classified C, E, M, G, or N) is argued not to block definition, typing, identity, transformation, invariants, or falsifiability.

assumption_register.statement: Five dependency kinds (definitional, operational, runtime, governance, reference) must be kept analytically separate when testing for cycles.
assumption_register.anchor: ## The five dependency kinds, kept apart

assumption_register.statement: Q_t is a projection of History, so no information is lost from the overall system regardless of which unask design is chosen.
