sources.note: The fully worked-out KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09 research artifact (status [PROP][OPEN], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched): a metro-encounter case study formalized as a four-layer execution loop (front-end interaction, gap detection/classification, epistemic agency selection, determination/output), hypotheses EA1-EA7 plus later EA8-EA11, and an expected-utility sub-specification EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t,R_t). Extends the candidate 'next-epistemic-act-function-and-gap-classification' object (S2833) into a full formal specification with a worked six-step human trace and a senior-review critique correcting K|=Q notation, gap taxonomy exhaustiveness, EA7's universality, and the Lord/Sarathi naming.

rows.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
rows.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

lineage_claims.quote: By mapping this human interaction to formal epistemic state transitions, you have isolated the missing bridge ... Epistemic Agency.

rows.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
rows.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

rows.anchor: Delta_t in {Semantic, Epistemic, Resource, Policy} ... I would not call these the four gap types yet ... ClassifyGap: Delta_Q -> G where G is itself still research-open.
rows.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).
missing: a closed/validated gap taxonomy G

rows.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
rows.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

rows.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
rows.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.
missing: experimentally determined decision criterion

rows.anchor: Resource_t(r) = (Avail,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...) ... Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) becomes meaningful.
rows.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

rows.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
rows.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

rows.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
rows.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

rows.anchor: Determine(Evidence) BEFORE Act. ... I would not make this universal. ... Required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination.
rows.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

rows.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
rows.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

rows.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
rows.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

rows.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
rows.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.
invariants: Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence
Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge
Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability

experiment.hypothesis: Selected epistemic action changes appropriately as resources/standards/risk/inquiry vary, and observation equivalence does not force intent equivalence
experiment.setup: Fixed K_t,Q,Delta with varied resource-availability cases A-D and standard/risk/inquiry cases E-G; four-world adversarial scenario sharing identical O_1
experiment.assumptions: Action selection depends on K,Q,Delta,R,C,EC,S,R
experiment.inputs: Synthetic metro-style scenarios
experiment.method: Controlled factorial variation plus adversarial world construction
experiment.limitations: Not yet executed
experiment.conclusion: Proposed as the next controlled experiment before large-scale testing

rows.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
rows.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.
missing: validated functional form F

rows.anchor: ||Delta_Q(K_t)||_G ... This is currently underdefined ... These don't naturally form a vector space. ... U_gap(a) = V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a; Q,C,EC,S) where V is a candidate gap-value/reduction function.
rows.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.
missing: experimentally validated numerical gap structure

rows.anchor: Reduction != Validation != Determination != Knowledge ... U_gap must not silently become KnowledgeGain. I recommend the term Expected Gap Resolution Value rather than Expected Epistemic Value
rows.statement: Argues raw gap-cardinality reduction (|Delta_{t+1}|<|Delta_t|) does not imply epistemic improvement, via a worked example (3 hypotheses reduced to 1 surviving hypothesis that is false), extending Reduction!=Validation!=Determination!=Knowledge; recommends renaming 'Expected Epistemic Value' to 'Expected Gap Resolution Value' to prevent gap reduction being silently equated with knowledge gain.

rows.anchor: rho(a) * E[DeltaRed] ... This risks double counting ... E[U(a)] = sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M) U(a,o) where reliability belongs in the observation/evidence model
rows.statement: Corrects the draft's reliability multiplier rho(a)*E[DeltaRed] as risking double-counting reliability (since it may already shape the observation distribution P(O|a,K)); recommends the cleaner E[U(a)]=sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M)U(a,o), moving resource reliability into the observation/evidence model P(O|a,R_t,...) instead.

rows.anchor: Constraint != Preference. ... PrivacyViolation(a)=1 may mean a not-in A^feasible rather than EU(a)-1000. ... A^safe = {a: P(harm|a) <= epsilon} and only then a* = argmax_{a in A^safe} EU(a).
rows.statement: Corrects the draft's treatment of safety/risk as a soft utility penalty (Omega_risk subtracted, beta(R_t) scaling) to a hard feasibility constraint where appropriate: Constraint != Preference, e.g. a privacy violation should remove an action from A^feasible rather than merely penalize its utility, giving A^safe={a: P(harm|a)<=epsilon} filtered before a*=argmax_{a in A^safe}EU(a); likewise the draft's 'high-precision mode' weight adjustment is reframed as a hard safety constraint rather than a mere utility-weight change.

rows.anchor: EU(a1) approx EU(a2) does not mean a1 equiv_sem a2. So I would call it: candidate deterministic tie-break policy not: selection invariant.
rows.statement: Corrects the draft's tie-breaking rule (favor lower latency when utilities are approximately equal) from a 'selection invariant' to a 'candidate deterministic tie-break policy', noting approximately-equal expected utility does not imply semantic equivalence of the two actions, and that the tie-break policy should itself be configurable under the active decision regime.

rows.anchor: Stop or NoFurtherInvestigation ... Suppose Adeq(K_t,Q,...) = True. Continuing to investigate can have negative utility. ... This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.
rows.statement: Adds a Stop/NoFurtherInvestigation candidate action to the action set A^possible, so that once Adeq(K_t,Q,...)=True continuing investigation can legitimately have negative utility and EU(Stop) can win, preventing KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.

rows.anchor: Agreement(Selection,Validation) not-implies Truth. ... ActionDecisionRecord_t containing at minimum: Inquiry, Current Knowledge State, Typed Gap, Candidate Actions, Resource States, Feasibility Results, Utility Model, Utility Parameters, Risk Policy, Selected Action, Rejected Alternatives, Decision Reason, Authorization.
rows.statement: Proposes a counterfactual-action-quality experiment (estimate P(Adeq(K_{t+1}^a,Q)=1 | K_t,Q,R_t) for every candidate action and compare to the selected action, using a candidate Regret(a)=U(a*)-U(a) or outcome proxies) and an adversarial reliability test giving Agreement(Selection,Validation) does not imply Truth; requires an ActionDecisionRecord_t (inquiry, state, typed gap, candidates, resource states, feasibility, utility model/parameters, risk policy, selected action, rejected alternatives, decision reason, authorization) for inspectability.

experiment.hypothesis: The utility-selected action produces better epistemic outcomes than alternatives, and the system can distinguish independent evidence from merely historically-reliable-but-currently-wrong evidence
experiment.setup: Two candidate resources: one historically reliable but wrong today, one less reliable but independent
experiment.assumptions: Outcome measures (determination probability, answerability, evidence quality, cost, risk, time) available as proxies if utility isn't trusted yet
experiment.inputs: Synthetic adversarial resource scenarios
experiment.method: Compare selected action's counterfactual outcome quality against alternatives; regret computation
experiment.limitations: Not yet executed
experiment.conclusion: Proposed as a stronger validation than merely confirming the formula outputs a number

rows.anchor: NextEpistemicAct = Generate + Feasible + Evaluate + Select + Policy. If that composition is semantically equivalent to the proposed agency operator ... then no kernel expansion. ... Epistemic Value != Task Utility != Operational Utility.
rows.statement: Reframes the kernel test as whether NextEpistemicAct is semantically equivalent to a composition Generate+Feasible+Evaluate+Select+Policy of existing capabilities (if so, no kernel expansion), states Selection Capability != Expected Utility Formula and Gap Reduction != Knowledge Gain as governing distinctions, and adds Epistemic Value != Task Utility != Operational Utility (e.g. asking for a destination may have low task utility but high epistemic value by making the inquiry well-formed).
invariants: Epistemic Value != Task Utility != Operational Utility

rows.anchor: Contract-Relative Adequacy (Replacing K_t |= Q) ... If inadequate, an operational gap is instantiated: Delta_Q(K_t) = typed collection of unsatisfied requirements.
rows.statement: Publishes KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09 v0.2 replacing K_t|=Q with contract-relative Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R), a three-phase decoupled pipeline (Phase 1 Inquiry Formation with a branch for underspecified vs well-formed inquiries; Phase 2 Epistemic Agency & Selection: gap classification -> candidate generation -> feasibility filtering -> decision/selection -> authorization gate; Phase 3 Execution & Determination), and a factorial-labeled resource experiment EXP-AGENCY-RESOURCE-2026-09 with cases A-E over resource availability.

lineage_claims.quote: By applying all 19 corrections, we stabilize the research proposal

rows.anchor: You now have both Pi -- preservation/epistemic contract, R_t -- risk policy, earlier theory also uses R_t for reasoning regime. That is a serious notation collision. ... do not use R_t for risk. I recommend Risk_t and retain R_t = Reasoning Regime.
rows.statement: Identifies a serious notation collision: R_t is used both for 'risk policy' in the new draft and previously for 'reasoning regime'; corrects by renaming risk to Risk_t and reserving R_t for reasoning regime.

rows.anchor: Cases A-E are not a factorial design. ... This is a resource-ablation / constrained intervention design, not a factorial experiment. ... EXP-AGENCY-RESOURCE-2026-09 -- Resource Ablation and Epistemic Action Selection.
rows.statement: Corrects the mislabeled 'FACTORIAL EXPERIMENT' EXP-AGENCY-RESOURCE-2026-09 (cases A-E vary resource combinations non-orthogonally) to its correct design type, a resource-ablation/constrained-intervention design, distinct from a true crossed-factor factorial design.

rows.anchor: the experiment does NOT yet test irreducibility ... EA equiv_sem Composition(Generate,Feasible,Evaluate,Select) ... Agreement of selected action is not sufficient for semantic equivalence.
rows.statement: Corrects the proposed irreducibility test: observing that a*=f(resources,...) across cases A-E only shows the selected action depends on resources, it does NOT show NextEpistemicAct is derivable from existing capabilities; the decisive test requires the capability-simulation relation K1<=_cap K2 applied both ways (EA<=_cap Composition and Composition<=_cap EA) to establish EA equiv_sem Composition(Generate,Feasible,Evaluate,Select); agreement of selected action alone is not sufficient for semantic equivalence since two systems can choose the same action with different internal epistemic semantics.
missing: executed capability-simulation test in both directions
invariants: Agreement of selected action is not sufficient for semantic equivalence

experiment.hypothesis: NextEpistemicAct is semantically equivalent to a composition of Generate+Feasible+Evaluate+Select
experiment.setup: Model A: explicit EA(K,Q,Delta,R,...)->a operator; Model B: Generate->Feasible->Evaluate->Select->a composition
experiment.assumptions: Existing capability-simulation relation <=_cap is well-defined and observable-trace-preserving
experiment.inputs: Resource ablation cases A-E plus additional policy/inquiry interventions
experiment.method: Test EA<=_cap Composition and Composition<=_cap EA bidirectionally
experiment.limitations: Not yet executed; original design only observed differing selected actions, not full trace equivalence
experiment.conclusion: Design valid but not yet decisive for irreducibility; recommend a second-stage composition/semantic-equivalence experiment

rows.anchor: mu_t = Freshness Rate ... This is not really freshness. A source can update every second and still contain stale information. ... UpdateRate != Freshness.
rows.statement: Corrects the resource-state 8-tuple's mu_t ('Freshness Rate' defined as update frequency) as conflating UpdateRate with actual Freshness/Age (Age_t(r)=t-t_lastUpdate); recommends separating f_t=UpdateRate from phi_t=Freshness/Age, since high-frequency information need not be epistemically fresh or reliable.

rows.anchor: rho_t in [0,1] ... bounded historical trust/precision metric ... combines several things ... Reliability_t(r,Q,C) rather than simply rho_t(r).
rows.statement: Corrects the resource tuple's single scalar rho_t ('trust/precision') which conflates historical accuracy, source reliability, precision, calibration, current validity, and relevance to Q; recommends a context-dependent Reliability_t(r,Q,C), and separately preserves Provenance != Reliability != Truth (a signed source can be reliably wrong; an unsigned direct observation can be right).

type_signature.domain: resource r, inquiry Q, context C

rows.anchor: Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient ... This should become a candidate invariant.
rows.statement: Proposes the candidate invariant Available(r)=1 != Feasible(a)=1 != ExpectedBenefit(a)>0 (Useful) != Adeq(K',Q,...)=1 (Sufficient), illustrated by 'Google Maps is available' not implying it can answer the particular question, and being able to answer not implying it is the best action.

rows.anchor: NoFeasibleAct => NoFabricatedDetermination. ... This is precisely the anti-fabrication behaviour we want.
rows.statement: Treats the fallback case A_t^feasible=empty (report incapability/defer) as a genuine epistemic outcome rather than an error state, proposing the candidate invariant NoFeasibleAct => NoFabricatedDetermination.

rows.anchor: Add NoOp/Wait ... Sometimes waiting for fresh evidence is better than searching ... Without NoOp, the system is forced to do something. That creates an artificial action bias.
rows.statement: Adds NoOp/Wait to the candidate action set, since ExpectedValue(Wait) can exceed ExpectedValue(Search) and omitting it creates an artificial action bias forcing the system to always do something.

rows.anchor: Determination -> Action is a policy-dependent ordering, not a universal epistemic law. ... an agent can need to act under uncertainty.
rows.statement: Further corrects EA7: even in v0.2, Determination->Action should not be a universal principal loop; a parallel path (Inquiry->Gap->Risk assessment->Immediate protective action->Evidence->Determination) exists for acting under uncertainty, confirming Determination->Action is policy-dependent, not a universal epistemic law.

rows.anchor: K_t not-implies Answer ... K_t,Q_t -> Gap_t -> Candidate Epistemic Acts -> Feasible Acts -> Selection -> Evidence -> Determination -> K_{t+1} ... Can KnowledgeOS select the next justified epistemic transition without confusing availability, evidence, determination, policy, and action?
rows.statement: States the sharpened research question emerging from the metro/epistemic-agency thread: not 'can KnowledgeOS store knowledge' but 'can KnowledgeOS select the next justified epistemic transition without confusing availability, evidence, determination, policy, and action', formalized as K_t,Q_t -> Gap_t -> Candidate Epistemic Acts -> Feasible Acts -> Selection -> Evidence -> Determination -> K_{t+1}, with K_t not-implies Answer as the governing non-triviality condition.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
rows.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

rows.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).
missing: validated measurability of Adeq and comparability of candidate dimensions

assumptions.statement: Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions have comparable expected value, costs are scalarizable, argmax exists
assumptions.anchor: But it assumes: Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions have comparable expected value, costs are scalarizable, an argmax exists.

rows.anchor: NoAction != NoDecision ... Inaction is itself a candidate action-state. ... A_t = {a_1,...,a_n, NoOp, Wait, InvestigateFurther}.
rows.statement: Extracts from Chapter 3's rejection of mere abstention (doing nothing is not automatically a valid alternative) the structural distinction NoAction != NoDecision, with inaction as itself a candidate action-state that must appear explicitly in the action set A_t={a1,...,an,NoOp,Wait,InvestigateFurther}, reinforcing the earlier Expected-Utility-derived NoOp/Wait addition.

lineage_claims.target: the Expected Utility sub-spec's NoOp/Stop addition (S2836/S2837)
lineage_claims.quote: This was already emerging from our Expected Utility work.

rows.anchor: Action Evaluation != Individual Utility Only ... ImmediateEffect and SystemicEffect ... EU(a|K,Q,C,S,R) could eventually need to distinguish U_local(a) from U_system(a). But do not add this to Theory v1.2 yet. It is a research hypothesis.
rows.statement: Extracts from Chapter 3's example-setting/systemic-consequence argument the candidate distinction Action Evaluation != Individual Utility Only, suggesting the existing expected-utility operator EU(a|K,Q,C,S,R) may eventually need to distinguish U_local(a) from U_system(a), explicitly flagged as an unadopted research hypothesis, not a Theory v1.2 addition.
missing: formal U_local/U_system decomposition, evidence it is needed

rows.anchor: Determine(H) not-implies Select(Action) and conversely Select(Action) not-implies Determine(H). ... the cause is determined but several actions are viable; the cause is underdetermined but an action is still necessary; no cause is uniquely determined but Wait, Investigate, or a safe mitigation is justified.
rows.statement: Proposes the paired candidate invariants Determine(H) does not imply Select(Action) and Select(Action) does not imply Determine(H), illustrated by three cases (cause determined but several actions viable; cause underdetermined but action still necessary; no unique cause determined but Wait/Investigate/safe-mitigation justified), giving the architecture FactFinding -> Determination -> ActionEvaluation -> ActionSelection rather than FactFinding -> Action directly.

rows.anchor: do not assume U(a) = U_local(a) + U_systemic(a). That would repeat the additive-utility assumption we already rejected as a default in the Expected Utility work. Instead: U(a) = F_U(U_local, U_systemic, Risk, Cost, Context, ...)
rows.statement: Rejects assuming additive utility composition U(a)=U_local(a)+U_systemic(a) (repeating the already-rejected default from the Expected Utility work), requiring instead a general composition function U(a)=F_U(U_local,U_systemic,Risk,Cost,Context,...) with additive composition treated as only one explicitly declared regime.

rows.anchor: EpistemicAgency -> Decision then Decision -> Governance/Policy -> Authorization then Authorization -> Execution. That preserves the distinction between epistemic agency and governance authority.
rows.statement: Corrects the ledger's compressed 'KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action' arrow (which could imply Epistemic Agency owns Authorization) to a clearer chain EpistemicAgency->Decision, then Decision->Governance/Policy->Authorization, then Authorization->Execution, preserving the distinction between epistemic agency and governance authority.

rows.anchor: Attention != Value != Truth. ... Epistemic Agency should not automatically optimize practical utility. ... practical relevance does not by itself establish the epistemic value of knowledge. ... Epistemic Value != Practical Utility.
rows.statement: Extracts from the anthology's curiosity/attention and pragmatic-encroachment chapters the candidate distinctions Attention != Value != Truth and Epistemic Value != Practical Utility, warning that the existing Epistemic Agency dimension-selection formula must not silently optimize practical utility as if it were epistemic value, and connecting this to the already-established EU != EpistemicQuality caution in the Expected Utility work.

rows.anchor: epistemic judgments contain a special kind of 'should', a binding/reason-giving character, rather than merely a calculation of which belief best achieves some goal. ... Epistemic Norm != Utility Function ... Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should'.
rows.statement: Extracts Grimm's argument that epistemic normativity is not reducible to teleological goal-promotion, giving Epistemic Norm != Utility Function and Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should', requiring KR-EXPECTED-UTILITY to remain downstream of epistemic assessment rather than silently defining epistemic rationality.

rows.anchor: Why did this dimension become worthy of attention in the first place? ... AttentionSelection != DimensionDiscovery != FactFinding. This could become important for Epistemic Agency.
rows.statement: Extracts Brady's curiosity-as-selective-attention chapter to propose a prior stage AttentionSelection != DimensionDiscovery != FactFinding, asking why a dimension becomes worthy of investigation before the existing dimension-selection argmax formula applies, relevant to Epistemic Agency.
missing: formal AttentionSelection operator

rows.anchor: Which source should be queried? ... different information sources, including agents and objective sources/oracles ... SourceSelection != FactFinding. It is an agency/query-planning decision. ... query-available information can be limited by subjective knowledge, measurement instruments, experimental design, computing power, missing resources ... Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's source-selection and resource-limitation discussion to propose S_t^available={Human,Log,Instrument,Database,Network,Agent,Oracle,...} and SelectSource(Q,K,C,S,R), giving SourceSelection != FactFinding (an agency/query-planning decision) and connecting resource limitations (subjective knowledge, instruments, computing power) to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work.

rows.anchor: not every question can be asked because of instrument limitations, information-source availability, social conventions, financial resources, procedural constraints. ... Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation. This connects directly to: Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's procedural-information limitations (instrument, source-availability, social, financial, procedural constraints) into Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation, explicitly connected to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work; uses the classic nine-pearls weighing problem (only certain questions available at each stage, next question depends on previous answer, forming a conditional event tree) as a candidate benchmark for Inquiry Strategy = conditional sequence of epistemic actions, pi:(K_t,I_t)->a_t with a_{t+1}=pi(K_{t+1},I_{t+1}), richer than static NextAction=argmax Utility(a).
invariants: Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation

experiment.hypothesis: Inquiry strategy is better modeled as a conditional sequence of epistemic actions than as static utility-maximizing action selection
experiment.setup: Nine-pearls weighing-problem-style conditional decision tree, adapted as a candidate KnowledgeOS benchmark
experiment.assumptions: Available questions depend on prior answers (procedural constraints)
experiment.inputs: Not yet specified for KnowledgeOS
experiment.method: Not yet executed
experiment.limitations: Purely a proposed future benchmark, not run
experiment.conclusion: Proposed as a possible future KnowledgeOS experiment for Epistemic Agency

rows.anchor: protocols as sets of legal sequences of inquiry actions. A protocol can constrain which questioning actions are available at each stage. ... InquiryProtocol_t with AvailableActions_t = Protocol(K_t,Q_t,C_t).
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's protocol semantics (legal sequences of inquiry actions, constraining availability at each stage) into a candidate InquiryProtocol_t with AvailableActions_t=Protocol(K_t,Q_t,C_t), giving the lifecycle Q_t -> AvailableInquiryActions_t -> Select -> Execute -> Observation -> Update as a stronger foundation for Epistemic Agency than unconstrained 'the AI chooses the next action.'
missing: formal Protocol() definition

rows.anchor: A_Q = A_Q^domain union A_Q^epistemic with applicability evaluated explicitly. Candidate epistemic actions: {InvestigateFurther, Wait, NoOp} where applicable. Mitigate is domain-dependent. This preserves: Available != Feasible != Applicable.
rows.statement: Reaffirms that the action space must not have universally mandatory members (the prior spec incorrectly required {a1,...,NoOp,Wait,InvestigateFurther,Mitigate} unconditionally); corrects to A_Q=A_Q^domain union A_Q^epistemic with applicability evaluated explicitly (only InvestigateFurther/Wait/NoOp are candidate-universal where applicable; Mitigate is domain-dependent), extending Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient with Available != Feasible != Applicable.

rows.anchor: Epistemic Agency != Chain of Responsibility but: Chain of Responsibility = candidate structural analogy. ... GoF says: pass the request until someone handles it. KnowledgeOS needs: evaluate evidence adequacy and policy before accepting the result.
rows.statement: Compares GoF's Chain of Responsibility (a request passes through potential handlers until one takes responsibility, sender need not know the final receiver) to the metro-example resource-selection problem (H1=InternalMemory,...,H5=ExternalSearch), concluding Epistemic Agency != Chain of Responsibility because KnowledgeOS additionally requires evaluating evidence adequacy and policy before accepting a handler's result, while Chain of Responsibility remains a candidate structural analogy.

sources.note: First reading of the Theory v1.0 numbered definition/axiom/theorem register (2026-09-02) by this investigation lane; refutes the InvariantReg-never-enumerated premise underlying prior K9-closure robustness research (found circularly hard-coded), explains the Sat_c 3-executable/5-blocked split as an inheritance boundary, and fixes/corrects several object definitions (Delta_t, Zero, I_t, kernel K, minimality DEF-33).

rows.anchor: 0. The finding that frames the rest ... My four authoritative artifacts cite zero of these numbers. ... I have been reconstructing a theory whose own canonical numbering I had never opened. ... [DEF] 33, [AX] 7, [THM] 11 (7,8,10 tagging defect), [COR] declared but 0 instances
rows.statement: Discloses that four of the investigation's own prior authoritative artifacts cite zero of Theory v1.0's own numbered statements (DEF-1, DEF-21, DEF-22, DEF-32, CIRC-5, THM-9, S^epi, Adequate all return 0 hits), meaning a whole theory had been reconstructed without ever opening its own canonical numbering register. Census of the register: 33 contiguous DEF numbers, 7 contiguous AX numbers, 11 theorems (three of which, 7/8/10, exist as sections but carry no [THM-n] tag -- a tagging defect, not a missing theorem), and a declared-but-empty [COR] (Corollary) statement class despite the document being titled to include 'Corollaries'.

rows.anchor: 1. ⭐⭐⭐ G-67 is a homonym, and the InvariantReg reading is misclassified ... two lanes assigned the same gap ID to two different objects ... The InvariantReg premise does not survive ... ℐ is enumerated three times, in three incompatible ways, by three lanes that do not cite each other
rows.statement: Finds G-67 is a homonym used by two unrelated corpus lanes: in phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/ steps 288-291, G-67 means the equiv_K/approx formula-collision, WITHDRAWN by Step 290 and replaced by N-1'; in readiness/07, a Gita document, and a forward plan, G-67 means 'InvariantReg (I), the mandatory invariant register, never enumerated' -- described in the investigator's own forward plan as 'the single most evidenced blocker in the estate.' Finds the InvariantReg reading does NOT survive: I is independently enumerated three times, in three mutually incompatible shapes, by three lanes that never cite each other: (1) Step 048 SS48.60's InvariantRegistry, a 10-field schema with 0 rows populated (2026-08-28); (2) Step 120's K1-K7, seven named invariants (Provenance, Authority, Epistemic status, Temporal validity, Deterministic verification, Traceability, Feedback) each with an experiment and verdict, plus a systematic absorption/necessity argument (2026-08-28T12:45:10); (3) Theory v1.0 SS75's I1-I9, nine boxed invariants explicitly titled 'Kernel invariants' and closing with 'these are now the beginning of the KnowledgeOS Constitution' (2026-09-02T00:46:31). Verifies enumeration 3 sits inside one unbroken internal section run (SS70 Kernel -> SS71 Kernel shape -> SS74 Invariant custody -> SS75 Kernel invariants I1-I9) requiring no inference to bridge.

rows.anchor: [EMP] Independence — citation zero, four directed checks plus a corpus-wide co-citation sweep ... any file citing both the 7 and the 9: none in the corpus. ... Chronology — the claim outlived its truth ... All three carriers of 'never enumerated' postdate enumeration 3
rows.statement: Runs five independence checks confirming zero cross-citation between the three InvariantReg enumerations and the 'never enumerated' claim: Theory v1.0 never cites Step 120/K1-K7/'seven invariants' (0); Step 120 never cites I1-I9/'Representation != Identity' (0); readiness/07 never cites Step 120/Theory v1.0/I1/I9 (0); the Gita G-67 document never cites Step 120/SS75/Theory v1.0 (0); no file in the whole corpus cites both the seven-invariant and nine-invariant enumerations together. Establishes a chronology showing the claim outlived its truth: all three documents asserting 'never enumerated' (readiness/07, the Gita doc, both 2026-09-06; the forward plan, 2026-09-07) postdate the third enumeration (2026-09-02 00:46:31) by four to five days.

rows.anchor: And 'blocked in 66 of 66 worlds' is not evidence of absence ... exec/extend_k9_worlds.py:15 hard-codes the premise: G_str['InvariantReg'] = (['K'], 'NOT ENUMERATED', 'D') ... 66/66 therefore measures the robustness of the closure computation to world choice — it does not measure the enumeration status of ℐ. ... the premise is the claim it is offered to support.
rows.statement: Critically re-examines the widely-cited '66 of 66 worlds' robustness finding (from a prior batch's k9-closure computation) supporting the InvariantReg-never-enumerated premise: finds the source code exec/extend_k9_worlds.py line 15 HARD-CODES the string 'NOT ENUMERATED' as an INPUT to all 66 world variants, so the 66/66 result measures only the robustness of the closure computation to world CHOICE, not the actual enumeration status of the invariant register -- the computation itself is sound, but its premise is exactly the claim it was being offered as evidence FOR. This is a circularity finding that undercuts the evidentiary weight of the prior 66-world robustness research thread on this specific premise.

rows.anchor: ⭐ Consequence for my own forward plan. D1 is recorded there as 'enumerate ℐ / ℛ_req — a derivation, not a decision'. On this evidence it is the opposite: three enumerations exist and no precedence rule chooses between them. D1 is a decision problem ... D1 is an instance of the pattern its own plan names, and was filed in the other column.
rows.statement: Applies this finding self-critically: the investigator's own forward plan had filed enumerating InvariantReg/R_req ('D1') as 'a derivation, not a decision' -- but given three enumerations already exist with no precedence rule choosing among them, D1 is actually a DECISION problem, precisely the same state-B category the plan itself separately identified for 16 of 17 other items. Concludes D1 was misfiled into the wrong column of its own author's classification scheme.

rows.anchor: [OPEN] Not settled by me: whether K1…K7 (transition-legality flavour) and I1…I9 (category-non-collapse flavour) are the same register under two readings or two registers. I9 and K1 plainly overlap; I3 has no K-counterpart. Relation recorded as RELATED — IDENTITY UNWITNESSED. Not merged. ... Disposition: C — COMPETING / DEPENDENCY-INCOMPLETE, not D — GENUINE CORPUS GAP.
rows.statement: Leaves explicitly open whether K1-K7 and I1-I9 are the same invariant register under two different readings or genuinely two separate registers: I9 ('Provenance must survive valid epistemic transition') and K1 (Provenance) plainly overlap, while I3 ('Representation != Identity') has no K-counterpart at all. Records the relation as RELATED-IDENTITY UNWITNESSED, explicitly not merged. Issues final disposition for the InvariantReg reading of G-67: class C (COMPETING/DEPENDENCY-INCOMPLETE), explicitly NOT class D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP) as the prior research thread had treated it.

rows.anchor: 2. ⭐⭐⭐ The Sat_c executability boundary is an inheritance boundary ... EXECUTABLE_NOW = ['content','evidence','provenance'] ... BLOCKED = ['status','consistency','governance','temporal','operational'] ... The three executable Sat_c classes are exactly the three with an ancestor in Theory v1.0. The five blocked classes are exactly the five added afterwards with no ancestor.
rows.statement: Discovers the historical cause of Sat_c's 3-executable/5-blocked class split (from satc_spec.py, previously established in this programme): Theory v1.0 carries two requirement/gap taxonomies (SS28 DEF-20's requirement kinds including evidence and provenance requirements; SS30's typed gap Delta_t=(Delta^content,Delta^uncertainty,Delta^model,Delta^observability,Delta^requirement)). An occurrence census across the whole document (with positive controls) finds content/evidence/provenance each have an ancestor while status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational all score exactly 0 as requirement or gap dimensions (despite occurring as bare words elsewhere in the document). Concludes the three executable Sat_c classes are EXACTLY the three with a Theory v1.0 ancestor, and the five blocked classes are exactly the five added afterward with no ancestor at all.

rows.anchor: ⭐⭐ Executability tracks provenance, not difficulty. ... status: '⪰ IS NOT DEFINED BY THE THEORY', governance: 'no evaluator exists', temporal: 'no temporal semantics defined', operational: 'δ is Step 290 and is open'. ... BLOCKED here means UN-INHERITED, and that is a fourth thing beside UNDEFINED, UNFORMALIZED and UNIMPLEMENTED. ... uncertainty and model were inherited and dropped.
rows.statement: Argues Sat_c executability tracks PROVENANCE, not difficulty: satc_spec.py's own blocker notes for each blocked class explicitly say the theory does not define it (status not defined by the theory, no governance evaluator exists, no temporal semantics defined, delta/operational is an open Step 290 item). Proposes BLOCKED here means UN-INHERITED, a fourth epistemic category distinct from UNDEFINED, UNFORMALIZED, and UNIMPLEMENTED. Notes the mapping is not a clean bijection -- uncertainty and model classes were inherited from Theory v1.0's taxonomy but then dropped from the final eight-class Sat_c list, so the eight-class list is neither a subset nor superset of either v1.0 taxonomy. Explicitly states this feeds but does not reopen the prior G-33 disposition (all 8 Sat_c classes defined/formalised, 5 dependency-blocked stands) -- it supplies only the historical CAUSE of the split.

rows.anchor: 3. Object-by-object: Δ_t Gap is a SET (DEF-21) ... §29 explicitly rejects the older K_t^* - K_t subtraction ... direct predecessor of v1.2's GapPartition ... Sat 2-argument and two-valued at birth ... the birth of U is exactly the v1.0 → v1.2 step ... Zero DEF-22 ... Adequate ≡ Zero collapse ... visible in the theory text itself — it is not an artifact of the simulation.
rows.statement: Fixes several object definitions from Theory v1.0: Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)} (DEF-21, 'the canonical v1.0 definition'), with SS29 explicitly rejecting an older K_t^*-K_t subtraction form ('heterogeneous epistemic structures cannot generally be subtracted') -- identified as the direct predecessor of v1.2's GapPartition(K,Req)=(violated,undetermined,satisfied), giving a two-step declared supersession chain subtraction->set->partition; Sat at birth (DEF-21) is 2-argument and strictly TWO-VALUED (clean negation, no third value), meaning the birth of the U/undetermined value is exactly the v1.0->v1.2 transition, though the registry notes Sat carries two different arities within this one document (per-requirement Sat(K_t,r) and per-contract Sat(K_t,EC_t)); Zero(K_t,EC_t) iff Delta_t=empty-set iff K_t models EC_t (DEF-22), with Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t) (DEF-20) and SS29 giving Delta_t=empty-set iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t) -- meaning the Adequate=Zero collapse (previously flagged elsewhere as TG-3/CIRC-3) is visible directly in the theory's own text, not merely an artifact of a downstream simulation; also fixes Zero_epistemic != Zero_probabilistic.

rows.anchor: I_t — a re-typing, not a refinement ... K_t^* = I(G,C,S,t) a state ... DEF-19 𝕀(EC_t) = {K ∈ 𝕂 : Sat(K,EC_t)} a region of knowledge states ... I_t = ℛ_t the requirement set ... My registry row Ideal State / I_t_v1 / 2026-09-02T08:23:33 is not the first version. 𝕀(EC_t) precedes it by 7h 37m and has a different codomain.
rows.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior registry entry for the Ideal State object: finds a third formulation, DEF-19's I(EC_t)={K in K: Sat(K,EC_t)} (2026-09-02 00:46:31, a REGION of knowledge states, type P(K)) precedes the registry's previously-recorded 'I_t_v1' formulation (I_t=R_t, the requirement set, 2026-09-02 08:23:33) by 7 hours 37 minutes and has a fundamentally different codomain -- meaning I_t underwent a RE-TYPING across its history, not merely a refinement, and the registry's 'v1' label was itself an error (the witness/timestamp was correct, only its version-ordering label was wrong).

rows.anchor: 𝒦 — the kernel is a 4-tuple; the 5-tuple is conditional ... 𝒦=(𝒫,ℛ,δ,ℐ) and potentially 𝔎=(𝒫,ℛ,δ,ℐ,𝒰) ... This remains a [PROP], not an established theorem. ... v1.1-simulation TG-13 reports the kernel shape ... was not tested — citing the conditional 5-tuple as if it were the proposal, and collapsing a distinction the theory marked typographically. The theory's headline candidate is the 4-tuple.
rows.statement: Fixes the kernel's headline shape as a 4-tuple K=(P,R,delta,I) with a conditional, explicitly-provisional 5-tuple variant K-fraktur=(P,R,delta,I,U) using a visually distinct glyph, self-marked '[PROP], not an established theorem.' Finds a downstream v1.1-simulation document (TG-13) mistakenly reports 'the kernel shape (P,R,delta,I,U) proposed by the prior lane was not tested,' citing the conditional 5-tuple as if it were the theory's actual headline proposal and collapsing a typographic distinction the source theory deliberately preserved -- the theory's real headline candidate is the 4-tuple. Also notes this section is the birth of delta ('transition/commit semantics') and I ('protected invariants') specifically AS kernel components, not as standalone objects.

rows.anchor: DEF-33 — minimality is explicitly not operator count ... K_min = argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to CapabilityClosure, SemanticAdequacy, Preservation, InvariantPreservation, TransitionCompleteness. ... custody(I,K) = {o ∈ K : I fails in K−{o}} ... Smaller Kernel ⇏ Better Kernel.
rows.statement: Fixes DEF-33's minimality definition: K_min=argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to five explicit constraints (CapabilityClosure, SemanticAdequacy, Preservation, InvariantPreservation, TransitionCompleteness) -- deliberately NOT defined as operator count. SS74 adds a custody function custody(I,K)={o in K: invariant I fails in K minus {o}} and concludes the boxed principle Smaller Kernel does NOT imply Better Kernel.

rows.anchor: §47 — the backbone, and a substitution inside it ... O_t → K_t → I_t → Δ_t → K_{t+1} refined to O_t → ℱ_t → K_t → EC_t → Δ_t → T_t → K_{t+1}. The refinement replaces I_t with EC_t. ... Two new objects appear here and nowhere in my registry: ℱ_t and T_t.
rows.statement: Traces the theory's core state-evolution backbone through a refinement: an earlier 5-stage form O_t->K_t->I_t->Delta_t->K_{t+1} is refined to a 7-stage form O_t->F_t->K_t->EC_t->Delta_t->T_t->K_{t+1}, replacing I_t with EC_t -- shown coherent with DEF-19 since I is defined FROM EC_t, so the refinement substitutes a derived object with the object it derives from. Flags two entirely new objects (F_t and T_t) that appear in this section but nowhere in the investigation's existing registry.

rows.anchor: §32 — four gap boundaries, Z4 subdivided ... Z1 known dimension/unknown value · Z2 unknown dimension · Z3 unknown relationship · Z4 representation/observability failure, itself split: Unobserved ≠ Unobservable ≠ Uninterpretable ≠ Representationally inadequate
rows.statement: Records Theory v1.0's four-way gap-boundary taxonomy (Z1 known dimension/unknown value, Z2 unknown dimension, Z3 unknown relationship, Z4 representation/observability failure), with Z4 itself explicitly subdivided into a boxed four-way distinction: Unobserved != Unobservable != Uninterpretable != Representationally inadequate.

rows.anchor: 4. v1.1-simulation is identified, not inferred ... theory-v1.1-simulation simulates 20260902-004631, and postdates 00:46:31. Provenance of the document's own timestamp remains UNRECORDABLE, not ABSENT.
rows.statement: Establishes via content evidence (not internal timestamps, since none exist across all 14 files) that theory-v1.1-simulation postdates and directly simulates Theory v1.0 (matching experiment ID/scenario seed 20260902, exactly resolving citations to SS47's refined 7-state backbone and SS66's Preservation vector, using DEF numbers all within DEF-1..33). Classifies the package's own timestamp provenance as UNRECORDABLE, explicitly distinct from ABSENT.

rows.anchor: And it contributes two objects of its own: EC is typed ... EpistemicContract(standard, requirements, attribution_policy) ... A standard/standard collision on two carriers, and it is not among the 10 collisions v1.1 registers. ... Γ is 4-argument: K = Γ(E,Q,C,EC) ... TG-1 proves it jointly unsatisfiable with DEF-1 factivity ... CE-1 is born here and cited by satc_spec.py — a verified cross-package citation.
rows.statement: Records two objects v1.1-simulation itself contributes: a typed EC=EpistemicContract(standard,requirements,attribution_policy), whose own 'standard' sub-field (EpistemicStandard(min_weight,require_independent_sources,require_corroboration)) is a DIFFERENT type from r's 'standard' field (an acceptance criterion) -- flagged as an unregistered standard/standard collision, not among v1.1's own ten registered collisions; and a 4-argument Gamma realized as K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC)=knowledge_attribution(E,Q,C,EC), whose TG-1 proves jointly unsatisfiable with DEF-1 factivity for any attributing Gamma (the CE-1 finding, connecting directly to the prior batch's v1-1-sim-factivity-impossibility-finding object), with three unchosen repairs R1/R2/R3 explicitly framed as 'a theory decision, not an experimental one.' Verifies CE-1 is genuinely cross-cited by a separate package (satc_spec.py's factivity_requirement note), confirming real cross-package citation rather than coincidental naming.

rows.anchor: ⭐ TG-2 is implemented-but-not-specified — the inversion ... No evidence-retirement relation: Revise exists, Supersede/Retract/Expire do not. Yet B-formal-model records History as 'append-only; supersession stores the prior record.' Supersession is realised in the state and undefined as a relation. ... This one runs the other way, and it is the only such case so far recorded.
rows.statement: Identifies a rare inverted case in the Specified/Implemented four-way classification pattern: TG-2 claims 'no evidence-retirement relation exists' (Supersede/Retract/Expire undefined as relations, only Revise exists), yet a separate B-formal-model document records History as append-only with supersession explicitly STORED IN THE STATE -- meaning supersession is realized operationally but undefined as a formal relation. Notes every other instance of this four-way distinction found so far in this reconstruction runs Specified-but-not-Implemented; this is the only case recorded running the opposite direction (Implemented-but-not-Specified).

rows.anchor: 5. Two collision registers, disjoint alphabets ... Neither cites the other, and they barely overlap. The true collision inventory is larger than either lane knows. ... I = IdealState I_t · Invariants I1..I9 · Information — this is the collision D1 rides on ... E = Evidence (DEF-7) · EpistemicState E_t — v1.1 calls it 'the most dangerous'
rows.statement: Finds two entirely disjoint symbol-collision registers exist in the corpus with no cross-citation: v1.1-simulation's C-type-system (10 Latin-alphabet collisions: P, K, E, H, I, S, C, R, M, Q) and the investigation's own H1 glyph act (16 Greek-alphabet collisions: Pi, Phi, Theta, Sigma, D_t, etc.), concluding the TRUE collision inventory is larger than either lane individually knows. Highlights two load-bearing collisions: 'I' (IdealState I_t, Invariants I1-I9, and Information -- identified as exactly the collision the investigation's own D1 item silently rides across, writing 'I/R_req' as one slash over a genuine three-way collision) and 'E' (Evidence per DEF-7, versus EpistemicState E_t, self-described by v1.1 as 'the most dangerous' collision since the v1.1 correction's whole point depends on the two NOT being confused). Also notes Sigma is given three separate axes (Support S, Conflict C, Resolution R), recorded only, explicitly not reconciled per standing prohibition.

rows.anchor: 6. What this does NOT do ... No canonicalization · no kernel selected · no 𝒪_core frozen · no merge of the three invariant enumerations · no repair of the Adequate ≡ Zero collapse · no choice among R1/R2/R3 · no reconciliation of Σ · |K| = 11 untouched · three_model_convergence/ not consumed.
rows.statement: Explicitly scopes what this reading does not do: no canonicalization of any object, no kernel selected, no O_core frozen, no merging of the three invariant enumerations, no repair of the Adequate=Zero collapse, no choice among the three factivity repairs R1/R2/R3, no reconciliation of Sigma's competing axes, the |K|=11 finding left untouched, and three_model_convergence/ not consumed (firewall respected).

rows.anchor: 1. ⭐⭐⭐ The programme's phase-level open questions ARE the theory's declared limits ... §86 ... A serious v1.0 must also state its limits ... declares six ... Five of the six programme-level blockers are §86 restated. They are DECLARED LIMITS of v1.0, not blockers discovered afterwards.
rows.statement: Discovers Theory v1.0 SS86 explicitly declares six named open limits (OPEN-1 canonical semantic carrier -- unique K or an equivalence class of representations; OPEN-2 K_t's exact mathematical structure -- graph/lattice/category/sheaf, explicitly called the current blocking question; OPEN-3 canonical equiv_sem; OPEN-4 canonical gap geometry -- does Delta_t admit a distance metric; OPEN-5 a universal epistemic uncertainty algebra; OPEN-6 a minimal primitive kernel, explicitly stating no 8- or 13-operator universal kernel has been established), and finds five of the investigation's own six independently-derived programme-level forward-plan blockers (OQ-1 the carrier decision, K's rival forms, CR-4, a G-12 metric question, TG-02 independence/Dempster blocking, and the not-yet-selected kernel) are essentially SS86 restated -- reframing them as the theory's own DECLARED limits from birth (2026-09-02 00:46:31), not gaps discovered afterward by this investigation.

rows.anchor: ⭐ This puts OQ-1 in the family of declared boundaries already recorded in this reconstruction (ρ_A, Det_r, Ω-B, ⪰) — a deliberate scope exclusion, not an omission. ... Undeclared and declared-open are different epistemic states, and only the second carries an author's intent.
rows.statement: Argues the carrier-decision blocker (OQ-1) belongs to a growing family of DECLARED boundaries already found in this reconstruction (alongside rho_A, Det_r, and the Omega-B philosophical-anchor exclusion) -- a deliberate scope exclusion made by the theory's own author, not an accidental omission. Corrects the forward plan's phrasing ('KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier') to the more accurate 'the carrier is declared OPEN, by name, as OPEN-1' -- explicitly distinguishing undeclared (no epistemic stance taken) from declared-open (an author's deliberate, intentional stance) as two different epistemic states.

rows.anchor: [EMP] Citation check. OPEN-1…OPEN-6 are cited once in the whole estate outside their own document ... The publicdigit/reviews/ hits for OPEN-1 are a different object ... A second identifier homonym, found the same day as G-67's.
rows.statement: Finds OPEN-1..OPEN-6 are cited exactly once anywhere in the whole estate outside their own document (in the 08:54:20 reply). Notes a separate set of 'OPEN-1' hits in publicdigit/reviews/ are a completely different, PHP-derived object from an unrelated contract-neutrality lane (2026-08-18/19) -- flagging this as a second identifier homonym discovered the same day as G-67's, in the same investigation session.

rows.anchor: 2. The reply, four hours and eight minutes later ... OPEN-1 / OPEN-2 — a carrier candidate, self-labelled as such ... K_t = (E_t,ρ_t,α_t,π_t,τ_t) ... This is not necessarily the final implementation tuple. ... the first serious candidate for closing OPEN-1 / OPEN-2. ... V1 therefore has at least two candidates to enumerate, not one.
rows.statement: Reads a same-day (08:54:20, 4h8m after the SS86 declaration) reply document proposing a candidate carrier: K_t=(E_t,rho_t,alpha_t,pi_t,tau_t) (epistemic content, semantic relations, attributions/assessments, provenance, temporal validity), self-labeled 'not necessarily the final implementation tuple' but 'the first serious candidate for closing OPEN-1/OPEN-2.' Notes the investigation's own forward plan describes all experimental results as produced on a DIFFERENT tuple r=(value,source,tag,time) with |D|<=6 and claims 'no declared carrier' -- corrects this: a candidate is not a decision so the plan's overall claim stands, but this 5-tuple is not cited by the plan at all, meaning the true carrier-candidate enumeration has at least two entries, not one.

rows.anchor: OPEN-4 — dissolved rather than answered ... Gap → Requirement Residual → optional Measurement ... This eliminates the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance. ... Recorded as DISSOLVED-BY-REORDERING, not ANSWERED.
rows.statement: Finds the reply document reframes OPEN-4 (does the gap set admit a distance metric) via a reordering: Gap -> Requirement Residual -> optional Measurement, explicitly eliminating the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance. Argues this does NOT show a useful distance function exists -- it re-orders the question, making any metric a regime choice made AFTER the residual structure, not a property inherent to Delta_t itself. Classifies this precisely as DISSOLVED-BY-REORDERING, explicitly distinct from ANSWERED.

rows.anchor: OPEN-3 — a definition that removes the circularity by name ... R_1≡_sem R_2 ⟺ ∀(Q,C,EC): Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_2) ... eight enumerated observables: Identity, Meaning, EvidenceRelations, Assessment, Gap, Determination, History, ValidTransitions. ... This is exactly what CIRC-5 needs. ... An enumerated observable set is precisely what stops 'a chosen projection' from being arbitrary.
rows.statement: Finds the reply document proposes an observational equiv_sem definition addressing OPEN-3: R1 equiv_sem R2 iff for all (Q,C,EC), Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R2), with eight explicitly enumerated observable dimensions (Identity, Meaning, EvidenceRelations, Assessment, Gap, Determination, History, ValidTransitions), self-described as removing the circularity of 'they are equivalent because they mean the same thing.' Connects this directly to the prior batch's CIRC-5 finding (equiv_sem defined via an arbitrarily-chosen behavioral projection) -- argues an ENUMERATED observable set is precisely what would stop the projection choice from being arbitrary, which is exactly what CIRC-5 and a separate J-proof-obligations document (filing 'equiv_sem is well defined' as still requiring mathematical work) both need. Notes as UNDECIDABLE whether the separately-dated v1.1-simulation package (no internal timestamp, datable only to after 00:46:31) could have known about this definition.

rows.anchor: 3. ⭐⭐⭐ But ≡_sem now has THREE rival definitions, and they conflict ... A ... B CLOSURE-4 ... reviewed as 'the semantic equivalence claim is too strong' ... C 𝔎 = (K, =_str, ≡_sem, ≈_obs, SameId, ≡_H, ≡_P) — a 7-tuple ... in which ≡_sem and ≈_obs are distinct tuple positions ... The conflict is structural, not stylistic. A defines ≡_sem observationally. C exists to keep ≡_sem and ≈_obs apart. If semantic equivalence IS observational equivalence, the two positions of C's 7-tuple collapse.
rows.statement: Identifies a genuine three-way structural conflict among rival equiv_sem definitions in the corpus: (A) the newly-found observational definition with 8 enumerated observables, never cited by any other lane; (B) CLOSURE-4's executable, Q/Gamma/O-indexed tester (K1 equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} K2 iff determinations match for all q,o), previously reviewed elsewhere as 'the semantic equivalence claim is too strong'; (C) Step 261's 7-tuple K-fraktur=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P), carried through Steps 288-291, in which equiv_sem and approx_obs are DELIBERATELY DISTINCT tuple positions. Argues the conflict is structural, not stylistic: definition A defines equiv_sem observationally, while structure C exists specifically to KEEP equiv_sem and approx_obs apart -- if semantic equivalence really is observational equivalence, C's two positions collapse into one, exactly the collapse C was constructed to prevent.

rows.anchor: ⭐⭐ Consequence for my own plan. CR-4 is filed there as ... 'cheapest — the corpus already contains its own repair' and 'nearly self-resolving'. On this evidence it is a three-way conflict in which one option collapses a distinction another was created to protect, and a second carries a standing 'too strong' review. sources.note: A full 35-section executable research protocol (explicitly modelled on the KR-2026-09-01 kernel-reduction protocol's discipline) mandating a controlled simulation of the full derived KnowledgeOS Theory v1.0/v1.1 epistemic lifecycle, to test whether ~26 named conceptual roles (Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, K_t, Inquiry, Ideal State, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision/Supersession) can coexist operationally without collapsing into each other. Specifies ten required synthetic-world scenario families (A simple determination through J unobservable property), a mandatory four-way Unknown taxonomy test, a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace requirement, an information-conservation (data-processing) test, a knowledge-attribution factivity test, a non-circular semantic-equivalence test, a representation-invariance test, a transition-vocabulary test (Acquire/Interpret/Assess/Determine/Attribute/Revise/Reject/Accept/Supersede), a reframed kernel-minimality test (capabilities first, operators only after), a Zero test over 8 named cases, an Ideal-State test, a decision-boundary test, a history/identity test, a causal/statistical confounding test, a provenance test, 18 named adversarial test cases, 20 named property-based tests (P1-P20), Monte Carlo requirements with mandatory vacuity auditing, a mandatory no-smuggling audit inspecting nine named operators for hidden capability leakage, an oracle-independence requirement, a formal type-check over 24 named types with notation-collision inspection, a circularity audit (five named candidate circular-definition pairs), a theory-consistency dependency graph, a first-class negative-results discipline, 17 named success criteria (S1-S17), an explicit success-does-not-mean-proof discipline, 12 required output artifacts (A-L, including a nine-class Theory Gap Register G1-G9), a seven-part final verdict format (with a four-choice, deliberately conservative Theory Status classification), an autonomous-execution rule, a reproducibility mandate, and a closing scientific principle that the goal is not to prove the theory correct but to discover exactly what survives, fails, and remains open.

rows.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.
rows.statement: States the protocol's foundational experimental discipline: the theory must never be silently repaired or modified merely to make the simulation pass, no undocumented assumptions may be introduced, and neither a successful nor a failed simulation may be treated as proof or disproof of the theory -- the purpose is only to determine whether the theory is internally executable, semantically coherent, well-typed, and behaviorally stable.

rows.anchor: Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, Knowledge State K_t, Inquiry Q, Ideal State I_t, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision, Supersession. ... test whether these are genuinely distinct conceptual roles or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.
rows.statement: States the primary research question: whether twenty-six named conceptual roles spanning the entire epistemic lifecycle can coexist operationally in one executable simulation without collapsing, or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.

rows.anchor: K_t = Gamma(E_t, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) where Gamma determines which parts of the epistemic state qualify as Knowledge State content ... Knowledge remains factive: Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t). Do NOT operationally assume that the simulation can magically observe objective truth. If truth is externally supplied by the simulation world, explicitly label that as world-state information and keep it separate from the agent's epistemic state.
rows.statement: Specifies the core theory-under-test's Knowledge Attribution mechanism K_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) with mandatory factivity Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), explicitly forbidding the simulation from assuming it can observe objective truth directly -- any world-supplied ground truth must be labelled as world-state information kept separate from the agent's own epistemic state (an oracle-vs-agent-knowledge separation).

rows.anchor: Do NOT make Bayesian likelihood ratios a universal KnowledgeOS law. Also test non-Bayesian / qualitative evidence assessment. ... Test whether changing epistemic standards can change assessment or determination while the underlying evidence remains identical. ... A model that fits simulated observations must not automatically be classified as true.
rows.statement: Mandates that evidence assessment be tested with BOTH a Bayesian likelihood-ratio realization AND non-Bayesian/qualitative assessment regimes (Bayesian ratios must never become a universal KnowledgeOS law); requires an explicit test that varying epistemic standards alone (holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed) can change assessment or determination; and requires model-fit to be tested separately from causal/epistemic validity so that a well-fitting model is never automatically classified as true.

Semantic Equivalence != Representation Equality, Mathematical Regime != Knowledge Ontology.
rows.statement: Enumerates a mandatory list of roughly twenty required state separations the simulator must never accidentally collapse (Reality/Observation/Evidence/Interpretation/Hypothesis/Determination/Knowledge/Decision/Authorization/Action chain; Epistemic State/Knowledge State/Ideal State; Gap/Zero/Innovation; Probability/Credence/Truth; Information Quantity/Evidence Weight/Knowledge Gain; Model Fit/Model Validity; History/Current State; Identity/State Equality; Completeness/Sufficiency; Rejection/Acceptance; Unknown/Unobserved/Unobservable/Underdetermined; Semantic Equivalence/Representation Equality; Mathematical Regime/Knowledge Ontology), with any collapse to be reported as a failure.
