This is an anti-fabrication test. ... SCENARIO C -- MULTIPLE COMPETING HYPOTHESES ... Test explicitly: Reject(H1) != Accept(H2). ... SCENARIO D -- DIFFERENT EPISTEMIC STANDARDS ... SCENARIO E -- DIFFERENT INQUIRIES
rows.statement: Specifies ten required scenario families (A-J): A simple determination (verifying knowledge is not merely copied from observation); B incomplete evidence (anti-fabrication test: the system must not invent a value when Determination is empty); C multiple competing hypotheses (testing Reject(H1)!=Accept(H2)); D different epistemic standards holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed while varying only S_t^epi; E different inquiries over the identical K_t testing inquiry-relative adequacy.

rows.anchor: SCENARIO F -- CONFLICTING EVIDENCE ... Do NOT automatically average them. ... The system can preserve unresolved conflict. SCENARIO G -- DEPENDENT EVIDENCE ... represent dependence, avoid double counting, or explicitly state that independence is an assumption. SCENARIO H -- MODEL MISMATCH ... Fit alone does not produce Knowledge. SCENARIO I -- RETROSPECTIVE REVISION ... Do NOT rewrite history as if K_1 never existed. SCENARIO J -- UNOBSERVABLE PROPERTY ... Do NOT classify this as: observed false, probability zero, rejected hypothesis, evidence absence.
rows.statement: Specifies scenario families F-J: F conflicting evidence (system must preserve unresolved conflict rather than automatically averaging); G dependent evidence (must represent dependence, avoid double-counting, or explicitly declare independence as an assumption); H model mismatch (a better-fitting but causally wrong model M1 versus a causally correct M2 -- fit alone must not produce Knowledge); I retrospective revision (K_2 != K_1, historical K_1 must remain traceable, never rewritten); J unobservable property (must be classified as Unknown/Unobservable, never as observed-false, probability-zero, rejected-hypothesis, or evidence-absence).

rows.anchor: UNOBSERVED, UNINTERPRETED, UNDERDETERMINED, UNOBSERVABLE. Create test cases where each one occurs independently. ... Verify that the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.
rows.statement: Mandates a four-way Unknown taxonomy test with independently constructed test cases for each of Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable, checking Observation/Interpretation/Evidence/Determination/Knowledge/Gap/Zero status for each, explicitly verifying the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.

rows.anchor: At every transition record: input state, output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information was added, whether uncertainty changed, whether knowledge attribution changed, whether requirements changed, whether the transition was reversible.
rows.statement: Mandates a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace (Reality->Observation->Information->Evidence->Interpretation->HypothesisSpace->EvidenceAssessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t->Inquiry->IdealState->RequirementEvaluation->Gap->Zero->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action->newObservation->K_{t+1}) with eleven recorded facts at every single transition (input/output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information/uncertainty/attribution/requirements changed, reversibility).

rows.anchor: If X -> Y -> Z and no new information enters between Y and Z, then Z must not magically contain semantic information unavailable in Y, except where explicitly introduced by: model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, standards. If new information appears, identify its source. Any unexplained semantic information creation is a critical failure.
rows.statement: Mandates an Information Conservation test operationalizing the data-processing-inequality principle: no unexplained semantic information may appear between two steps with no new input, unless explicitly attributable to model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, or standards -- any unexplained semantic-information creation is a critical failure.

rows.anchor: high probability != knowledge, strong evidence != knowledge, coherent belief != knowledge, model fit != knowledge, determination != knowledge. ... If the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify the claim as Knowledge.
rows.statement: Mandates a Knowledge Attribution test constructing six epistemic-state cases (true/false/uncertain/rejected/highly-probable/justified-but-not-truth-verified hypotheses) and checking five non-collapse requirements (high probability, strong evidence, coherent belief, model fit, and determination all != knowledge); if the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify a claim as Knowledge.

rows.anchor: Implementation A: explicit Interpret + Represent. Implementation B: single combined semantic transformation. Implementation C: different internal data structure. ... The comparison MUST NOT be based only on operator names. ... If semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior, report the circularity.
rows.statement: Mandates a Semantic Equivalence test comparing three deliberately different implementations of the same conceptual operation (split Interpret+Represent, a single combined transformation, and a different internal data structure) over nine behavioral dimensions (inquiries, context, evidence, determinations, gaps, history, transitions, knowledge attribution, invariant preservation), explicitly never based on operator names alone, and mandates reporting circularity if semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior.

rows.anchor: This is NOT the previous 13-operator counting experiment. Do NOT begin with: "How many operators are there?" Instead ask: "What semantic capabilities are required?" ... K_min = argmin Complexity(R) subject to: semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, fixed semantic carrier, fixed observable behavior contract. If the feasible set changes between representations, cardinality comparisons are invalid. Report this explicitly.
rows.statement: Explicitly reframes the Kernel Minimality test away from the prior 13-operator counting approach: begin with 'what semantic capabilities are required' (Capability = externally distinguishable epistemic transformation/responsibility), construct the required capability set C and a candidate representation R, and test capability-set equivalence between differently-operator-counted implementations BEFORE any minimization; formalizes K_min=argmin Complexity(R) subject to six simultaneous constraints, mandating an explicit report that cardinality comparisons are invalid whenever the feasible set changes between representations.

rows.anchor: Investigate whether: Zero = no unmet requirement can be maintained without turning Zero into a semantic notion of absolute certainty. ... test all combinations: Gap exists, Gap empty, Evidence incomplete, Evidence conflicting, Evidence unavailable, Requirement irrelevant, Requirement satisfied by negative determination, Requirement satisfied by "cannot determine".
rows.statement: Mandates a Zero test evaluating Delta_t and Zero(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) across eight named combinations (gap exists/empty, evidence incomplete/conflicting/unavailable, requirement irrelevant, requirement satisfied by negative determination, requirement satisfied by 'cannot determine'), investigating whether Zero can be maintained as no-unmet-requirement without sliding into a semantic notion of absolute certainty.

rows.anchor: Create cases where: determination is unique but multiple actions are possible. Expected: Determination does not automatically imply one Decision. ... decision exists but authorization is absent. Expected: Decision != Authorization. ... authorization exists but action does not occur. Expected: Authorization != Action.
rows.statement: Mandates a Decision Boundary test with three constructed cases proving Determination does not automatically imply one Decision, Decision != Authorization (decision without authorization), and Authorization != Action (authorization without resulting action).

rows.anchor: X causes Y but an observed confounder Z creates a strong association. Also create: X and Y correlated but X does not cause Y. ... The result must distinguish: Association, Prediction, Explanation, Causal Claim. A fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.
rows.statement: Mandates a Causal/Statistical test with two constructed confounding scenarios (X causes Y with a confounding Z creating spurious association; X and Y correlated with no causal link), requiring the system to distinguish Association, Prediction, Explanation, and Causal Claim as four separate categories -- a fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.

rows.anchor: 1. highly probable but false claim 2. true claim with weak evidence 3. duplicated evidence 4. correlated evidence 5. misleading source ... 18. conclusion generated without supporting evidence. The simulator must prefer: "cannot determine" over fabricated certainty.
rows.statement: Mandates eighteen named adversarial test cases explicitly designed to fool the simulator (highly-probable-but-false claim, true-claim-with-weak-evidence, duplicated/correlated evidence, misleading source, wrong-model-with-excellent-fit, correct-model-with-sparse-evidence, rejected-hypothesis-later-reinstated, ambiguous interpretation, representation change, changing inquiry/standard, unavailable observation, historical-vs-current state, conflicting/irrelevant evidence, false inference from correlation, unsupported conclusion), with the overriding requirement that the simulator prefer 'cannot determine' over fabricated certainty in every case.

rows.anchor: P1: Evidence != Knowledge ... P8: Evidence dependence prevents unjustified double counting ... P11: Knowledge attribution respects factivity ... P19: Changing K_t does not imply changing identity ... P20: Zero is inquiry-relative. ... For each property define: Property ID, Formal statement, Generator assumptions, Test procedure, Observed result, Counterexamples.
rows.statement: Mandates property-based testing with a required protocol per property (ID, formal statement, generator assumptions, test procedure, observed result, counterexamples), specifying twenty named minimum properties P1-P20 spanning Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Rejection!=Acceptance, Gap!=Zero, inquiry-relative adequacy, historical-vs-current-state distinguishability, representation-vs-semantic equality, dependence-aware evidence, model-fit-vs-causal-validity, no-unsupported-information-creation, factivity-respecting attribution, standards-dependent assessment, Unobservable!=Underdetermined, Completeness!=Sufficiency, the Decision/Determination/Authorization/Action chain, CurrentState!=History, identity-preservation-under-state-change, and inquiry-relative Zero.

rows.anchor: Use at least 10,000 trials per major property family ... But DO NOT interpret the result as a population estimate about the real world. Monte Carlo uncertainty describes the simulator/generator. ... Always audit vacuity. If: guard_active = 0 then: 100% pass means nothing.
rows.statement: Mandates Monte Carlo requirements (>=10,000 trials per major property family where computationally reasonable) explicitly forbidding interpretation as a real-world population estimate (Monte Carlo uncertainty describes only the simulator/generator), and mandates an always-run vacuity audit (guard_active=0 makes a 100% pass rate meaningless) -- directly carrying forward the vacuity-audit discipline discovered in the earlier kernel-reduction experiment.

rows.anchor: For every successful property identify exactly where the tested capability came from. Detect hidden capabilities embedded in: world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function. Particularly inspect: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate.
rows.statement: Mandates a No-Smuggling Audit for every successful property, tracing exactly where the tested capability actually came from and checking nine possible hidden-capability locations (world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function), with particular scrutiny of nine named operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate) -- directly carrying forward the semantic-smuggling discipline from the kernel-reduction experiment.

rows.anchor: The test oracle must not simply duplicate the implementation. Where possible: implementation_under_test != evaluator. ... If an oracle necessarily relies on a theory definition, mark the result as partly definitional. Distinguish: empirical simulation evidence from: logical consequence of the implementation.
rows.statement: Mandates Oracle Independence: the test oracle must not simply duplicate the implementation under test; where an oracle necessarily relies on a theory definition, the result must be marked partly definitional, explicitly distinguishing empirical simulation evidence from mere logical consequence of the implementation.

rows.anchor: For every type specify: Input, Output, Dependencies, Allowed transformations, Forbidden substitutions. Identify any type collision. Especially inspect notation collisions involving: P H E K S C R M I Q. If notation must change, document it. Do NOT silently change the theory.
rows.statement: Mandates a Formal Type Check constructing a complete type table over 24 named types (RealityState through Identity) each specified with input/output/dependencies/allowed-transformations/forbidden-substitutions, with explicit inspection for notation collisions among the heavily overloaded single-letter symbols P, H, E, K, S, C, R, M, I, Q -- any notation change must be documented, never silently applied to the theory.

rows.anchor: Explicitly search for circular definitions. At minimum test: Knowledge defined using Truth, Truth inferred from Knowledge. Semantic equivalence defined using behavior, Behavior defined using semantic equivalence. Adequacy defined using Satisfaction, Satisfaction defined using Adequacy. ... If circularity exists: do NOT repair silently. Report: CIRCULARITY-ID, Definition A, Definition B, Why circular, Whether harmless definitional recursion or fatal circularity, Possible independent grounding.
rows.statement: Mandates a Circularity Audit explicitly testing five named candidate circular-definition pairs (Knowledge/Truth, Semantic-equivalence/Behavior, Adequacy/Satisfaction, Determination/Knowledge, Zero/Gap), with any detected circularity reported (never silently repaired) via a structured record distinguishing harmless definitional recursion from fatal circularity and naming a possible independent grounding.

rows.anchor: If any proposition fails: DO NOT hide it. DO NOT modify the generator until the failure disappears. First preserve the counterexample. Then classify: theory failure, implementation failure, test oracle failure, generator artifact, missing assumption, ambiguous semantics, representation problem, genuine unresolved research question. Negative results must receive permanent IDs.
rows.statement: States the negative-results-are-first-class-results discipline: a failing proposition must never be hidden or eliminated by tweaking the generator; the counterexample must be preserved first, then classified into one of eight named failure categories, and every negative result assigned a permanent ID.

rows.anchor: The experiment is successful only if ALL of the following can be shown: S1..S17 ... Even if every test passes: Do NOT write: "The KnowledgeOS theory is proven." Write instead: "[EXP] The current theory survived the tested simulation conditions." ... simulation success != mathematical proof != empirical validation of real-world knowledge != production architecture validation != kernel minimality proof.
rows.statement: Defines seventeen named success criteria S1-S17 (full lifecycle execution, semantic distinctions remain operationally distinct, no fabricated knowledge from incomplete evidence, unresolved competing hypotheses, target-relative evidence assessment, representable evidence dependence, explicit standards/model assumptions, distinct knowledge attribution, inquiry-relative adequacy without K_t change, traceable history, semantically-equivalent-representations produce equivalent behaviour, capability-first kernel testing, no unexplained information creation, distinct decision/authorization/action, inquiry-relative Zero, distinguishable unknown-taxonomy), immediately followed by an explicit discipline that even universal success must never be reported as 'the theory is proven' but only as 'the current theory survived the tested simulation conditions' -- with four explicit non-equivalences (simulation success != mathematical proof, != empirical real-world validation, != production architecture validation, != kernel minimality proof).

rows.anchor: A. EXECUTIVE RESULT ... B. FORMAL MODEL ... C. TYPE SYSTEM ... D. SCENARIO CATALOG ... E. PROPERTY CATALOG ... F. TEST RESULTS ... G. COUNTEREXAMPLE REGISTER ... H. NO-SMUGGLING REGISTER ... I. CIRCULARITY REGISTER ... J. PROOF-OBLIGATION REGISTER ... K. KERNEL RESULT ... L. THEORY GAP REGISTER ... G1 Mathematical ... G9 Governance.
rows.statement: Mandates twelve required output artifacts (A Executive Result through L Theory Gap Register), with the Kernel Result artifact (K) explicitly forbidden from reporting a bare operator count (must report semantic capability set, candidate reductions, derivable capabilities, irreducible candidates, representation-dependent results, semantic-equivalence results, and remaining minimality questions instead), and the Theory Gap Register (L) required to classify every remaining gap into one of nine named classes (G1 Mathematical, G2 Semantic, G3 Epistemological, G4 Statistical, G5 DDD, G6 Computational, G7 Empirical, G8 Architectural, G9 Governance).

rows.anchor: # 6. KERNEL STATUS ... NOT TESTED, PARTIALLY TESTED, SUPPORTED, UNRESOLVED, REFUTED UNDER CURRENT MODEL. # 7. THEORY STATUS Choose exactly one: A. INCONSISTENT B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE C. INTERNALLY COHERENT UNDER TESTED CONDITIONS D. STRONGLY SUPPORTED BUT NOT PROVED. Do not choose D merely because the tests pass.
rows.statement: Mandates a seven-part final verdict format (established/strongly-supported/failed/open/cannot-establish/kernel-status/theory-status/next-experiment), with Kernel Status restricted to five named values (never a bare operator count) and Theory Status restricted to exactly one of four deliberately conservative choices (INCONSISTENT, PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE, INTERNALLY COHERENT UNDER TESTED CONDITIONS, STRONGLY SUPPORTED BUT NOT PROVED), with an explicit warning against choosing the strongest option merely because tests pass.

rows.anchor: The goal is NOT to prove that the KnowledgeOS theory is correct. The goal is to discover whether the theory survives contact with an executable formal model. ... Preserve uncertainty. Preserve competing interpretations. Preserve counterexamples. Preserve provenance. Never convert experimental success into canon.
rows.statement: States the closing Final Scientific Principle: the goal is not to prove the theory correct but to discover whether it survives contact with an executable formal model, with the strongest possible outcome being a precise map of what is definitionally established, derivable, simulation-supported, failed, or genuinely open -- never converting experimental success into canon, always preserving uncertainty, competing interpretations, counterexamples, and provenance.

rows.anchor: In particular, I would **not** let Claude declare a "minimal kernel" from this experiment merely because it gets, say, 12 or 13 operators. The previous experiment showed why that is unsafe: operator cardinality changed when semantic granularity changed. The new experiment should establish the **capability contract first**
rows.statement: States the file's rationale for the whole protocol: the earlier kernel-reduction experiment showed operator cardinality changes with semantic granularity, so this new experiment must establish the capability contract first and only then ask whether different implementations realize the same capabilities -- explicitly refusing to let a bare operator count (e.g. 12 or 13) be declared a minimal kernel.

rows.anchor: 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL in the deterministic suite ... this is the *weakest* outcome, not the strongest.
rows.statement: Deterministic suite across 10 scenarios x 20 properties yields 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL(CIRC-5)/2 DEFINITIONAL, but the report explicitly warns this is the weakest evidence in the paper because deterministic passes can be vacuous.

rows.anchor: Any of this describes real knowledge | STILL REQUIRING EMPIRICAL VALIDATION | the world is synthetic; nothing here is evidence about actual epistemic practice
rows.statement: Explicitly grades every simulation result as providing no empirical evidence about real epistemic practice, since the tested world is synthetic.

rows.anchor: The non-circularity and the impossibility are the same fact. Because truth never re-enters the agent's state, Gamma cannot consult it -- which is exactly why CE-1 occurs.
rows.statement: CIRC-1 (Knowledge-via-Truth / Truth-via-Knowledge) is found NOT circular, and this non-circularity is identified as the same underlying fact that produces CE-1: World.truth is exogenous and no agent transition reads it, so Gamma structurally cannot be factive.

rows.anchor: TG-13 | The kernel shape (P, R, delta, I, U) proposed by the prior lane was not tested | G8 architectural | out of scope | MEDIUM
rows.statement: Registers TG-13: the prior kernel-reduction lane's proposed kernel shape (preservation vector, relations, transition function, invariants, uncertainty) was never tested by this simulation, kept explicitly out of scope.

rows.anchor: The theory executes the whole epistemic lifecycle and keeps every distinction it declares -- except that DEF-1 (factivity) and the v1.1 attribution equation K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) cannot both hold. Theory status: B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE.
rows.statement: States the one-line headline result for the whole v1.1 simulation lane and its Theory Status verdict (B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE), restated from the FINAL-VERDICT artifact.

rows.anchor: Status [EXP] -- simulation of the theory, not of the product. Not canonical architecture, not a production implementation, not a final kernel, not a proven theory, not a validated ontology.
rows.statement: Explicitly disclaims canonical, production, kernel, proof, or ontology status for the entire simulation lane, framing it strictly as a simulation of the theory.

rows.anchor: Determination is genuinely set-valued. |A| = 0, 1, >1 are three observably different outcomes, and Reject(H1) never produced Accept(H2).
rows.statement: Establishes that determination is genuinely set-valued (zero, one, or many admissible answers are three distinct observable outcomes) and that rejection never silently produces acceptance of an alternative.

rows.anchor: Both v1.1 failures persist -- and v1.2 makes one of them better reported. ... v1.2 splits into 1 violated (rs) + 6 undetermined. The failure is identical; the report is strictly more informative.
rows.statement: Details result 4 (E3): CE-1 factivity and CE-3 revision both persist under v1.2 unrepaired, but three-valued Sat improves diagnostic resolution (splitting one undifferentiated gap into 1 violated + 6 undetermined).

rows.anchor: INV-9 is stale by a factor of 25 [CORPUS] ... My 00-CORPUS-INVENTORY.md recorded 3 .py files in the whole docs/knowledgeos/ tree ... Measured today: docs/knowledgeos/**.py 77 (was 3), repo-root research/**.py 68, 7384 LOC, JSON result files 122. And it executes. I ran it: $ cd research/knowledgeos-sim && python3 run_v12.py ... DONE. INV-9 WITHDRAWN. An executable theory simulation exists, is reproducible, and I reproduced it.
rows.statement: Withdraws the auditor's own prior finding INV-9 ('nothing executable exists') as stale by a factor of 25 in Python file count (3 -> 77 in docs/knowledgeos/, plus 68 more at repo-root totaling 7384 LOC and 122 JSON result files); personally executed research/knowledgeos-sim/run_v12.py and observed it produce five result JSON files (v12_E1_zero_readings.json through v12_E5_zero_ontology.json), confirming an executable theory simulation exists and is reproducible.

lineage_claims.target: the auditor's own prior INV-9 finding ('nothing executable exists')
lineage_claims.quote: INV-9 WITHDRAWN

experiment.hypothesis: an executable KnowledgeOS theory simulation exists and can be reproduced
experiment.setup: navigate to research/knowledgeos-sim and run run_v12.py
experiment.assumptions: the script's dependencies are satisfied in the auditor's environment
experiment.inputs: the existing run_v12.py script and its inputs
experiment.method: direct execution and observation of console output and produced files
experiment.result: the script completed and wrote five result JSON files (v12_E1_zero_readings.json ... v12_E5_zero_ontology.json), printing DONE
experiment.interpretation: the theory simulation is genuinely executable and reproducible, not merely described
experiment.limitations: confirms execution of one script; does not itself validate the theory content the simulation tests
experiment.conclusion: INV-9 WITHDRAWN

lexical.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.

formal.anchor: K_t = Gamma(E_t, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) where Gamma determines which parts of the epistemic state qualify as Knowledge State content ... Knowledge remains factive: Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t). Do NOT operationally assume that the simulation can magically observe objective truth. If truth is externally supplied by the simulation world, explicitly label that as world-state information and keep it separate from the agent's epistemic state.

operational.anchor: Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, Knowledge State K_t, Inquiry Q, Ideal State I_t, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision, Supersession. ... test whether these are genuinely distinct conceptual roles or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.

governance.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The non-circularity and the impossibility are the same fact. Because truth never re-enters the agent's state, Gamma cannot consult it -- which is exactly why CE-1 occurs.
rationale_evidence.statement: CIRC-1 (Knowledge-via-Truth / Truth-via-Knowledge) is found NOT circular, and this non-circularity is identified as the same underlying fact that produces CE-1: World.truth is exogenous and no agent transition reads it, so Gamma structurally cannot be factive.

aliases: Step 22: Identity, Lineage, Provenance, Causality, and Traceability

sources.note: S0879's Step 22: five-way Identity/Provenance/Lineage/Causality/Traceability separation; EntityIdentity!=EntityState; Provenance!=Source; Lineage as dependency/derivation graph distinct from causation; three never-conflated graphs (G_L/G_P/G_C) unified as one typed epistemic graph; append-only history with no retroactive rewriting; Reconstructability as the headline architectural result (ten reconstructable questions); Integrity!=Truth, Authenticity!=Authority!=Reliability; 17 invariants across six letter-prefixed groups; hands off to Step 23 (epistemic sufficiency/readiness/completeness/knowledge boundary), which revisits the Step 13 sufficiency theme.

rows.anchor:
KnowledgeOS can accumulate a very sophisticated collection of facts while losing the ability to reconstruct history. Identity 
eq Provenance 
eq Lineage 
eq Causality 
eq Traceability. They are related, but they are not the same concept.
rows.statement: States the governing five-way separation Identity≠Provenance≠Lineage≠Causality≠Traceability, warning that without it a system can have sophisticated facts yet be unable to reconstruct history.

rows.anchor: The fundamental problem ... Nexus was upgraded. Which Nexus? Which version was it before? Which version is it now? What evidence established the old version? ... Did the upgrade cause the observed change? What happened afterward? This is not one graph edge. It is a chain: Entity → Observation → Evid
rows.statement: Lists twelve questions a bare statement like 'Nexus was upgraded' must answer, establishing this is a full chain (Entity→Observation→Evidence→Knowledge→Decision→Authorization→Action→Outcome→Observation), not one graph edge.

rows.anchor: Identity ... E=(EntityID,Type,Context,Identifiers,Attributes,IdentityEvidence,Validity). ... Entity identity is not its attributes ... Nexus_123 changes Version:3.69→3.72. It remains the same entity. EntityIdentity\neq EntityState. ... Identity versus state ... ID(e)=constant while State(e,t) change
rows.statement: Defines Entity=(EntityID,Type,Context,Identifiers,Attributes,IdentityEvidence,Validity) with EntityIdentity≠EntityState — a version change (3.69→3.72) does not create a new entity, preventing state changes from becoming false identity changes.

rows.anchor: Identity is contextual ... Infrastructure: NexusHost, Application: RepositoryService, Security: ExternalEndpoint. These may all refer to the same underlying entity. ContextualRepresentation\neq UnderlyingIdentity. ... Identity resolution ... ResolveIdentity(x,y,C) \rightarrow \{Same,Distinct,Unknown
rows.statement: Reaffirms context-specific representations of one underlying entity (ContextualRepresentation≠UnderlyingIdentity), defining three-valued ResolveIdentity(x,y,C)→{Same,Distinct,Unknown}.

rows.anchor: Identity evidence ... DNS(FQDN)\rightarrow IP and HostConfiguration(IP)\rightarrow Nexus. IdentityResolution is itself epistemic knowledge. This connects Step 22 directly to Steps 19–20. ... Identity confidence ... not simply store identity_confidence = 0.93 unless there is a defined probabilistic b
rows.statement: States identity resolution is itself epistemic knowledge (connecting to Steps 19-20), requiring a structured IdentityAssessment=(Evidence,MatchingCriteria,Conflicts,Status) with a five-value status enum instead of a bare confidence scalar.

rows.anchor: Provenance ... Where did this particular piece of information come from? Provenance(x) as the history of the origin and derivation of x. P=(Origin,Agent,Activity,Source,Time,Transformation,ParentObjects). ... Provenance is not source ... Source document → Text extraction → LLM interpretation → Candi
rows.statement: Defines Provenance P=(Origin,Agent,Activity,Source,Time,Transformation,ParentObjects), distinguishing it from Source (where information was obtained) — Source⊆Provenance conceptually but Source≠Provenance, since provenance covers the entire transformation chain.

rows.anchor: Lineage ... What was derived from what? E_1 → A_1 → D_1 → Action_1. Lineage(x)=Ancestors(x)\cup Descendants(x). ... Provenance versus lineage ... Provenance How an artifact came to exist. Lineage The dependency/derivation graph between artifacts. Provenance \supseteq Origin+Transformation+Agent+Time
rows.statement: Defines Lineage(x)=Ancestors(x)∪Descendants(x), distinguishing it from Provenance: Provenance is how an artifact came to exist, Lineage is the dependency/derivation graph between artifacts.

rows.anchor: Causality ... Decision → Action → Outcome. This establishes an operational sequence. It does not automatically prove causality. A\prec B does not imply A\rightarrow_c B. Sequence\neq Causality. ... Causal relation ... P(B\mid do(A)) rather than merely P(B\mid A). ... Example ... Upgrade\prec Failure
rows.statement: Reaffirms Sequence≠Causality using do(A) notation, illustrated by an upgrade-then-failure sequence that must be represented only as a CandidateCausalRelation given five alternative explanations.

rows.anchor: Causal evidence ... controlled intervention; natural experiment; causal model; temporal mechanism; counterfactual analysis; repeated observations; domain mechanism. The strength depends on the context. ... Causal provenance ... CausalAssertion=(Cause,Effect,Mechanism,Evidence,Model,Assumptions,Tempo
rows.statement: Defines CausalAssertion=(Cause,Effect,Mechanism,Evidence,Model,Assumptions,TemporalScope,Status) drawing on seven kinds of causal evidence, making causal reasoning auditable.

rows.anchor: Event identity ... Event=(EventID,Type,Actor,Subject,Time,PreState,PostState,Evidence). ... Event versus state ... An event is something that happened. A state describes what is true afterward. Event\neq State. ... State transition ... S_{t+1}=T(S_t,e). For uncertain outcomes P(S_{t+1}\mid S_t,e). .
rows.statement: Defines Event=(EventID,Type,Actor,Subject,Time,PreState,PostState,Evidence) with Event≠State, and a state transition function S_{t+1}=T(S_t,e), stating ModeledTransition≠EmpiricallyEstablishedCausality — the system's own transition model does not itself prove real-world causation.

rows.anchor: Traceability ... Can we travel from one important object to all relevant objects connected to it? Traceability = Reachability through governed relationships. ... Traceability is directional ... Backward traceability Why did we make this decision? Decision → Knowledge → Evidence → Source. Forward tra
rows.statement: Defines Traceability=Reachability through governed relationships, requiring both backward (why?) and forward (what did it cause?) directions.

rows.anchor: The trace graph ... Source ↓ Evidence ↓ Assertion ↓ Knowledge ↓ Discrepancy ↓ Candidate Action ↓ Decision ↓ Authorization ↓ Action ↓ Outcome ↓ Observation ↓ Evidence. But this is not merely a graph database. The edges have semantics. ... Typed trace relationships ... DerivedFrom, SupportedBy, Contra
rows.statement: Assembles the full trace graph from Source through Evidence/Assertion/Knowledge/Discrepancy/Decision/Authorization/Action/Outcome/Observation, requiring eleven distinct typed edge kinds that must not be interchangeable.

rows.anchor: Causal edge versus provenance edge ... Decision BasedOn Evidence. That is provenance. Action Caused Outcome. That is causal. BasedOn\neq Caused. A graph that merely has an edge A\rightarrow B is semantically insufficient. ... Derivation versus causation ... A DerivedFrom B means A was derived from B
rows.statement: States BasedOn ≠ Caused and DerivedFrom ⇏ causal (B→_c A), warning an untyped graph edge A→B is semantically insufficient — a conclusion derived from evidence does not mean the evidence caused the underlying real-world event.

rows.anchor: Decision causality ... Evidence → Decision. The decision was based on the evidence. But whether the evidence caused the decision in a psychological or organizational sense is a different proposition. DecisionDependency\neq PsychologicalCausation.
rows.statement: Distinguishes DecisionDependency (evidence the decision was based on) from PsychologicalCausation (whether the evidence caused the decision in a human sense).

rows.anchor: Lineage graph ... G_L=(V,E_L) ... Provenance graph ... G_P=(V,E_P) ... Causal graph ... G_C=(V,E_C) represents causal hypotheses/models. The three graphs should not be conflated. G_L\neq G_P\neq G_C. They may reference the same nodes. ... One integrated trace model ... G=(V,E_{semantic},E_{lineage},
rows.statement: Defines three distinct graphs (Lineage G_L, Provenance G_P, Causal G_C) that must never be conflated (though sharing nodes), combined architecturally into one typed epistemic graph G with five edge kinds.

rows.anchor: Temporal lineage ... ADR_1 may lead to ADR_2 which supersedes it. Supersedes(ADR_2,ADR_1) has temporal meaning. Historical lineage must remain intact. ... Immutable historical records ... EventLog=(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n). New events are appended. We do not rewrite e_i to make history look cleaner. Inst
rows.statement: Requires an append-only EventLog (no rewriting history to look cleaner), with CorrectionEvent/CorrectedBy superseding rather than erasing — Correction ≠ Deletion, preserving historical truth about what the system previously believed.

rows.anchor: Knowledge history ... K_{t+1} = Transition(K_t,e_{t+1}). Historical snapshots can be reconstructed. ... Snapshot reproducibility ... K_t=T(K_0,e_1,\ldots,e_t). This allows KnowledgeOS to answer: What did we know on August 10? rather than: What do we know now about August 10? Those are different ques
rows.statement: Reaffirms historical snapshot reconstruction K_t=T(K_0,e_1,...,e_t), distinguishing 'what did we know then' from 'what do we now believe about then' — different questions.

rows.anchor: Decision reproducibility ... D_t should reference K_t. Decision_t \not\leftarrow CurrentKnowledge. It depends on the knowledge snapshot actually available at decision time. ... Preventing hindsight contamination ... K_{10} suggested migration was safe. K_{15} shows a serious previously unknown risk.
rows.statement: Requires decisions reference their actual historical knowledge snapshot, never current knowledge — worked example (K10 vs K15) establishing 'no retrospective knowledge leakage' as a major epistemic invariant.

rows.anchor: Decision lineage ... DecisionLineage=(KnowledgeSnapshot,EvidenceSet,Rules,Models,Goals,Constraints,Authority). This allows complete reconstruction. ... Action lineage ... Action \rightarrow Decision. But execution may differ from the decision. ExecutionDeviation must be represented. ... Decision ver
rows.statement: Defines DecisionLineage=(KnowledgeSnapshot,EvidenceSet,Rules,Models,Goals,Constraints,Authority) for complete reconstruction, requiring ExecutionDeviation be represented when actual execution (a rollback) differs from the original decision.

rows.anchor: Outcome lineage ... Outcome → Action → Decision → KnowledgeSnapshot. Now we can ask: What knowledge and decision produced this outcome? ... Causal attribution ... Did the decision actually produce the outcome? CausalHypothesis: Decision→Outcome. Status: Candidate until sufficient evidence exists. Th
rows.statement: Chains Outcome→Action→Decision→KnowledgeSnapshot, and treats whether a decision actually caused its outcome as its own epistemic claim (CausalHypothesis, Candidate until evidenced Supported/Rejected).

rows.anchor: Counterfactual traceability ... What would have happened if we had chosen the alternative? Outcome(do(a_1)) versus Outcome(do(a_2)). KnowledgeOS may model this using causal models. But it must distinguish ObservedOutcome from CounterfactualOutcome. ... Counterfactual provenance ... Observed: No. Mod
rows.statement: Requires ObservedOutcome be distinguished from CounterfactualOutcome, recording a candidate counterfactual with explicit model/assumptions rather than storing hypothetical reasoning as observed fact.

rows.anchor: Traceability query ... Trace(x,direction,relationTypes) \rightarrow Subgraph. Trace(Decision_{123},Backward) returns Decision, Goal, Knowledge Snapshot, Assertion, Evidence, Source, Rule, Constraint, Authorization. ... Forward trace ... Trace(Decision_{123},Forward) returns Decision → Action → Execu
rows.statement: Defines the computable query Trace(x,direction,relationTypes)→Subgraph, worked with backward (why) and forward (what caused) trace examples over a decision node.

rows.anchor: Blast-radius analysis ... If this assertion is retracted, what depends on it? Dependents(A). Impact(A) = Reachable(A,E_{depends}). This allows knowledge blast-radius analysis. ... Example ... A: NexusVersion=3.69 supported D_1: UpgradeRequired which led to Action_1: Migration. If A is later found in
rows.statement: Defines Impact(A)=Reachable(A,E_depends) enabling knowledge blast-radius analysis, worked with an example tracing a retracted version assertion through the decision and action it drove.

rows.anchor: Provenance-aware re-evaluation ... A_{old}\rightarrow A_{new}, KnowledgeOS can find affected decisions AffectedDecisions(A). Then Reevaluate(D_i). This creates an intelligent governance loop. ... This connects to Zero ... A critical premise supporting the current decision has become invalid. Knowled
rows.statement: Extends Zero (detecting when a premise supporting a decision becomes invalid, KnowledgeChange→DependencyImpact→Discrepancy), Lord (prioritizing evidence by downstream impact count), and Sārathi (triggering DecisionReview for affected decisions) using the lineage/impact machinery.

rows.anchor: DDD aggregate boundaries ... Identity Context ... Provenance Context ... Lineage Context ... Event Context ... Causal Context ... Traceability Context. This is cleaner than putting everything into one giant "KnowledgeGraph" aggregate. ... Identity ownership ... Only the Identity Context owns canonic
rows.statement: Proposes six bounded contexts (Identity/Provenance/Lineage/Event/Causal/Traceability) instead of one giant KnowledgeGraph aggregate; only the Identity Context owns canonical identity (others reference EntityID); Provenance is a first-class domain concern, not mere created_by/created_at CRUD metadata.

rows.anchor: Traceability versus audit logging ... Audit log Who changed this record? Provenance How did this knowledge artifact arise? Traceability What does this artifact depend on and what depends on it? Audit\neq Provenance\neq Traceability.
rows.statement: Distinguishes three related but different capabilities: Audit log (who changed a record), Provenance (how an artifact arose), Traceability (dependency reachability) — Audit≠Provenance≠Traceability.

rows.anchor: Cryptographic integrity ... h_x=Hash(x). HashChain: h_i=Hash(h_{i-1}\Vert x_i). This allows tamper detection. But Integrity\neq Truth. A perfectly preserved false statement is still false. This is another critical invariant. ... Signature versus authority ... DigitalSignature(x) proves that a holder
rows.statement: Defines a hash-chain integrity mechanism (h_i=Hash(h_{i-1}‖x_i)) for tamper detection, stating Integrity ≠ Truth (a perfectly preserved false statement is still false), Authenticity ≠ Authority ≠ Truth, and Authenticity ≠ Reliability (a properly signed document can still be outdated).

rows.anchor: The complete lineage object ... L=(NodeID,ParentNodes,RelationType,Agent,Activity,Time,Context,Version,Evidence) where RelationType specifies whether the relationship is derived; based-on; generated-by; superseded-by; caused-by; observed-by; authorized-by; executed-by.
rows.statement: Defines the complete Lineage object L=(NodeID,ParentNodes,RelationType,Agent,Activity,Time,Context,Version,Evidence) with eight named relationship types.

rows.anchor: Identity graph ... G_I=(E,R_I) where E are entity representations and R_I are identity relationships. SameAs, Represents, AliasOf, ContextualRepresentationOf, FormerIdentityOf. Again, these must be typed. ... Identity evolution ... E_1,E_2 \rightarrow E_3. Or E_1 \rightarrow E_2,E_3. This occurs in
rows.statement: Defines a typed Identity graph G_I=(E,R_I) with five relation types, allowing entity merge/split transitions, requiring an IdentityResolutionEvent record rather than silently erasing a prior distinct-identity belief when later evidence shows entities were the same.

rows.anchor: Mathematical closure of Step 22 ... Identity I(x,y,C,t) \rightarrow \{Same,Distinct,Unknown\} ... State transition S_{t+1}=T(S_t,e_t) ... Lineage G_L=(V,E_L) ... Provenance G_P=(V,E_P) ... Causal model G_C=(V,E_C) ... Traceability Trace(x,R,d) \rightarrow Subgraph ... Dependency impact Impact(x)=Rea
rows.statement: Consolidates the Step 22 mathematical closure: identity resolution, state transition, three named graphs (lineage/provenance/causal), traceability query, dependency impact, and causal intervention — declared mathematically distinct operations.

Step 22 invariants ... I1 EntityIdentity

rows.statement: States seventeen candidate invariants grouped I1-I3 (identity), P1-P2 (provenance), L1-L2 (lineage), C1-C2 (causality), T1-T3 (traceability), and H1-H6 (historical/integrity), covering identity/state separation, epistemic identity resolution, provenance preservation, typed lineage, derivation≠causation, temporal-order≠causality, bidirectional traceability, no silent rewriting, no retroactive contamination, correction-not-destruction, and integrity/authenticity/authority/reliability all distinct.

rows.anchor: The major architectural result ... Reconstructability. What did we know? K_t Why did we believe it? Evidence+Provenance What semantic interpretation did we use? OntologyVersion What rules were active? RuleVersion What decision did we make? D_t Why? DecisionLineage What did we do? Action_t What actua
rows.statement: States Reconstructability as the major architectural result of Step 22 — ten explicitly answerable historical questions (what did we know, why, what semantics/rules were active, what decision/action/outcome, what changed) — distinguishing KnowledgeOS from ordinary RAG systems.

rows.anchor: The complete KnowledgeOS loop is now much stronger ... Reality \xrightarrow{Event} State \xrightarrow{Observation} Evidence \xrightarrow{Assessment} Assertion ... KnowledgeState \xrightarrow{Reasoning} DerivedKnowledge ... Discrepancy+Goal \xrightarrow{Lord} CandidateActions ... Decision \xrightarro
rows.statement: Assembles the complete Steps 1-22 architecture loop with ten cross-cutting dimensions surrounding it (Identity, Semantics, Time, Evidence, Provenance, Lineage, Causality, Authority, Uncertainty, Governance).

rows.anchor: Step 22 verdict ... FOUNDATIONALLY RESOLVED ... we have defined the mathematical and domain semantics, not yet selected the implementation technologies. We should not yet decide: graph database; event store; RDF; property graph; relational representation; W3C PROV; OWL; SHACL; causal inference libra
rows.statement: Declares Step 22 foundationally resolved at the domain-semantics level, explicitly deferring ten implementation technology choices (graph DB, event store, RDF, OWL, SHACL, vector DB, etc.) as separate from the domain model.

rows.anchor: What has changed since Step 1 ... an AI knowledge system. That description is now far too weak. A governed epistemic operating system for organizations. It does not merely retrieve knowledge. It maintains Identity → Meaning → Evidence → Knowledge → Reasoning → Discrepancy → Decision → Action → Outco
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS has evolved past 'an AI knowledge system' description into 'a governed epistemic operating system for organizations' maintaining a ten-stage Identity→Meaning→Evidence→Knowledge→Reasoning→Discrepancy→Decision→Action→Outcome→Learning chain, preserving the why behind every transition.

rows.anchor: One remaining foundational issue ... K may be perfectly adequate to answer "What version of Nexus is currently installed?" but completely inadequate to answer "Is it safe and authorized to migrate Nexus tomorrow?" This means we need a formal concept of Epistemic Sufficiency / Readiness. Not simply c
rows.statement: Poses Step 23: formalize Epistemic Sufficiency/Readiness/Completeness/Knowledge Boundary — when KnowledgeOS knows enough, and when it must stop, ask for more, escalate, or refuse to act, illustrated by a version-query being adequate while a migration-safety question is not.
