rationale_evidence.anchor: The fundamental problem ... Nexus was upgraded. Which Nexus? Which version was it before? Which version is it now? What evidence established the old version? ... Did the upgrade cause the observed change? What happened afterward? This is not one graph edge. It is a chain: Entity → Observation → Evid
rationale_evidence.statement: Lists twelve questions a bare statement like 'Nexus was upgraded' must answer, establishing this is a full chain (Entity→Observation→Evidence→Knowledge→Decision→Authorization→Action→Outcome→Observation), not one graph edge.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Identity evidence ... DNS(FQDN)\rightarrow IP and HostConfiguration(IP)\rightarrow Nexus. IdentityResolution is itself epistemic knowledge. This connects Step 22 directly to Steps 19–20. ... Identity confidence ... not simply store identity_confidence = 0.93 unless there is a defined probabilistic b
rationale_evidence.statement: States identity resolution is itself epistemic knowledge (connecting to Steps 19-20), requiring a structured IdentityAssessment=(Evidence,MatchingCriteria,Conflicts,Status) with a five-value status enum instead of a bare confidence scalar.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Causality ... Decision → Action → Outcome. This establishes an operational sequence. It does not automatically prove causality. A\prec B does not imply A\rightarrow_c B. Sequence\neq Causality. ... Causal relation ... P(B\mid do(A)) rather than merely P(B\mid A). ... Example ... Upgrade\prec Failure
rationale_evidence.statement: Reaffirms Sequence≠Causality using do(A) notation, illustrated by an upgrade-then-failure sequence that must be represented only as a CandidateCausalRelation given five alternative explanations.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Outcome lineage ... Outcome → Action → Decision → KnowledgeSnapshot. Now we can ask: What knowledge and decision produced this outcome? ... Causal attribution ... Did the decision actually produce the outcome? CausalHypothesis: Decision→Outcome. Status: Candidate until sufficient evidence exists. Th
rationale_evidence.statement: Chains Outcome→Action→Decision→KnowledgeSnapshot, and treats whether a decision actually caused its outcome as its own epistemic claim (CausalHypothesis, Candidate until evidenced Supported/Rejected).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Blast-radius analysis ... If this assertion is retracted, what depends on it? Dependents(A). Impact(A) = Reachable(A,E_{depends}). This allows knowledge blast-radius analysis. ... Example ... A: NexusVersion=3.69 supported D_1: UpgradeRequired which led to Action_1: Migration. If A is later found in
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines Impact(A)=Reachable(A,E_depends) enabling knowledge blast-radius analysis, worked with an example tracing a retracted version assertion through the decision and action it drove.

aliases: Step 25A.3: Knowledge-State Revision, Conflict, Temporal Validity and Retraction

sources.note: S0888's Step 25A.3: twelve lettered experiments (A-L) testing knowledge revision; K_t historically immutable / K_current revisable; WorldEvolution!=KnowledgeRevision in both directions with a KnowledgeLag metric; refined four-way Conflict predicate; Delete vs Invalidate distinction; three temporal states Valid/Superseded/Invalid; monotonic history vs non-monotonic content; no-silent-revision and Replayability invariants; eleven state-transition operations; six candidate bounded contexts; verdicts CONCEPTUALLY PASSED with three remaining algebra gaps; hands off to Step 25A.4 (Executable Knowledge-State Model).

rows.anchor: Now we test whether the knowledge state remains mathematically coherent when knowledge changes. Can KnowledgeOS revise its knowledge without destroying history, hiding contradictions, or confusing changes in reality with changes in knowledge?
rows.statement: Frames Step 25A.3's governing question: whether KnowledgeOS can revise knowledge without destroying history, hiding contradictions, or confusing reality-change with knowledge-change.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1}=Revise(K_t,E_{t+1},C,t+1) ... This operator is one of the most important operators in the entire KnowledgeOS theory. If this cannot be made coherent, everything above it becomes unstable.
rows.statement: Defines the revision operator Revise(K_t,E_{t+1},C,t+1), called one of the most important operators in the whole theory since its incoherence would destabilize everything built above it.

rows.anchor: First principle: never rewrite history ... We must not mutate K_10. Instead K_10 \rightarrow K_11. K_t is historically immutable. while K_current is revisable. This gives us a clean separation between historical truth of the knowledge state and current epistemic belief.
rows.statement: States K_t is historically immutable while K_current is revisable, giving a clean separation between historical knowledge-state truth and current epistemic belief.

rows.anchor: Experiment A — Simple knowledge growth ... K_0=\varnothing. E_1: Version(Nexus)=3.69. K_1=\{A_1\}. K_0\xrightarrow{E_1}K_1. This is ordinary knowledge acquisition.
rows.statement: Works the baseline ordinary-knowledge-acquisition experiment A (single evidence item extending K0 to K1).

rows.anchor: Experiment B — World changes ... W_1: Version=3.69 to W_2: Version=3.72. This is not a contradiction in knowledge. It is a change in the world. Event: NexusUpgraded(3.69\rightarrow3.72). W_1 \xrightarrow{Event} W_2. KnowledgeOS subsequently observes this and updates K_1\rightarrow K_2. WorldEvolutio
rows.statement: Works experiment B distinguishing world-state evolution (an actual upgrade event) from knowledge revision — WorldEvolution ≠ KnowledgeRevision.

rows.anchor:
Experiment C — Apparent contradiction ... A_1: Version=3.69 valid at [t_1,t_2]. A_2: Version=3.72 valid at [t_3,\infty) with t_2<t_3. A_1
eq A_2 but they are not contradictory. Conflict(A_1,A_2)
eq A_1
eq A_2. Conflict requires overlapping semantic scope.
rows.statement: Works experiment C showing two successive non-overlapping-validity assertions are not conflicting despite differing values — Conflict requires overlapping semantic scope, not mere inequality.

rows.anchor: Conflict predicate ... Conflict(A_1,A_2) only if Incompatible(A_1,A_2) and Overlap(Context_1,Context_2) and Overlap(Time_1,Time_2) and Overlap(Scope_1,Scope_2). Conflict = Incompatibility \land ContextOverlap \land TemporalOverlap \land ScopeOverlap. This is a significant formal refinement.
rows.statement: Formalizes the refined Conflict predicate as a four-way conjunction (Incompatibility, ContextOverlap, TemporalOverlap, ScopeOverlap), a significant formal refinement over the earlier informal notion.

rows.anchor: Experiment D — Genuine contradiction ... ValidTime(A_1)=ValidTime(A_2). Then Conflict(A_1,A_2)=True. KnowledgeOS must represent K_t=\{A_1,A_2,Conflict(A_1,A_2)\} rather than arbitrarily deleting one. ... Why we should preserve both ... source A is an inventory; source B is a direct server query. If
rows.statement: Works experiment D with fully-overlapping validity times producing a genuine Conflict=True, requiring both assertions be preserved (K_t={A1,A2,Conflict}) rather than arbitrarily deleting either.

rows.anchor: Conflict resolution is not conflict deletion ... Resolve(C_1)\rightarrow A_2. We should not necessarily delete A_1. Instead A_1.status=Superseded or A_1.status=Rejected depending on what the evidence establishes. History remains available.
rows.statement: States conflict resolution must set the losing assertion's status to Superseded or Rejected, never delete it, preserving history.

rows.anchor: Experiment E — Retraction ... E_1 supported A_1. Later we discover that E_1 itself was invalid. We execute Retract(E_1). We cannot simply execute delete(E1) because E_1\rightarrow A_1 may have downstream dependencies. ... Dependency graph ... E_1\rightarrow A_1\rightarrow A_3\rightarrow Decision_1.
rows.statement: Works experiment E (retraction) tracing a four-hop dependency chain (evidence→assertion→derived assertion→decision) requiring cascading reevaluation, not blind deletion.

rows.anchor: Important distinction: deletion vs invalidation ... Delete(E) The system no longer stores this object. Invalidate(E) The system stores that this evidence must no longer support the relevant epistemic claims. For an auditable knowledge system, Invalidate is generally much more important than physical
rows.statement: Distinguishes Delete(E) (no longer stored) from Invalidate(E) (stored as no-longer-supporting), stating Invalidate is generally more important for an auditable knowledge system.

rows.anchor: Experiment F — Partial retraction ... A_1 has support from E_1,E_2,E_3. Now E_1 is invalidated. We must not automatically retract A_1. Instead Support(A_1)=\{E_2,E_3\}. Then reassess. Possibilities: StillSupported, WeaklySupported, Unsupported, Conflicted. This gives us a dependency-sensitive revisi
rows.statement: Works experiment F (partial evidence loss) requiring recomputed support {E2,E3} and reassessment into one of four states, rather than automatic retraction of the assertion.

rows.anchor: Experiment G — Derived knowledge ... A_1,A_2 \vdash A_3. If A_1 is retracted, A_3 must be reconsidered. Therefore derived knowledge needs DerivationLineage not merely source provenance. ... Three different dependency types ... Evidence support E\rightarrow A. Logical derivation A_1,A_2\vdash A_3. De
rows.statement: Works experiment G (derived knowledge from two premises) requiring a distinct DerivationLineage (not just source provenance), formalizing three separate dependency types (Support, Derivation, DecisionDependency).

rows.anchor: Experiment H — Temporal invalidation ... E_1 was valid at t_1. At t_2 the underlying reality changed. Does that mean E_1=False? No. It may remain valid evidence about W_{t_1}. ValidAt(E_1,t_1)=True while ValidAt(E_1,t_2)=False. This is temporal supersession, not evidence falsification. ... Three sta
rows.statement: Works experiment H distinguishing temporal supersession (ValidAt changes over time without falsification) from invalidation, defining three non-equivalent states Valid/Superseded/Invalid.

rows.anchor: Experiment I — Knowledge revision without world change ... Reality remains W_t: Version=3.69. But KnowledgeOS initially believes K_t: Version=3.72. New evidence reveals Version=3.69. The world did not change. Only K_t\rightarrow K_{t+1} changed. KnowledgeRevision \not\Rightarrow WorldStateChange.
rows.statement: Works experiment I showing knowledge revision can correct a prior mistaken belief without any world-state change — KnowledgeRevision ⇏ WorldStateChange.

rows.anchor: Experiment J — World change without immediate knowledge change ... W_t\rightarrow W_{t+1}. But KnowledgeOS receives no observation. Therefore K_t=K_{t+1} even though W_t\neq W_{t+1}. This is perhaps the most important epistemic property: RealityCanChangeWithoutKnowledgeChanging. This makes the disti
rows.statement: Works experiment J (the reverse case: world changes with no observation, so K_t=K_{t+1} despite W_t≠W_{t+1}), called perhaps the most important epistemic property, defining KnowledgeLag=t_observation-t_worldChange as a quality metric.

rows.anchor: Experiment K — Future information ... K_{t_0}: Rollback=Unknown. A migration decision occurs. At t_1>t_0 Rollback=False is discovered. The historical decision must still be evaluated using K_{t_0}. We must not rewrite history ... This is our anti-hindsight invariant: HistoricalDecision(D_{t_0}) depe
rows.statement: Works experiment K reaffirming the anti-hindsight invariant: a historical decision must be evaluated only against its actual historical knowledge snapshot.

rows.anchor: Experiment L — Contradiction resolution ... A_1: Version=3.69 supported by three dependent documents. And A_2: Version=3.72 supported by a direct current system query. A policy says: Direct current observation has precedence over stale derived documentation. Then Resolution(C) \rightarrow A_2. But w
rows.statement: Works experiment L (policy-driven conflict resolution favoring a direct current observation over dependent stale documents) while retaining the loser as historical/superseded — a governed resolution, not a mathematical truth function.

rows.anchor: First formal revision operator ... K_{t+1} = Revision(K_t,NewEvidence,Events,Rules,Context,Time) with the invariants: History(K_t)=Immutable, Provenance(K_{t+1})\supseteq RequiredHistory, Conflicts remain explicit, Invalidation propagates.
rows.statement: Refines the revision operator to Revision(K_t,NewEvidence,Events,Rules,Context,Time) with four invariants (immutable history, sufficient provenance, explicit conflicts, propagating invalidation).

rows.anchor: Candidate state representation ... K_t=(Assertions,Assessments,EvidenceRefs,Conflicts,Derivations,TemporalValidity,RevisionMetadata) with immutable historical snapshots K_0,K_1,\ldots,K_t. This is still PROVISIONAL but it is now strongly motivated by the experiments.
rows.statement: Refines the candidate KnowledgeState representation to seven fields (Assertions,Assessments,EvidenceRefs,Conflicts,Derivations,TemporalValidity,RevisionMetadata) with immutable snapshots, provisional but now strongly experiment-motivated.

rows.anchor: The knowledge-state transition graph ... New Evidence → Assessment → Support/Conflict/Reject → Commit/Resolve → KnowledgeState → Revision Event → New KnowledgeState. This is much closer to something we can actually implement.
rows.statement: Diagrams the full knowledge-state transition graph from New Evidence through Assessment, branching outcomes, Commit/Resolve, to Revision Event and New KnowledgeState.

rows.anchor: Critical invariant: monotonic history ... Current knowledge is non-monotonic: K_t\not\subseteq K_{t+1}. But history itself is monotonic. Once we have recorded K_t, we don't rewrite it. KnowledgeContent may be non-monotonic while KnowledgeHistory is monotonic. This is a very useful architectural prin
rows.statement: States the architectural principle KnowledgeContent may be non-monotonic while KnowledgeHistory is monotonic — content can shrink/change but the historical record only ever grows.

rows.anchor: Critical invariant: no silent revision ... K_t\rightarrow K_{t+1} \Rightarrow RevisionCause exists. A knowledge change must have an identifiable cause. The cause might be new evidence; invalidation; temporal event; policy change; ontology change; human correction; rule change. But there must be a tr
rows.statement: States no-silent-revision: every K_t→K_{t+1} transition must have an identifiable RevisionCause among seven listed kinds.

rows.anchor: Critical invariant: revision must be reproducible ... K_{t+1}=Revision(K_t,X) then an independent evaluator should be able to reproduce the transition from K_t+X+Rules. Replayability. It will become very important when we build the executable kernel.
rows.statement: States a Replayability requirement: any revision transition must be reproducible by an independent evaluator from K_t, the input X, and the rules.

rows.anchor: Critical invariant: revision is not necessarily truth correction ... K_t: A=True ... K_{t+1}: A=Unknown. That is perfectly valid. Knowledge revision does not always mean True\rightarrow False. It can mean Known\rightarrow Unknown. or Supported\rightarrow Conflicted. or HighConfidence\rightarrow LowC
rows.statement: States revision need not be True→False truth correction; it can equally be Known→Unknown, Supported→Conflicted, or HighConfidence→LowConfidence transitions.

rows.anchor: Our state transition algebra now needs at least these operations ... AddEvidence, AssessEvidence, CommitAssertion, CreateConflict, ResolveConflict, SupersedeAssertion, InvalidateEvidence, RetractAssertion, DeriveAssertion, RecalculateDependents, CreateSnapshot. These should become explicit domain op
rows.statement: Lists eleven required state-transition-algebra operations that must become explicit domain operations, not implicit database updates.

rows.anchor: DDD interpretation ... I would not make KnowledgeState a giant mutable aggregate containing the entire universe. Instead ... Evidence context Owns evidence identity, provenance and assessment. Knowledge context Owns assertion lifecycle and knowledge state. Revision context Owns transitions/revisions
rows.statement: Rejects a monolithic mutable KnowledgeState aggregate, proposing six candidate bounded contexts (Evidence, Knowledge, Revision, Temporal, Governance, Decision) each owning a distinct responsibility, provisional pending later bounded-context validation.

rows.anchor: Mathematical result of 25A.3 ... K_{t+1} = F(K_t,Evidence,Events,Rules,Context,Time) subject to HistoryImmutable, RevisionTraceable, ConflictExplicit, TemporalValidityExplicit, DependencyAware, UnknownPreserved.
rows.statement: Consolidates the mathematical result of 25A.3: K_{t+1}=F(K_t,Evidence,Events,Rules,Context,Time) subject to six named invariants.

rows.anchor: What passed? World and knowledge can evolve independently PASS. Historical snapshots can remain immutable PASS conceptually. Temporal apparent conflict can be distinguished from true conflict PASS conceptually. Genuine contradiction can be represented PASS. Retraction can be represented PASS concept
rows.statement: Delivers a ten-row 'what passed' table, all marked PASS or PASS conceptually, explicitly caveated as model-level passes only, not yet executable test results.

rows.anchor: What failed or remains incomplete? 1. Revision algebra We still need a precise definition of Revision(K,E). 2. Conflict algebra We know how to represent conflict, but not yet the complete resolution mathematics. 3. Dependency propagation We know that retraction must propagate, but the exact algorith
rows.statement: Identifies three genuine unresolved mathematical areas: the precise Revision(K,E) algebra, the complete conflict-resolution mathematics, and the exact dependency-propagation algorithm.

rows.anchor: A very important conclusion ... K_t is not simply {things we know}. A better model is: K_t = the governed epistemic state at time t, including what is currently supported; what is uncertain; what conflicts; what has been superseded; what has been derived; why each claim is held; when it is valid; wh
rows.statement: Refines the definition of K_t from 'things we know' to 'the governed epistemic state at time t', encompassing eight listed properties — a substantially stronger definition.

rows.anchor: 25A.3 Verdict ... CONCEPTUALLY PASSED with three mandatory mathematical refinements: Revision Algebra, Conflict Algebra, Dependency Propagation. And there is an important architectural conclusion: KnowledgeOS needs immutable historical knowledge states plus a revisable current projection. That gives
rows.statement: Verdicts Step 25A.3 CONCEPTUALLY PASSED with three mandatory refinements still needed, concluding KnowledgeOS needs both immutable historical states and a revisable current projection, giving Auditability plus Epistemic Revision.

rows.anchor: Next step ... I recommend not moving to Zero yet. The next experiment should be Step 25A.4 — Executable Knowledge-State Model. Here we take everything from 25A.1–25A.3 and actually construct a small state machine. We will give it: an initial empty knowledge state; evidence; assessments; assertions;
rows.statement: Proposes Step 25A.4 (Executable Knowledge-State Model): construct an actual small state machine covering ten listed features, to finally test whether the K_t→K_{t+1} transition can execute without violating invariants — the first move from thought experiment to genuinely executable experiment.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 25A.4 -- Executable Knowledge-State Model

lexical.anchor: Now we test whether the knowledge state remains mathematically coherent when knowledge changes. Can KnowledgeOS revise its knowledge without destroying history, hiding contradictions, or confusing changes in reality with changes in knowledge?

conceptual.anchor: The knowledge-state transition graph ... New Evidence → Assessment → Support/Conflict/Reject → Commit/Resolve → KnowledgeState → Revision Event → New KnowledgeState. This is much closer to something we can actually implement.

formal.anchor: Conflict predicate ... Conflict(A_1,A_2) only if Incompatible(A_1,A_2) and Overlap(Context_1,Context_2) and Overlap(Time_1,Time_2) and Overlap(Scope_1,Scope_2). Conflict = Incompatibility \land ContextOverlap \land TemporalOverlap \land ScopeOverlap. This is a significant formal refinement.

operational.anchor: Experiment A — Simple knowledge growth ... K_0=\varnothing. E_1: Version(Nexus)=3.69. K_1=\{A_1\}. K_0\xrightarrow{E_1}K_1. This is ordinary knowledge acquisition.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
Experiment C — Apparent contradiction ... A_1: Version=3.69 valid at [t_1,t_2]. A_2: Version=3.72 valid at [t_3,\infty) with t_2<t_3. A_1
eq A_2 but they are not contradictory. Conflict(A_1,A_2)
eq A_1
eq A_2. Conflict requires overlapping semantic scope.
rationale_evidence.statement: Works experiment C showing two successive non-overlapping-validity assertions are not conflicting despite differing values — Conflict requires overlapping semantic scope, not mere inequality.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Critical invariant: revision is not necessarily truth correction ... K_t: A=True ... K_{t+1}: A=Unknown. That is perfectly valid. Knowledge revision does not always mean True\rightarrow False. It can mean Known\rightarrow Unknown. or Supported\rightarrow Conflicted. or HighConfidence\rightarrow LowC
rationale_evidence.statement: States revision need not be True→False truth correction; it can equally be Known→Unknown, Supported→Conflicted, or HighConfidence→LowConfidence transitions.

sources.note: S0891's Step 25B: a full 34-sub-step Nexus-migration end-to-end simulation from goal definition through Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Governance/Execution/Outcome, with six deliberate adversarial injections; six epistemic stopping conditions S1-S6 and an epistemic budget B_epi; discovers two distinct Epistemic/Operational loops; delivers a 24-row computability table (all Yes) and a narrowed U1-U6 open-mathematics list; revises the KnowledgeOS definition; verdicts CONDITIONAL PASS; hands off to Step 25C (Evidence Aggregation Algebra).

rows.anchor: We now move from the kernel to the whole KnowledgeOS loop. Can the model take heterogeneous information, construct a governed knowledge state, identify what is missing, decide what should be investigated, evaluate whether a decision is possible, and safely reach an action?
rows.statement: Frames Step 25B's ambition: testing the whole KnowledgeOS loop (not just the knowledge-state kernel) end to end via the Nexus migration scenario.

rows.anchor: 25B.1 — Define the problem ... G = "Migrate Nexus OSS to the target Nexus Pro/container architecture safely." But this sentence is not yet executable. We need an epistemic contract EC_G = {ArchitectureKnown,TargetKnown,DependenciesKnown,NetworkKnown,BackupVerified,RollbackVerified,SecurityRequiremen
rows.statement: Defines the Nexus migration goal and a nine-requirement EpistemicContract EC_G, reaffirming Goal ≠ EpistemicContract.

rows.anchor: 25B.2 — Heterogeneous inputs ... I=\{Documents,Database,Internet,Rules,Manifesto,HumanInstructions,Scope,Constitution,Settings,ADR,Textbooks,AIOutput\}. All of these are inputs. But Input\neq Evidence.
rows.statement: Instantiates the twelve-kind heterogeneous input set with concrete Nexus examples, reaffirming Input ≠ Evidence.

rows.anchor: 25B.3 — Source classification ... Nexus inventory Infrastructure Unassessed ... Architecture Constitution Governance Authoritative normative source ... LLM output AI-generated Candidate information ... Notice what we do not do: We do not assign Truth=True to any of them.
rows.statement: Classifies eight concrete Nexus sources by type and initial epistemic status, none assigned Truth=True.

rows.anchor: 25B.4 — Observation extraction ... O_1: NexusVersion=3.69.0 ... O_8: Podman=rootless. These are observations. They are not yet business conclusions. ... 25B.5 — Evidence construction ... E_1: NexusVersion=3.69.0 with provenance E_1 \rightarrow InfrastructureInventory \rightarrow SystemInspection. ..
rows.statement: Works through the full concrete Observation→Evidence→Assertion chain for eight Nexus facts, reaffirming that evidence linkage does not automatically commit an assertion — assessment must come first.

rows.anchor: 25B.7 — Add governance knowledge ... A production architecture change requires architecture assessment and the appropriate governance approval. A_G: ArchitectureApprovalRequired=True. Its source is not an infrastructure observation. It comes from Constitution. DescriptiveKnowledge\neq NormativeKnowl
rows.statement: Adds a concrete normative constitutional assertion and an ADR-derived target-architecture assertion, reaffirming DescriptiveKnowledge ≠ NormativeKnowledge, both needed together for reasoning to begin.

rows.anchor: 25B.9 — Zero becomes computable ... \Delta=Zero(K_t,I,EC_G). The output is not merely "There is a difference." It should identify epistemic and operational gaps. \Delta_1: Rollback=Unknown ... \Delta_5: GovernanceApproval=Missing. This is our first genuinely useful Zero result.
rows.statement: Runs the first genuinely useful concrete Zero(K_t,I,EC_G) computation, producing five specific typed gaps (Rollback, BackupRestoreTest, FirewallRequirements, TargetCapacity all Unknown; GovernanceApproval Missing).

rows.anchor: 25B.10 — Important distinction ... Zero should not simply calculate TargetState-CurrentState. That is ordinary state comparison. KnowledgeOS requires EpistemicGap + OperationalGap + GovernanceGap. There may be no obvious infrastructure-state difference for rollback. But epistemically \Delta_{rollbac
rows.statement: Argues Zero must compute EpistemicGap+OperationalGap+GovernanceGap, not merely TargetState-CurrentState — a rollback-capability gap can be epistemically nonzero with no obvious infrastructure difference, making Zero fundamentally different from a configuration-diff tool.

rows.anchor: 25B.11 — Lord receives the discrepancy ... Lord(K_t,\Delta,G,C) \rightarrow Actions. For \Delta_{rollback} candidate actions might be L_1=SearchDocumentation, L_2=InspectBackupConfiguration, L_3=PerformRestoreTest, L_4=AskInfrastructureOwner. Lord does not necessarily change the world. It can first
rows.statement: Works Lord generating four concrete candidate epistemic actions for the rollback gap, confirming Lord does not necessarily change the world.

rows.anchor: 25B.12 — Epistemic action ... L_3=PerformRestoreTest. The test produces O_9: RestoreFailed. Now O_9\rightarrow E_9. Then E_9\rightarrow A_9 where A_9: RollbackRestoreCapability=False. Now KnowledgeOS knows something it previously did not know. ... 25B.13 — The famous KnowledgeOS result ... Before th
rows.statement: Executes the concrete rollback-test action producing RollbackRestoreCapability=False, demonstrating KnowledgeGain≠ProgressTowardGoal inside a live end-to-end loop rather than merely as prior theoretical discussion.

rows.anchor: 25B.14 — Zero runs again ... K_{t+1}\neq K_t, Zero is recalculated: \Delta_{t+1}=Zero(K_{t+1},I,EC_G). Previously Rollback = Unknown. Now Rollback = Failed. The gap becomes more precise. Zero becomes more informative as knowledge improves.
rows.statement: Shows recalculating Zero after new evidence produces a more precise gap (Unknown→Failed), confirming Zero becomes more informative as knowledge improves.

rows.anchor: 25B.15 — Lord now chooses another action ... L_5=DesignRollbackAlternative. Or L_6=RepairBackup. Or L_7=DoNotMigrate. Lord generates possibilities. It does not decide which business alternative should be accepted. That belongs to Sārathi/governance.
rows.statement: Shows Lord generating three new remediation candidates after the failed rollback test, reaffirming Lord does not decide the business alternative.

rows.anchor: 25B.16 — Sārathi ... Sārathi(K,\Delta,A,C) \rightarrow Recommendation. Migrate now Fast High. Repair backup first Medium Lower. Delay migration Low Lowest. Build alternative rollback Medium Medium. Sārathi evaluates these according to the applicable decision criteria. The result might be Recommendat
rows.statement: Works Sārathi evaluating four concrete benefit/risk-profiled options, producing a Recommendation while reaffirming Recommendation ≠ Decision.

rows.anchor: 25B.17 — Human governance ... The Architecture Board reviews the recommendation. It may decide: Decision: RepairBackupFirst. Then the authorized body grants Authorization=True. Only now can the governed execution path proceed. Recommendation \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Authorization \rightarrow
rows.statement: Works the human governance stage (Architecture Board decision and authorization), confirming the full Recommendation→Decision→Authorization→Execution chain remains intact.

rows.anchor: 25B.18 — Inject an LLM hallucination ... The firewall already permits the target migration. No evidence. Support(A_{LLM})=\varnothing. Status=Unsupported. Zero continues to report Firewall=Unknown. The hallucination cannot close the gap. This is a very important end-to-end safety property.
rows.statement: Injects an LLM hallucination (unsupported firewall claim) and confirms it fails to close the Zero-reported gap — a very important end-to-end safety property.

rows.anchor: 25B.19 — Inject conflicting Internet evidence ... vendor documentation says Port8081Required. An internal document says Port8081NotRequired. KnowledgeOS does not choose arbitrarily. It creates Conflict(E_{10},E_{11}). Now Zero reports FirewallRequirement=Conflicted. That is more informative than Fir
rows.statement: Injects two directly conflicting evidence items, confirming the system produces an explicit Conflicted status rather than arbitrary choice — more informative than Unknown, giving Unknown ≠ Conflicted.

rows.anchor: 25B.20 — Inject a stale source ... internal firewall document is from 2023. Vendor documentation is 2026. Temporal assessment may resolve the apparent conflict for the current migration. But the old document remains valid historical evidence. A_{old} becomes Superseded rather than Deleted. History s
rows.statement: Injects a temporally-stale conflicting source, confirming resolution via Superseded status rather than deletion — history survives.

rows.anchor: 25B.21 — Inject a changed requirement ... Originally R_1: ZeroDowntime=True. Later R_1': MaintenanceWindowAllowed=True. The KnowledgeOS state must not pretend the old requirement never existed. We now have RequirementVersion_1 and RequirementVersion_2. This means requirements themselves are temporal
rows.statement: Injects a changed business requirement, discovering requirements themselves are temporal knowledge requiring their own versioning (RequirementVersion_1/2), never silently overwritten.

rows.anchor: 25B.22 — What happens to the recommendation? ... Sārathi previously recommended RepairBackupFirst under EC_1. Now the contract becomes EC_2. The old recommendation remains historically valid under EC_1. But the current recommendation must be reevaluated: Recommendation_{new} = Sārathi(K_{current},EC
rows.statement: Shows a changed epistemic contract requires reevaluating (not overwriting) the prior recommendation, concluding DecisionContext is part of epistemic history.

rows.anchor: 25B.23 — Inject execution failure ... O_{failure}: MigrationFailed. That outcome is not merely an operational log. It becomes Observation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Knowledge. KnowledgeOS learns MigrationProcedure_X has failed under Context_X. This is the beginning of organizational learning.
rows.statement: Injects an execution-failure outcome, confirming it flows through Observation→Evidence→Knowledge as the beginning of organizational learning, not merely an operational log.

rows.anchor: 25B.24 — The closed loop ... Reality → Observe → Evidence → Assess → Assertion → Commit → KnowledgeState → ZERO → Discrepancy → LORD → Candidate Actions → SĀRATHI → Recommendation → Governance → Decision/Authorization → Action → Outcome → Observe → KnowledgeState. That is the first time our complete
rows.statement: Diagrams the complete closed loop from Reality through Zero/Lord/Sārathi/Governance/Action/Outcome back to Observation, the first time the complete theory forms one coherent closed loop.

rows.anchor: 25B.25 — Now the serious attack ... Can this loop terminate? Unknown \rightarrow Investigate \rightarrow Unknown \rightarrow Investigate \rightarrow\cdots An AI system could investigate forever. Therefore we need a stopping rule. EpistemicStoppingCondition.
rows.statement: Attacks the loop with the possibility of infinite investigation, requiring an EpistemicStoppingCondition.

rows.anchor: 25B.26 — Stopping conditions ... S1 Sufficient Sufficient(K,P)=True. S2 Impossible The missing knowledge cannot reasonably be obtained. S3 Economically unjustified VOI(Action)<Cost(Action). S4 Governed rejection A human authority explicitly decides not to pursue the gap. S5 Time constraint The decis
rows.statement: Defines six stopping conditions S1-S6 (Sufficient, Impossible, Economically unjustified, Governed rejection, Time constraint, Safety boundary) for terminating investigation, extremely important for autonomous AI.

rows.anchor: 25B.27 — New mathematical concept: epistemic budget ... B_{epi} an epistemic investigation budget. It can include Time, Cost, Risk, HumanAttention, Compute. Then Lord does not ask "Can I learn more?" It asks "Is learning more worth the cost/risk under the current goal?" This gives us a bridge toward
rows.statement: Introduces an epistemic investigation budget B_epi (Time, Cost, Risk, HumanAttention, Compute), reframing Lord's question from 'can I learn more?' to 'is learning more worth it?'.

rows.anchor: 25B.28 — Another major discovery ... KnowledgeOS has two loops. Epistemic loop Question \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Uncertainty \rightarrow Question. Operational loop Knowledge \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Knowledge. They interact
rows.statement: Discovers KnowledgeOS has two distinct interacting loops — an Epistemic loop (question-driven evidence gathering) and an Operational loop (decision-driven action) — establishing EpistemicAction ≠ OperationalAction as an architectural principle.

rows.anchor: 25B.29 — Can the whole model compute? ... Source Yes ... Assessment Yes, with unfinished mathematics ... Discrepancy Yes, provisional ... Human input Yes. This is a significant milestone.
rows.statement: Delivers a 24-row 'is it computable?' table across every major concept in the theory, with all rows marked Yes (two flagged with caveats: Assessment 'unfinished mathematics', Discrepancy 'provisional') — a significant milestone.

rows.anchor: 25B.30 — What is still mathematically unresolved? U1 Evidence aggregation Given E_1,\ldots,E_n how exactly do we calculate combined support? U2 Statistical uncertainty How do we represent P(H|E) when evidence is dependent, missing, biased or heterogeneous? U3 Conflict resolution When A_1\perp A_2, u
rows.statement: Narrows the remaining unresolved mathematics to six localized research problems U1-U6 (evidence aggregation, statistical uncertainty representation, conflict resolution conditions, VOI computation, discrepancy algebra, decision mathematics under risk) — no longer an undefined theoretical universe.

rows.anchor: 25B.31 — This is a very strong result ... We don't need one magical definition of "knowledge." We can decompose the problem into computational transformations: Observe \rightarrow Represent \rightarrow Assess \rightarrow Commit \rightarrow Revise \rightarrow Compare \rightarrow Investigate \rightarr
rows.statement: States the strong result that KnowledgeOS needs no single magical 'knowledge' definition, only a ten-stage decomposition (Observe→Represent→Assess→Commit→Revise→Compare→Investigate→Decide→Act→Observe) with a domain contract at each boundary, making the architecture tractable.

rows.anchor: 25B.32 — But I would change one thing in the theory ... I would not define KnowledgeOS as a system that knows everything. I would define it as A governed computational system for constructing, evaluating, evolving and applying purpose-relative knowledge under uncertainty. That is mathematically much
rows.statement: Revises the definition of KnowledgeOS from 'a system that knows everything' to 'a governed computational system for constructing, evaluating, evolving and applying purpose-relative knowledge under uncertainty' — mathematically more defensible and DDD-aligned.

rows.anchor: 25B.33 — 25B preliminary verdict ... 25B — CONDITIONAL PASS. The end-to-end architecture is computationally representable. But we have not yet mathematically solved EvidenceAggregation, ConflictResolution, VOI, Zero, DecisionOptimization. Those are the next major research targets.
rows.statement: Verdicts Step 25B CONDITIONAL PASS: the end-to-end architecture is computationally representable, with five specific mathematical mechanisms (EvidenceAggregation, ConflictResolution, VOI, Zero, DecisionOptimization) still unsolved as next research targets.

rows.anchor: 25B.34 — The next logical step ... Step 25C — Evidence Aggregation Algebra. Given multiple heterogeneous, possibly dependent, contradictory and temporally different pieces of evidence, can KnowledgeOS calculate a defensible assessment without double-counting, losing uncertainty or inventing certaint
rows.statement: Proposes Step 25C (Evidence Aggregation Algebra): whether KnowledgeOS can calculate a defensible assessment across nine evidence types without double-counting/losing-uncertainty/inventing-certainty, explicitly refusing to pre-select Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/weighted-scoring/fuzzy-logic before deriving the required properties first.

sources.note: The 8-family organization of the Constitutional Invariant Map register (Identity, Evidence, Authority, Transformation, Temporal, Reasoning, Contradiction, Agent), each with its own governing question (e.g. Evidence: 'Why should we believe this?').

rows.anchor: the following research lenses have been analysed
rows.statement: Full enumerated list of research lenses consumed by the study, explicitly framed as 'research lenses only. They are not automatically kernel laws': EKS/PKS/AIP archaeological evidence; Epistemic Control Systems; Knowledge lifecycle and snapshot models; TMS/AGM belief revision; Logic and inference theory; Nyaya Tarka Shastra reasoning; Vedanta epistemology; Jnana/Jneya/Jnata distinction; Vani (expression and transmission); Zero as neutral-state metaphor; Topological invariants; Sheaf/context composition; and six Navya-Nyaya sub-lenses: Abhava (structured absence), Avacchedaka (semantic delimitation), Hetvabhasa (reasoning fallacies), Coextension without identity, Intensional identity preservation, Type-theoretic interpretation.

rows.anchor: Expected Registered Invariants ... Identity Family ... Evidence Family ... Authority Family ... Transformation Family ... Temporal Family ... Reasoning Family ... Contradiction Family ... Agent Family
rows.statement: Part 3 schema (ID|Invariant|Dimensions|Forbidden Collapse|Evidence|Strength|Validation Target|Notes/Boundary) plus the expected 8-family protect-statements: Identity (Representation != Identity: 'knowledge identity survives representation changes'; Expression != Meaning; Context Preservation: 'meaning requires semantic frame'); Evidence ('Observation != Interpretation', 'Evidence != Authority'); Authority ('Source authority is assigned, not intrinsic'); Transformation ('Knowledge evolution must preserve lineage'); Temporal ('Knowledge exists with temporal validity'); Reasoning ('Observation != Inference'; 'Inference requires preserved justification'); Contradiction ('Contradiction != Failure'; 'Conflicting knowledge may coexist'); Agent ('Knower identity is part of epistemic state').

rows.anchor: Family 1 -- IDENTITY (What is this knowledge? -- identity conditions of meaning)
rows.statement: Family 1 (IDENTITY) table: INV-KOS-002 Semantic Continuity (forbids Representation->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-001 Semantic Frame Preservation (forbids Context Removal->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-002 Avacchedaka (forbids Unbounded Claim->Over-extended Knowledge; compression ruling SUBSUMES SemanticBoundary-001, Ontology-001, Abhava Boundary-001 facet, and the type-model context-clause as facets of this one row); H-KOS-Relationship-001 Knowledge Relationship Integrity/Tripuji (forbids Known Object->Detached Autonomous Truth); H-KOS-Relation-001 Epistemic Relations as First-Class (forbids Relation->Attribute; compression ruling: the general principle UNDER the separation family, with INV-001..004 + Expression!=Meaning + Observation!=Inference as its instances).

rows.anchor: Family 2 -- EVIDENCE (Why should we believe this?)
rows.statement: Family 2 (EVIDENCE) table: INV-001 Evidence != Authority (ESTABLISHED); INV-KOS-Pramana-001 Means of Acquisition (forbids the 'Source-role collapse' -- flattening sensor=expert statement=AI inference=historical document; the designation ruling names the Pramana source-role separation AS this row's Forbidden-Collapse content, not a separate row); H-KOS-EvidenceAuthenticity-001 Evidence vs Pseudo-Evidence (forbids Pseudo-evidence->Evidence, anti-hallucination); H-ZERO-001 UNKNOWN is a Valid Epistemic State (forbids Unknown->False / Unknown->Missing, i.e. Unknown != Absent != False); H-KOS-Uncertainty-001 Structured Doubt/Samsaya (forbids Doubt->Missing data; compression ruling: a proposed H-KOS-Abhava-001 compresses INTO Uncertainty-001).

rows.anchor: 83.67 — New invariants: I_TemporalTruth, I_EventTime, I_HistoricalIntegrity, I_TemporalAuthority, I_TemporalUncertainty, I_TemporalSupersession
rows.statement: States six new named invariants: I_TemporalTruth (claims whose truth can change must have explicit temporal interpretation), I_EventTime (event/observation/processing times must remain distinguishable when materially relevant), I_HistoricalIntegrity (historical decisions must be interpreted using knowledge/models/policies/authorities valid at decision time), I_TemporalAuthority (authorization must be evaluated at time of action), I_TemporalUncertainty (unknown/interval timestamps must not be converted into false point precision), I_TemporalSupersession (superseded knowledge remains historically reconstructable).

rows.anchor: 82.72 — New invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation, I_Dependence, I_ModelUncertainty, I_Calibration, I_EpistemicPrecision, I_DecisionSensitivity, I_UncertaintyImpact
rows.statement: States seven new named invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation (transformations must not silently discard material uncertainty), I_Dependence (dependencies between uncertain variables must be represented when material), I_ModelUncertainty (model-structure uncertainty must be distinguished from parameter uncertainty), I_Calibration (probabilistic claims should have defined semantics and empirical calibration where applicable), I_EpistemicPrecision (output precision must not misrepresent evidence quality), I_DecisionSensitivity (when uncertainty can change the selected action, sensitivity must remain visible), I_UncertaintyImpact (material upstream evidence changes must permit identification of affected downstream knowledge/decisions).

rows.anchor: 84.63 — New invariants: I_Intervention, I_CounterfactualProvenance, I_CounterfactualUncertainty, I_TemporalCausalSeparation, I_CounterfactualGovernance, I_Interference
rows.statement: States six new named invariants: I_Intervention (observed association must not be represented as causal intervention without justification), I_CounterfactualProvenance (material counterfactual claims retain their model, evidence, and assumptions), I_CounterfactualUncertainty (counterfactual results preserve uncertainty and model sensitivity), I_TemporalCausalSeparation (observed historical outcomes must remain distinct from unobserved alternative outcomes), I_CounterfactualGovernance (causal feasibility of an intervention does not imply authorization to execute it), I_Interference (counterfactual analysis must account for material interactions between agents, components, or interventions).

rows.anchor: 85.77 — New strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment, I_MetricIntegrity, I_StrategicRobustness, I_AuthorizationUnknown, I_GovernanceBoundary, I_MetaGovernance, I_IncentiveObservability
rows.statement: States seven new strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment (material incentives must not systematically reward behavior violating higher-level objectives), I_MetricIntegrity (governance metrics must not be equated with the underlying objective without justified relationship), I_StrategicRobustness (governance evaluation should consider adaptive/optimizing-against-mechanism behavior), I_AuthorizationUnknown (unknown authorization must not be interpreted as permission), I_GovernanceBoundary (material governance constraints must account for alternative execution paths), I_MetaGovernance (changes to governance mechanisms are themselves governed changes), I_IncentiveObservability (where strategic behavior is material, the system should model incentives and information as part of the behavioral model).

rows.anchor: 87.75 — New invariants: I_Aggregation, I_AuthorityExpertise, I_CollectiveConstraint, I_Quorum, I_Delegation, I_HistoricalAggregation, I_RecommendationDecision, I_DecisionAuthorization
rows.statement: States eight new invariants: I_Aggregation (every collective decision must use an explicitly defined aggregation mechanism), I_AuthorityExpertise (expertise, evidence quality, preference, and decision authority must not be conflated), I_CollectiveConstraint (collective preference cannot override higher-order mandatory constraints), I_Quorum (a decision requiring quorum must not become valid without sufficient authorized participation), I_Delegation (delegated authority cannot exceed the authority validly delegated by the delegator), I_HistoricalAggregation (historical decisions must be interpreted using the aggregation rules valid at decision time), I_RecommendationDecision (recommendation must not automatically become decision without required authority), I_DecisionAuthorization (a decision does not automatically grant execution authority unless the governance model explicitly defines that transition).

rows.anchor: 86.83 — New invariants: I_Mechanism, I_IncentiveCompatibility, I_IndependentVerification, I_GovernanceSurface, I_StrategicRobustness2, I_MechanismVersioning, I_FeasibleActionSpace
rows.statement: States seven new invariants: I_Mechanism (governance mechanisms must be evaluated by resulting behavior, not only formal rules), I_IncentiveCompatibility (where truthful/desired behavior is required, the mechanism must not create a systematic incentive to deviate), I_IndependentVerification (material claims should not depend exclusively on self-reported evidence when independent verification is feasible and material), I_GovernanceSurface (material alternative execution paths must be governed, restricted, or recognized as exception paths), I_StrategicRobustness2 (governance must be evaluated under plausible strategic responses, not only cooperative behavior), I_MechanismVersioning (changes to governance mechanisms must be versioned, authorized, and historically reconstructable), I_FeasibleActionSpace (optimization must occur within the set of constitutionally, governance, and authority-valid actions).

rows.anchor: 88.80 — New mathematical invariants: I_InformationPreservation, I_Sufficiency, I_CompressionProvenance, I_CompressionTime, I_CompressionUncertainty, I_NegativeKnowledge, I_RetrievalAssurance, I_DerivedReproducibility, I_RepresentationSeparation
rows.statement: States nine new invariants: I_InformationPreservation (a transformation must preserve all information required for its declared assurance purpose), I_Sufficiency (a representation declared sufficient must specify the question, model, and assurance context), I_CompressionProvenance (compression must not destroy required provenance relationships), I_CompressionTime (material temporal semantics must survive representation changes), I_CompressionUncertainty (compression must not convert uncertainty into unjustified certainty), I_NegativeKnowledge (failure to retrieve evidence must not automatically imply falsity), I_RetrievalAssurance (evidence completeness requirements must be proportional to decision criticality), I_DerivedReproducibility (material derived knowledge should retain sufficient references to reproduce/audit its derivation), I_RepresentationSeparation (derived representations such as embeddings/summaries/indexes must remain distinguishable from authoritative evidence).

rows.anchor: 89.73 — New invariants: I_Decidability, I_ComputationalFeasibility, I_ProofScope, I_ModelReality, I_VerificationState, I_Approximation, I_ComputationProvenance, I_SafetyLiveness, I_GovernanceConsistency, I_ProofEstimation
rows.statement: States ten new invariants: I_Decidability (distinguish undecidable from merely unknown), I_ComputationalFeasibility (infeasibility must not be represented as logical impossibility), I_ProofScope (verification claims must identify model, assumptions, scope), I_ModelReality (proof of a model property must not automatically be proof of the real-world property), I_VerificationState (verification must support True/False/Unknown), I_Approximation (approximate computation must remain distinguishable from exact), I_ComputationProvenance (material derived results must retain sufficient computational-derivation information for their assurance level), I_SafetyLiveness (governance verification must distinguish safety from liveness properties), I_GovernanceConsistency (mandatory governance rules must not contain unresolved logical contradictions), I_ProofEstimation (statistical/probabilistic support must not be represented as formal proof without explicit justification).

rows.anchor: 90.73 — New invariants: I_Complexity, I_Incremental, I_CacheValidity, I_DecisionPrecision, I_GracefulDegradation, I_DistributedTime, I_Correlation, I_AssuranceOptimization, I_CriticalityBudget
rows.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Complexity (material computational limits must be distinguishable from logical impossibility), I_Incremental (incremental recomputation must be semantically equivalent to required full recomputation under the declared model), I_CacheValidity (cached knowledge must retain the versions/validity conditions it depends on), I_DecisionPrecision (computational precision must be sufficient relative to the decision boundary and required assurance), I_GracefulDegradation (resource exhaustion must not silently convert incomplete computation into a definitive result), I_DistributedTime (observations from distributed sources must preserve their temporal semantics), I_Correlation (multiple computational outputs must not be treated as independent evidence when they share material dependencies), I_AssuranceOptimization (performance optimization must not silently reduce declared assurance), I_CriticalityBudget (computational resources and verification depth should be proportional to decision criticality where governance permits optimization).

rows.anchor: 91.80 — New invariants: I_Refinement, I_Representation, I_Contract, I_Trace, I_MeaningTechnology, I_SpecSync, I_Composition, I_ExecutableInvariant, I_AssuranceProvenance
rows.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Refinement (every implementation behavior affecting governed semantics must correspond to a permitted formal-model behavior), I_Representation (every concrete state exposed as valid must map to a valid abstract state), I_Contract (component implementations must satisfy declared preconditions/postconditions/invariants), I_Trace (observable implementation traces must remain within the permitted specification trace space), I_MeaningTechnology (implementation technology must not silently redefine domain semantics), I_SpecSync (material specification changes must trigger assessment of affected implementations), I_Composition (component-level correctness must not be promoted to system-level correctness without validating interaction contracts), I_ExecutableInvariant (where feasible, critical invariants should be represented as executable contracts/tests/enforcement), I_AssuranceProvenance (implementation-correctness claims must retain evidence of how they were established).

rows.anchor: 92.79 — New invariants: I_AtomicInvariant, I_Concurrency, I_Conflict, I_Version, I_CausalOrder, I_Idempotency, I_AuthorizationFreshness, I_AuthorityUniqueness, I_DecisionSnapshot, I_GlobalInvariant, I_IrreversibleAction
rows.statement: States eleven new invariants: I_AtomicInvariant (every atomic transition must preserve declared transaction-scope invariants), I_Concurrency (concurrent executions must not produce a state forbidden by the sequential spec), I_Conflict (unmergeable concurrent modifications must become explicit conflicts, not silent overwrites), I_Version (material writes must identify the state version validated against), I_CausalOrder (causal relationships must not be inferred solely from arrival order), I_Idempotency (idempotent operations must preserve semantic result under duplicate execution), I_AuthorizationFreshness (authorization decisions must satisfy freshness requirements per criticality), I_AuthorityUniqueness (distributed systems must prevent simultaneous conflicting authoritative states where exclusive authority is defined), I_DecisionSnapshot (material decisions must identify the evidence/policy/model/authority state used), I_GlobalInvariant (a multi-component invariant must be enforced at a boundary observing the combined state), I_IrreversibleAction (irreversible actions require assurance proportional to impact and rollback inability).

rows.anchor: 93.75 — The strongest recovery invariant ... I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode F, recovery must either restore a valid state, or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state. The system must never silently fabricate validity.
rows.statement: States the strongest recovery invariant I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode, recovery must restore a valid state or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state — never silently fabricate validity.

rows.anchor: 93.78 — New invariants: I_AtomicRecovery, I_Durability, I_RecoveryValidity, I_FailureHistory, I_Reconciliation, I_RecoveryFreshness, I_RetrySafety, I_Compensation, I_FailureEpistemics, I_RecoveryAssurance
rows.statement: States nine further new invariants: I_AtomicRecovery (failed atomic transitions must not leave semantically invalid committed states), I_Durability (a committed authoritative state must remain recoverable per its durability contract), I_RecoveryValidity (recovery must produce a valid state or explicitly degraded/unknown state), I_FailureHistory (recovery must not silently erase evidence of failure/partial execution/compensation), I_Reconciliation (recovered state must be reconciled with surviving authoritative state where divergence is possible), I_RecoveryFreshness (a recovered state must not be represented as current unless freshness is established), I_RetrySafety (retryable operations must have explicit duplicate-execution semantics), I_Compensation (compensation must remain distinguishable from perfect rollback and preserve residual effects), I_FailureEpistemics (observed failure, inferred cause, and unresolved cause must remain distinct knowledge states), I_RecoveryAssurance (recovery assurance must include correctness, completeness, freshness, and provenance appropriate to criticality).

rows.anchor: 94.71 — New invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity, I_AINonAuthority, I_TrustBoundary, I_AuthSeparation, I_LeastPrivilege, I_ProvenanceSecurity, I_IntegrityTruth, I_TemporalTrust, I_AdversarialEvidence, I_SeparationOfDuties, I_MultiPartyAuthorization, I_SecurityEvidence
rows.statement: States twelve new security invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity (authority must originate from an authorized governance mechanism, not an untrusted claim), I_AINonAuthority (AI-generated statements must not acquire authoritative status solely through generation), I_TrustBoundary (crossing a trust boundary must not automatically increase authority/trust level), I_AuthSeparation (identity verification must remain distinct from permission verification), I_LeastPrivilege (actors must possess no more capability than required), I_ProvenanceSecurity (material claims must retain sufficient provenance to distinguish authoritative/verified/unverified/untrusted origins), I_IntegrityTruth (integrity verification must not be represented as proof of semantic truth), I_TemporalTrust (trust/identity/authority/credentials must be evaluated within their applicable time interval), I_AdversarialEvidence (evidence exposed to material adversarial manipulation must carry a trust/risk assessment), I_SeparationOfDuties (no single actor may perform mutually exclusive roles in the same decision process where required), I_MultiPartyAuthorization (actions requiring multiple authorities must not execute until all required independent authorizations are established), I_SecurityEvidence (material security events must remain observable and attributable so they can become auditable evidence).

rows.anchor: 95.69 — Privacy as a mathematical invariant ... I_Privacy: for every actor, purpose, time, and context, the information accessible through the system must remain within the authorized information boundary.
rows.statement: States the core privacy invariant I_Privacy: accessible information must remain within the authorized information boundary for every actor/purpose/time/context.

rows.anchor: 95.75 — New invariants: I_InformationAuthorization, I_PurposeLimitation, I_DataMinimization, I_InformationFlow, I_DerivedProtection, I_AuthorizedRetrieval, I_PrivacyComposition, I_TemporalPrivacy, I_DeletionPropagation, I_AuditPrivacy, I_AIContextBoundary
rows.statement: States eleven further new invariants: I_InformationAuthorization (permission to act must not automatically imply permission to access all relevant information), I_PurposeLimitation (knowledge access must respect the declared/authorized purpose), I_DataMinimization (only information necessary for the purpose should be exposed where practicable), I_InformationFlow (restricted information must not flow into less-protected representations without authorized transformation), I_DerivedProtection (derived knowledge/summaries/embeddings/predictions/AI outputs remain subject to applicable information controls), I_AuthorizedRetrieval (access policy should constrain retrieval, not merely final presentation, wherever feasible), I_PrivacyComposition (repeated disclosures must be evaluated collectively), I_TemporalPrivacy (information authorization/classification must remain valid for the applicable time interval), I_DeletionPropagation (material deletion requirements must evaluate derived representations/downstream artifacts), I_AuditPrivacy (conflicts between audit retention and privacy requirements must be explicitly governed, not silently resolved), I_AIContextBoundary (an AI agent must receive only knowledge within its authorized epistemic boundary).

rows.anchor: 96.75 — New invariants: I_HistoricalSemantics, I_ModelProvenance, I_ModelApplicability, I_LearningProvenance, I_MigrationIntegrity, I_SemanticVersion, I_EvolutionImpact, I_EvolutionRegression, I_LearningAuthority, I_AdaptationBoundary, I_FeedbackIntegrity, I_ContinuousAssurance
rows.statement: States twelve new invariants: I_HistoricalSemantics (evolution must not silently change the meaning of historical knowledge/decisions/evidence), I_ModelProvenance (every material model-derived result must retain model version and configuration), I_ModelApplicability (a model must not be treated as valid outside its declared domain/context/validity interval without explicit assessment), I_LearningProvenance (learning updates must identify the evidence/observations/process that caused them), I_MigrationIntegrity (schema/ontology migration must not convert unknown/uncertain information into stronger knowledge without evidence), I_SemanticVersion (material decisions must retain relevant versions of software/schema/model/policy/ontology/workflow), I_EvolutionImpact (material changes must identify potentially affected invariants/contracts/artifacts/decisions), I_EvolutionRegression (material evolution must re-establish affected assurance properties before being treated as equivalent), I_LearningAuthority (learned patterns/predictions/AI proposals must not become authoritative without the applicable authorization process), I_AdaptationBoundary (autonomous adaptation must remain within an explicitly authorized boundary), I_FeedbackIntegrity (observed outcomes, causal interpretations, and counterfactual inferences must remain distinct knowledge objects), I_ContinuousAssurance (material system evolution must trigger appropriate revalidation of affected invariants).

rows.anchor: 97.80 — New invariants: I_AuthorityProvenance, I_Responsibility, I_Accountability, I_Delegation, I_Dissent, I_ProceduralValidity, I_EpistemicHumility, I_Override, I_DecisionScope, I_ExceptionAuthority, I_AgentAttribution, I_KnowledgeContinuity, I_GovernanceCompleteness
rows.statement: States thirteen new invariants: I_AuthorityProvenance (every material authority must have a traceable source/assignment/delegation), I_Responsibility (every material governed domain/critical action must have an explicitly defined responsible role), I_Accountability (material decisions/actions must be attributable to responsible actor and authority), I_Delegation (delegated authority cannot exceed the delegator's and must respect scope/time), I_Dissent (legitimate dissent must remain distinguishable from the final collective decision), I_ProceduralValidity (collective decisions must satisfy applicable quorum/authority/voting/process rules), I_EpistemicHumility (insufficient evidence/confidence must be representable as Unknown/Uncertain/EscalationRequired rather than fabricated certainty), I_Override (material human overrides of AI must preserve recommendation, override, actor, rationale), I_DecisionScope (a decision must not be applied beyond its declared scope), I_ExceptionAuthority (exceptions require explicitly authorized exception records), I_AgentAttribution (material AI actions must be attributable to a distinct agent identity/capability/authorization context), I_KnowledgeContinuity (critical organizational knowledge must not depend unknowingly on a single unreplaceable source), I_GovernanceCompleteness (critical domains/actions/decisions must have identifiable responsibility/authority/escalation paths).

rows.anchor: 99.80 — New invariants: I_RuntimeConformance, I_ObservabilityIntegrity, I_MeasurementHonesty, I_SilenceSemantics, I_AssuranceProvenance, I_MonitoringAssurance, I_DriftDetection, I_AssuranceFreshness, I_InvariantMonitoring, I_EvidenceSeparation
rows.statement: States ten new invariants: I_RuntimeConformance (observed system behavior must remain consistent with the approved architecture spec where runtime conformance is required), I_ObservabilityIntegrity (assurance claims must account for telemetry integrity/completeness/availability), I_MeasurementHonesty (measurements must retain sampling/uncertainty/coverage/freshness characteristics), I_SilenceSemantics (absence of telemetry must not be interpreted as evidence the event didn't occur), I_AssuranceProvenance (every assurance claim must be traceable to supporting evidence/verification/version/conditions), I_MonitoringAssurance (the system must detect/expose material failures in its own observability mechanisms), I_DriftDetection (material divergence between approved architecture/configuration and observed runtime must become detectable knowledge), I_AssuranceFreshness (an assurance claim must have a validity interval appropriate to the rate of system change), I_InvariantMonitoring (material runtime invariants must have an appropriate observation/verification mechanism where required), I_EvidenceSeparation (runtime observations, interpretations, and assurance claims must remain distinguishable).

rows.anchor: 98.81 — New invariants: I_ResourceHonesty, I_RiskProportionalAssurance, I_HardConstraints, I_AttentionAllocation, I_VerificationProvenance, I_FreshnessPolicy, I_ResourceIsolation, I_RetentionGovernance, I_ModelSelection, I_DegradationHonesty, I_InformationValue
rows.statement: States eleven new invariants: I_ResourceHonesty (resource limitation must not cause incomplete verification to be represented as complete), I_RiskProportionalAssurance (verification effort must be proportionate to risk/impact/uncertainty, subject to mandatory governance requirements), I_HardConstraints (optimization must never trade mandatory security/privacy/authority/semantic invariants for cost/latency/convenience), I_AttentionAllocation (human review capacity must be allocated by material risk/uncertainty, not merely volume), I_VerificationProvenance (the system must retain what verification was performed, at what version, under what conditions, with what result), I_FreshnessPolicy (cached knowledge must respect freshness requirements appropriate to its criticality), I_ResourceIsolation (noncritical workloads must not consume resources required for critical assurance/governance functions), I_RetentionGovernance (knowledge retention must follow explicit value/audit/privacy/lifecycle requirements), I_ModelSelection (AI model selection must satisfy the required assurance level while considering cost/latency/privacy/capability), I_DegradationHonesty (when resources are insufficient, the system must expose degraded/partial/unavailable status rather than fabricating full assurance), I_InformationValue (additional information should be acquired when its expected decision value justifies the cost, subject to mandatory assurance requirements).

rows.anchor: 103.81 — New semantic invariants: I_EvidenceDistinction, I_InferenceDistinction, I_DecisionDistinction, I_AuthorityBinding, I_ActionTraceability, I_OutcomeDistinction, I_TemporalKnowledge, I_ConflictPreservation, I_ScopeBinding, I_SemanticProvenance
rows.statement: States ten new semantic invariants: I_EvidenceDistinction (evidence must remain distinguishable from claims/interpretations/decisions), I_InferenceDistinction (an inferred proposition must not automatically become authoritative fact), I_DecisionDistinction (a recommendation must not automatically become an organizational decision), I_AuthorityBinding (material decisions/actions must be associated with the authority under which they are valid), I_ActionTraceability (material actions must be traceable to their authorization or pre-authorized policy), I_OutcomeDistinction (successful execution must not automatically be interpreted as successful outcome), I_TemporalKnowledge (knowledge claims must be interpretable relative to their validity period), I_ConflictPreservation (material contradictory evidence must remain detectable until explicitly resolved), I_ScopeBinding (claims/decisions/policies/evidence must not be applied outside their declared scope without justification), I_SemanticProvenance (the system must preserve whether a proposition was observed/sourced/inferred/assumed/decided/executed).

rows.anchor: 104.87 — New governance invariants: I_GovernanceAuthority, I_RuleLifecycle, I_GovernanceTraceability, I_ExceptionGovernance, I_GovernanceConflict, I_GovernanceFreshness, I_GovernanceEnforcement, I_AIGovernanceBoundary, I_GovernanceMemory
rows.statement: States nine new governance invariants: I_GovernanceAuthority (a governance decision must originate from an authority valid for its scope/time), I_RuleLifecycle (only rules in an authorized active state may govern current actions), I_GovernanceTraceability (material actions must be traceable to the governing rule/decision/pre-authorized policy), I_ExceptionGovernance (a deviation from a mandatory rule requires an explicitly authorized exception), I_GovernanceConflict (conflicting applicable governance rules must be surfaced, not silently resolved), I_GovernanceFreshness (superseded/expired rules must not silently govern current actions), I_GovernanceEnforcement (mandatory rules must have appropriate enforcement or explicit human control), I_AIGovernanceBoundary (AI recommendations/inferences must not silently become organizational authority), I_GovernanceMemory (material governance decisions must remain recoverable with authority/scope/rationale/validity).

rows.anchor: 105.65 — Agent invariants: I_SharedKnowledge, I_AgentBoundary, I_AgentAuthority, I_Recommendation, I_AgentAttribution, I_AgentAutonomy, I_KnowledgePromotion, I_AgentKnowledgeVersion
rows.statement: States eight new agent invariants: I_SharedKnowledge (agents must use designated authoritative KnowledgeOS knowledge sources), I_AgentBoundary (agent configuration must define behavior, not become a competing knowledge store), I_AgentAuthority (agent capability does not imply organizational authority), I_Recommendation (agent recommendation must remain distinguishable from authorized decision), I_AgentAttribution (material agent actions must be attributable to agent/session/scope/authorization), I_AgentAutonomy (autonomous agent actions must be bounded by pre-authorized policy), I_KnowledgePromotion (agent-generated knowledge must not become authoritative solely because an agent generated it), I_AgentKnowledgeVersion (agents must be able to distinguish current from superseded knowledge).

rows.anchor: 106.76 — Runtime invariants: I_RuntimeIdentity, I_RuntimeProvenance, I_DesiredActual, I_Drift, I_DriftGovernance, I_RuntimeEvidence, I_HistoricalRuntime
rows.statement: States seven new runtime invariants: I_RuntimeIdentity (every material runtime component must be identifiable against its logical component and deployed version), I_RuntimeProvenance (material runtime observations must retain sufficient provenance for when/where/how they were observed), I_DesiredActual (desired architecture and observed runtime state must remain distinguishable), I_Drift (material deviations between expected and observed architecture must be detectable), I_DriftGovernance (intentional deviations must have explicit authority/scope/validity), I_RuntimeEvidence (material runtime observations must be capable of becoming provenance-bearing evidence), I_HistoricalRuntime (material historical runtime states required for assurance/incident analysis must remain reconstructable).
